24	//!
25	//! These types form the contract between pipeline stages.
26	//! Rules:
27	//! - `CompactString` for names/type strings (avoids heap alloc for short strings)

33	use compact_str::CompactString;

132	#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "camelCase")]
133	pub enum PropType {
134	    // ── Primitives
135	    String,
136	    Number,
137	    Boolean,
138	    Null,
139	    Undefined,
140	    Any,
141	    Never,
142	    Unknown,
143	    Void,
144	
145	    // ── Literals
146	    StringLiteral(String),
147	    NumberLiteral(f64),
148	    BoolLiteral(bool),
149	
150	    // ── Composites
151	    Union(Vec<PropType>),
152	    Intersection(Vec<PropType>),
153	    Array(Box<PropType>),
154	    Tuple(Vec<PropType>),
155	    Object(Vec<ObjectField>),
156	
157	    // ── Named reference (post-resolution)
158	    Named {
159	        name: TypeName,
160	        /// Generic args, already resolved to PropType
161	        args: Vec<PropType>,
162	    },

165	    /// ReactNode, ReactElement, JSX.Element — all treated the same for docgen
166	    ReactNode,
167	    /// React.CSSProperties
168	    CssProperties,
169	    /// Event handler: (e: MouseEvent) => void etc.
170	    EventHandler {
171	        /// "MouseEvent", "ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>", etc.

173	    },
174	    /// Ref<T> / RefObject<T> / ForwardedRef<T>
175	    Ref {

178	    },

182	
183	    // ── HTML attribute inheritance
184	    /// All attributes of an HTML element, minus omitted keys.

186	    HtmlAttributes {
187	        element: String,
188	        omitted: Vec<String>,
189	    },

192	    /// Result of CvaVariantPropsHandler — the wrapper is fully dissolved.
193	    /// Each member is a string literal value.

195	        members: Vec<String>,
196	        /// true if this prop has a defaultVariant

198	    },

202	    SxProps,

212	impl PropType {
213	    /// True if this type is a pure literal union (all members are literals).
214	    /// Used by serializers to choose between "enum" and "union" in RDT output.
215	    pub fn is_literal_union(&self) -> bool {
216	        match self {
217	            PropType::Union(members) => members.iter().all(|m| {
218	                matches!(
219	                    m,
220	                    PropType::StringLiteral(_)
221	                        | PropType::NumberLiteral(_)
222	                        | PropType::BoolLiteral(_)
223	                )
224	            }),
225	            PropType::LiteralUnion { .. } => true,
226	            _ => false,
227	        }
228	    }
229	
230	    /// Raw type string for display (e.g. in RDT PropItemType.raw)
231	    pub fn raw_string(&self) -> String {
232	        match self {
233	            PropType::String => "string".into(),
234	            PropType::Number => "number".into(),
235	            PropType::Boolean => "boolean".into(),
236	            PropType::Null => "null".into(),
237	            PropType::Undefined => "undefined".into(),
238	            PropType::Any => "any".into(),
239	            PropType::Never => "never".into(),
240	            PropType::Unknown => "unknown".into(),
241	            PropType::Void => "void".into(),
242	            PropType::StringLiteral(s) => format!("\"{}\"", s),
243	            PropType::NumberLiteral(n) => n.to_string(),
244	            PropType::BoolLiteral(b) => b.to_string(),
245	            PropType::Union(members) => {
246	                members.iter().map(|m| m.raw_string()).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(" | ")
247	            }
248	            PropType::Intersection(members) => {
249	                members.iter().map(|m| m.raw_string()).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(" & ")
250	            }
251	            PropType::Array(inner) => format!("{}[]", inner.raw_string()),
252	            PropType::LiteralUnion { members, .. } => members.join(" | "),
253	            PropType::Named { name, args } if args.is_empty() => name.to_string(),
254	            PropType::Named { name, args } => {
255	                let args_str = args.iter().map(|a| a.raw_string()).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ");
256	                format!("{}<{}>", name, args_str)
257	            }
258	            PropType::ReactNode => "ReactNode".into(),
259	            PropType::CssProperties => "CSSProperties".into(),
260	            PropType::EventHandler { event_type } => format!("({}: {}) => void", "e", event_type),
261	            PropType::Ref { element: Some(e) } => format!("Ref<{}>", e),
262	            PropType::Ref { element: None } => "Ref<unknown>".into(),
263	            PropType::ElementType => "ElementType".into(),
264	            PropType::HtmlAttributes { element, .. } => {
265	                format!("{}HTMLAttributes", element_to_type_name(element))
266	            }
267	            PropType::SxProps => "SxProps".into(),
268	            PropType::Opaque { raw, .. } => raw.clone(),
269	            PropType::Object(_) => "object".into(),
270	            PropType::Tuple(_) => "tuple".into(),
271	            PropType::CssProperties => "CSSProperties".into(),
272	        }
273	    }
274	}

276	fn element_to_type_name(element: &str) -> &'static str {
277	    match element {
278	        "button" => "Button",
279	        "input" => "Input",
280	        "textarea" => "Textarea",
281	        "select" => "Select",
282	        "a" => "Anchor",
283	        "form" => "Form",
284	        "label" => "Label",
285	        "img" => "Img",
286	        "div" | "span" | "p" | "h1" | "h2" | "h3" | _ => "HTML",
287	    }

582	## CRITICAL: Use camino's Utf8Path
583	
584	All path operations use `camino::{Utf8Path, Utf8PathBuf}` — never `std::path::Path`.
585	This eliminates `.to_str().unwrap()` patterns throughout the codebase.
586	
587	## What NOT to Do
588	
589	- Do not use `std::collections::HashMap` — always `FxHashMap`
590	- Do not use `String` for type/prop names in hot-path structs — use `CompactString`/`TypeName`
591	- Do not put logic in this file — only type definitions and simple inherent methods
592	- Do not add `Display` impls here — that belongs in the serializer or CLI
593	- Do not use `Box<dyn Error>` — use typed errors via `thiserror`
594	- Do not add `#[allow(dead_code)]` — if something is defined, it must be used

9	## The Three Output Formats
10	
11	All three formats are produced from the same `ExtractionOutput`.
12	No separate extraction — just different views.
13	
14	```rust
15	// crates/core/src/serializer.rs
16	
17	use serde_json::{json, Value};
18	use crate::types::*;
19	
20	// ── Canonical — the native rich format ──────────────────────────────────────
21	// Just serde_json::to_string(&output) — ExtractionOutput derives Serialize
22	
23	// ── RDT Compatible ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
24	
25	pub fn to_rdt(output: &ExtractionOutput) -> Value {
26	    let components: serde_json::Map<String, Value> = output.components.iter()
27	        .map(|(name, entry)| (name.clone(), component_to_rdt(entry, output)))
28	        .collect();
29	    Value::Object(components)
30	}
31	
32	fn component_to_rdt(entry: &ComponentEntry, output: &ExtractionOutput) -> Value {
33	    let props: serde_json::Map<String, Value> = entry.props.iter()
34	        .map(|(name, prop)| (name.clone(), prop_to_rdt(prop, output)))
35	        .collect();
36	    
37	    json!({
38	        "displayName": entry.display_name,
39	        "filePath": entry.file_path,
40	        "description": entry.description,
41	        "props": props,
42	        "methods": [],
43	        "tags": entry.tags,
44	    })
45	}
46	
47	fn prop_to_rdt(prop: &ParsedProp, output: &ExtractionOutput) -> Value {
48	    json!({
49	        "name": prop.name,
50	        "required": prop.required,
51	        "description": prop.description,
52	        "defaultValue": prop.default_value.as_ref().map(|d| json!({ "value": d.value })),
53	        "type": prop_type_to_rdt(&prop.prop_type, output),
54	        "parent": prop.parent.as_ref().map(|p| json!({
55	            "name": p.name,
56	            "fileName": p.file_name,
57	        })),
58	        "declarations": prop.declarations.iter().map(|d| json!({
59	            "name": d.name,
60	            "fileName": d.file_name,
61	        })).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
62	        "tags": prop.tags,
63	    })
64	}
65	
66	fn prop_type_to_rdt(pt: &PropType, output: &ExtractionOutput) -> Value {
67	    match pt {
68	        PropType::String => json!({ "name": "string" }),
69	        PropType::Number => json!({ "name": "number" }),
70	        PropType::Boolean => json!({ "name": "boolean" }),
71	        PropType::Null => json!({ "name": "null" }),
72	        PropType::Undefined => json!({ "name": "undefined" }),
73	        PropType::Any => json!({ "name": "any" }),
74	        PropType::Never => json!({ "name": "never" }),
75	        PropType::Unknown => json!({ "name": "unknown" }),
76	        PropType::Void => json!({ "name": "void" }),
77	        PropType::ReactNode => json!({ "name": "ReactNode" }),
78	        PropType::CssProperties => json!({ "name": "CSSProperties" }),
79	        PropType::ElementType => json!({ "name": "elementType" }),
80	        PropType::SxProps => json!({ "name": "SxProps", "raw": "SxProps<Theme>" }),
81	        PropType::Ref { element } => json!({
82	            "name": "other",
83	            "raw": element.as_deref().map(|e| format!("Ref<{}>", e)).unwrap_or_else(|| "Ref<unknown>".into()),
84	        }),
85	        PropType::EventHandler { event_type } => json!({
86	            "name": "func",
87	            "raw": format!("(e: {}) => void", event_type),
88	        }),
89	        PropType::StringLiteral(s) => json!({ "name": "enum", "value": [{"value": s, "description": ""}] }),
90	        PropType::NumberLiteral(n) => json!({ "name": "number", "raw": n.to_string() }),
91	        PropType::BoolLiteral(b) => json!({ "name": "boolean", "raw": b.to_string() }),
92	        
93	        // Pure literal unions → RDT "enum"
94	        PropType::LiteralUnion { members, .. } => json!({
95	            "name": "enum",
96	            "raw": members.join(" | "),
97	            "value": members.iter().map(|m| json!({"value": m, "description": ""})).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
98	        }),
99	        
100	        PropType::Union(members) if pt.is_literal_union() => {
101	            let values: Vec<_> = members.iter()
102	                .map(|m| json!({"value": m.raw_string(), "description": ""}))
103	                .collect();
104	            json!({
105	                "name": "enum",
106	                "raw": members.iter().map(|m| m.raw_string()).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(" | "),
107	                "value": values,
108	            })
109	        }
110	        
111	        PropType::Union(members) => json!({
112	            "name": "union",
113	            "raw": members.iter().map(|m| m.raw_string()).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(" | "),
114	            "value": members.iter().map(|m| prop_type_to_rdt(m, output)).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
115	        }),
116	        
117	        PropType::Array(inner) => json!({
118	            "name": "Array",
119	            "raw": format!("{}[]", inner.raw_string()),
120	        }),
121	        
122	        PropType::HtmlAttributes { element, .. } => json!({
123	            "name": "HTMLAttributes",
124	            "raw": format!("{}HTMLAttributes<HTML{}Element>", capitalize(element), capitalize(element)),
125	        }),
126	        
127	        PropType::Named { name, args } => json!({
128	            "name": name.as_str(),
129	            "raw": pt.raw_string(),
130	        }),
131	        
132	        PropType::Opaque { raw, .. } => json!({ "name": raw.as_str() }),
133	        
134	        _ => json!({ "name": pt.raw_string() }),
135	    }
136	}
137	
138	fn capitalize(s: &str) -> String {
139	    let mut c = s.chars();
140	    match c.next() {
141	        None => String::new(),
142	        Some(f) => f.to_uppercase().collect::<String>() + c.as_str(),
143	    }
144	}

146	// ── Storybook __docgenInfo format ────────────────────────────────────────────
147	
148	pub fn to_storybook_block(entry: &ComponentEntry) -> String {
149	    let json = serde_json::to_string(entry)
150	        .unwrap_or_default()
151	        // HTML-safe escaping
152	        .replace('<', "\\u003c")
153	        .replace('>', "\\u003e")
154	        .replace('&', "\\u0026");
155	    
156	    format!(
157	        "if (typeof {} !== 'undefined') {{\n  {}.__docgenInfo = {}\n}}",
158	        entry.display_name, entry.display_name, json
159	    )
160	}

321	## NAPI Thread Safety
322	
323	```rust
324	// SESSIONS must be globally accessible across NAPI calls.
325	// Use LazyLock<DashMap<...>> — DashMap is Send + Sync.
326	// Never use std::sync::Mutex<HashMap<...>> — can deadlock under NAPI.
327	
328	static SESSIONS: LazyLock<DashMap<u32, Arc<WatchSession>>> = LazyLock::new(DashMap::new);
329	
330	// WatchSession fields must all be Send + Sync:
331	// ✓ DashMap (Send + Sync)
332	// ✓ ArcSwap (Send + Sync)
333	// ✓ Arc<GlobalSourceData> (Send + Sync if GlobalSourceData: Send + Sync)
334	// ✗ Rc, RefCell, raw pointers — never use in WatchSession
335	```
336	
337	## BTreeMap vs FxHashMap — The Rule
338	
339	```
340	FxHashMap: internal lookup, hot paths, GlobalSourceData.interfaces/type_aliases
341	BTreeMap:  any struct that becomes JSON output (deterministic key ordering!)
342	
343	Why: serde_json serializes maps with key ordering preserved.
344	     Different key orders = different JSON = flaky snapshot tests.
345	     BTreeMap in output structs = always alphabetical = stable.
346	```

349	
350	```rust
351	// CompactString stores strings ≤24 bytes inline (no heap alloc).
352	// Most type names ("ButtonProps", "FC", "string") are ≤24 bytes — free.
353	// Be careful with very long type names in HashMap keys:
354	// "packages/ui/src/Button.tsx:ButtonProps" is > 24 bytes — heap allocated.
355	// This is fine — CompactString still works, just with a heap alloc.

390	## RDT propFilter Compatibility
391	
392	```
393	The #1 RDT usage pattern is:
394	  propFilter: (prop) => !prop.parent?.fileName.includes('node_modules')
395	
396	For this to work, HTML/DOM props inherited from @types/react MUST have:
397	  parent.fileName containing "node_modules/@types/react/..."
398	
399	This means:
400	- When resolving ButtonHTMLAttributes, the PropParent must point to
401	  the actual @types/react .d.ts file path, not our baked-in table.
402	- Use oxc_resolver to find @types/react location, parse it on first use,
403	  cache the result. Don't hardcode paths.
404	- If @types/react is not installed, fall back to our baked-in table
405	  with a synthetic parent.fileName of "node_modules/@types/react/index.d.ts".
406	```

409	
410	```rust
411	// Always emit a Diagnostic for unresolvable types.
412	// The user should know what couldn't be resolved and why.
413	// PropType::Opaque always pairs with a Diagnostic in the output.
414	
415	// WRONG — silent failure
416	if ctx.global.interfaces.get(&key).is_none() {
417	    return ResolvedChain::default();  // silently empty
418	}
419	
420	// CORRECT — fail loudly but gracefully
421	if ctx.global.interfaces.get(&key).is_none() {
422	    diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
423	        severity: DiagnosticSeverity::Warning,
424	        message: format!("Cannot resolve type '{}' — it will appear as opaque", type_name),
425	        help: Some("Check that the package is installed and its types are resolvable".into()),
426	        code: DiagnosticCode::UnresolvableImport,
427	        ..
428	    });
429	    return ResolvedChain::empty_with_compose(type_name.to_owned());
430	}

#!/bin/bash
# Pull real .d.ts files from npm for fixture testing
# Run: bash fixtures/update-fixtures.sh

set -e
TMPDIR=$(mktemp -d)

pull_dts() {
  local pkg="$1"
  local file="$2"
  local dest="$3"
  npm pack "$pkg" --pack-destination="$TMPDIR" --silent
  TARBALL=$(ls "$TMPDIR"/*.tgz | head -1)
  tar -xzf "$TARBALL" -C "$TMPDIR" "package/$file" 2>/dev/null
  cp "$TMPDIR/package/$file" "$dest"
  rm -rf "$TMPDIR"/*.tgz "$TMPDIR"/package
}

[workspace]
members = [
    "crates/core",
    "crates/napi",
    "crates/cli",
    "packages/rolldown-plugin",
]
resolver = "2"

[workspace.package]
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
rust-version = "1.94"
authors = ["oxc-react-docgen contributors"]
license = "MIT"

[workspace.dependencies]
# OXC — all main crates move in lockstep; module_lexer and resolver have separate versioning
oxc_allocator     = "0.135"
oxc_parser        = "0.135"
oxc_ast           = "0.135"
oxc_span          = "0.135"
oxc_module_lexer  = "0.38"
oxc_resolver      = "11"

# Core data
compact_str       = { version = "0.9", features = ["serde"] }
rustc-hash        = "2.1"
dashmap           = "6.1"
arc-swap          = "1.9"
camino            = { version = "1.2", features = ["serde1"] }
indexmap          = { version = "2.14", features = ["serde"] }
dirs              = "6.0"

# Serde
serde             = { version = "1.0", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json        = "1.0"
rmp-serde         = "1.3"

# Error handling
thiserror         = "2.0"
miette            = "7.6"
anyhow            = "1.0"

# Parallelism
rayon             = "1.12"
tokio             = { version = "1.52", features = ["rt-multi-thread", "process", "io-util", "sync", "macros"] }

# File system
ignore            = "0.4"

# LSP (Tier 4 scaffold — not implemented)
lsp-types         = "0.97"

# CLI
clap              = { version = "4.6", features = ["derive", "env", "wrap_help"] }
clap_complete     = "4.6"
clap_mangen       = "0.3"
indicatif         = "0.18"
tracing-indicatif = "0.3"
tracing           = "0.1"
tracing-subscriber = { version = "0.3", features = ["env-filter", "fmt"] }
owo-colors        = "4.3"
watchexec         = "8.2"

# NAPI (3.x series)
napi              = { version = "3", features = ["napi4"] }
napi-derive       = "3"

# Dev
divan             = "0.1"
insta             = { version = "1.48", features = ["json", "redactions"] }
pretty_assertions = "1.4"

[profile.release]
opt-level = 3
lto = "thin"
codegen-units = 1

[profile.bench]
inherits = "release"
debug = true

You are implementing Phase 1a of oxc-react-docgen: the shared type definitions in `crates/core/src/types.rs`.

Both phases completed successfully:

**Phase 1a — types.rs ✅**
- All shared types implemented: `ExtractionOutput`, `ComponentEntry`, `ParsedProp`, `PropType` (25 variants), `SourceData`, `GlobalSourceData`, diagnostics, stats, import/export types
- `cargo build` and `cargo clippy -D warnings` both pass clean
- Two spec bugs fixed: duplicate `CssProperties` arm removed, `Utf8Path` added to imports

**Phase 1b — Fixtures ✅**
7 files created covering all the key extraction patterns:

| File | Key pattern tested |
|------|-------------------|
| `shadcn/button.tsx` | `cva` + `forwardRef` + `VariantProps` |
| `shadcn/input.tsx` | Simple `forwardRef` + `InputHTMLAttributes` |
| `shadcn/badge.tsx` | `cva` + function component (no ref) |
| `panda/button.tsx` | `defineRecipe` + `RecipeVariantProps` + `splitCssProps` |
| `radix/button.d.ts` | `ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'button'>` + `asChild` |
| `mui/Button.d.ts` | Multi-level extends + `SxProps` + string literal union variants |
| `react-aria/Button.d.ts` | ARIA-first API, render props, no HTML attribute inheritance |

**Up next:** Phase 2a (Extractor), 2b (ImportMap), 2c (KnownPatterns) — all three can run in parallel. Ready when you are.
What are some of the react component libraries and design systems that have react-docgen already that we can validate against? Radix might be a good choice, what else?

Good ones for validation — prioritized by how useful they are as test cases:

**Tier 1 — Most valuable (complex types, known RDT users)**
- **MUI** (`@mui/material`) — the hardest test: deeply nested inheritance, `SxProps`, `OverridableStringUnion`, `styled` HOC patterns, thousands of props. If we match RDT output here it proves correctness.
- **Chakra UI** — uses `HTMLChakraProps<'button'>` (a pattern we explicitly handle), `forwardRef` everywhere, `as` prop polymorphism.
- **Mantine** — huge component surface, TypeScript-first, actively uses Storybook autodocs with RDT.

**Tier 2 — Good coverage of specific patterns**
- **Radix Primitives** (already planned) — `ComponentPropsWithoutRef`, `asChild`, clean `.d.ts` files.
- **Ariakit** — similar to React Aria, ARIA-first, very well typed, tests our render-prop handling.
- **Headless UI** (Tailwind Labs) — simpler but representative of HOC-wrapped components.

**Tier 3 — Interesting edge cases**
- **Radix Themes** — higher-level Radix, adds their own prop systems on top of primitives, tests multi-layer resolution.
- **NextUI/HeroUI** — built on React Aria + Tailwind, tests composed prop systems.
- **Tremor** — data viz, lots of union types for chart config.

**My recommendation:** add **MUI**, **Chakra**, and **Mantine** to fixtures alongside Radix. That combination covers:
- Every HTML attribute inheritance pattern
- `SxProps` / `SystemStyleObject`
- `HTMLChakraProps` / `HTMLArkProps`
- `OverridableStringUnion`
- Multi-level extends chains
- HOC wrapping patterns

MUI is especially important because it's the hardest case and the most commonly reported source of RDT slowness (it's the main reason people want to replace RDT at all). If we're fast and correct on MUI, that's the headline benchmark.

Want me to add those to the fixtures now, or wait until Phase 2a/b/c are done so we can actually run extraction against them?
Let's also not lose track of what our architecture is, react best practices, performance considerations, the DX and the accuracy of the resulting docgen

Good flag. Let me map what's covered vs what needs explicit attention as we implement:

**Architecture — well-specified**
- Two-phase: parallel parse → parallel resolve, never the reverse
- `GlobalSourceData` as the single shared read-only context during resolution
- No AST refs escape `parse_file` — allocator is per-call
- `FxHashMap` internally, `BTreeMap` on output (determinism)
- NAPI boundary is a JSON string, not marshalled structs

**React best practices — gaps in the current spec**

# Open Questions & Architecture Decisions

Tracks gaps in the phase specs, decisions needed before implementation, and
accuracy/DX concerns to carry forward into each phase.

---

## Config File Name

**Decision:** `docgen.config.ts` (not `oxc-react-docgen.config.ts`)

Follows `vite.config.ts` / `eslint.config.js` convention. Short, obvious in
context, no collision risk. Config shape mirrors `PipelineOptions` + a
`propFilter` function.

TODO (Phase 4b): implement config file loading in the CLI.

---

## Validation Strategy

We compare output against two baselines on the same fixture files:

| Tool | Basis | What it proves |
|------|-------|----------------|
| `react-docgen` 7.x | babel, JS/TSX only | detection accuracy vs the original |
| `react-docgen-typescript` 2.x | tsc, full type resolution | the primary drop-in target |
| **ours** | OXC, no tsc | speed + correctness |

Infrastructure: `packages/validate/` — run `pnpm baseline` then `pnpm compare`.

### Validation fixture libraries (priority order)

1. **shadcn/ui** — cva + forwardRef + VariantProps ✅ in fixtures
2. **Radix UI** — ComponentPropsWithoutRef + asChild ✅ in fixtures
3. **MUI** — deepest type chains, SxProps, OverridableStringUnion ✅ in fixtures
4. **Chakra UI** — HTMLChakraProps, ThemingProps ✅ in fixtures
5. **Mantine** — StylesApiProps, polymorphic component ✅ in fixtures
6. **React Aria** — ARIA-first, render props, no HTML inheritance ✅ in fixtures

### Accuracy dimensions to validate

- Components detected (false positives, false negatives)
- Prop names (completeness)
- Type accuracy (`"string" | "number"` vs `"enum"`)
- Required/optional correctness
- Default values extracted
- JSDoc descriptions preserved
- `parent.fileName` pointing to correct file (critical for RDT propFilter compat)
- Speed: our tool vs rdt (target: 10-100x faster)

---

## React Best Practices — Implementation Gaps

### React 19 `ref` as plain prop
In React 19, `ref` is passed as a regular prop — `forwardRef` is no longer
needed and is deprecated. The extractor must detect:
```tsx
// React 19 — ref is just a prop
function Button({ ref, ...props }: ButtonProps & { ref?: Ref<HTMLButtonElement> }) {}
```
`ReactVersion.ref_as_prop` exists in `react_types.rs` — Phase 2a must wire it up.

### Compound components
`Dialog.Trigger`, `Select.Item` etc. are not addressed in Phase 2a spec.
Pattern: `const DialogTrigger = Dialog.Trigger` or `Dialog.Trigger = DialogTrigger`.
Decision needed: detect and emit as separate components, or skip?
**Recommendation:** emit as `Dialog.Trigger` display name, separate ComponentEntry.

### `displayName` fallback
Some HOC-wrapped components set `Comp.displayName = 'Button'` after definition.
Phase 2a extractor must scan for `MemberExpression.displayName = StringLiteral`
assignments to correct the component name.

### `defaultProps` (deprecated but present in .d.ts)
MUI ships `defaultProps` in its .d.ts declarations. We should read them as
default values rather than ignoring them. Phase 3a resolver decision.

### Generic components
`Table<TData extends object>`, `Select<T>` etc. — the extractor currently
only handles non-generic component patterns. Phase 2a: when a component's
props type has type params, emit `Named { name, args }` and let the resolver
degrade gracefully.

---

## Performance

### SLOs (non-negotiable)
- `parse_single_file`: < 10µs per file
- `full_pipeline` (50 components): < 10ms wall clock
- Watch mode incremental update: < 5ms per changed file

### DTS Cache (`cache.rs`) — UNDESIGNED
This is the main cross-run perf mechanism. Needs design before Phase 3a.
Required interface:
```rust
pub struct DtsCache { ... }
impl DtsCache {
    pub fn load_from_disk() -> Self;
    pub fn get(&self, path: &Utf8Path, mtime: SystemTime) -> Option<SourceData>;
    pub fn insert(&self, path: &Utf8Path, mtime: SystemTime, data: SourceData);
    pub fn save_to_disk(&self);
}
```
Storage: MessagePack (rmp-serde) keyed by `(path, mtime)`.
Location: `dirs::cache_dir() / "oxc-react-docgen" / "dts-cache.msgpack"`.

### Watch mode incremental — UNIMPLEMENTED
`WatchSession::update_file` is `todo!()`. Needs reverse-dep graph walk.
Phase 3b must implement before Phase 4a (NAPI depends on it).

---

## Accuracy — Edge Cases Not in Spec

### Unhandled TypeScript utility types
Currently specified: `Omit`, `Pick`, `Partial`, `Required`.
Also present in real libraries:
- `Exclude<T, U>` — often used in variant types
- `Extract<T, U>` — opposite of Exclude
- `ReturnType<typeof fn>` — Mantine uses this for recipe return types
- `Parameters<typeof fn>[0]` — uncommon but present
- `NonNullable<T>` — already in `known.rs` as passthrough

**Recommendation for Phase 3a:** degrade unknown utility types to
`Opaque { reason: OpaqueReason::ConditionalType }` with a diagnostic,
rather than silently emitting empty props.

### JSDoc `@param` → prop description
The spec maps JSDoc `@tags` as a flat `BTreeMap<String, String>`.
Real libraries use `@param propName description` to document props.
Phase 2a extractor should parse `@param {type} propName description`
and merge into the prop's `description` field.

### JSDoc `@default` tag
Some libraries document defaults via JSDoc rather than destructuring:
```ts
/** @default "md" */
size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'
```
Phase 2a: parse `@default <value>` and populate `RawProp`'s default.
Phase 3a: surface as `ParsedProp.default_value`.

### Event handler type inference
The spec detects `MouseEventHandler` etc. from baked-in names.
Real libraries use: `(event: React.MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>) => void`.
Phase 2a: parse inline function types and classify as `EventHandler`.

---

## DX Checklist

- [ ] `docgen.config.ts` config file (Phase 4b)
- [ ] `oxc-react-docgen inspect Button` shows props in a table (Phase 4b) ✅ specified
- [ ] Shell completions (Phase 4b) ✅ specified
- [ ] Vite plugin `propFilter` option (Phase 5a) ✅ specified
- [ ] Storybook autodocs drop-in (Phase 5a) ✅ via __docgenInfo
- [ ] Diagnostic messages point to exact source location via miette (Phase 3a+)
- [ ] `--react-version` auto-detection from `package.json` peerDependencies (Phase 4b)
- [ ] Watch mode `oxc-react-docgen watch` (Phase 4b) ✅ specified

content.text:
Yes and no — and the data makes it clear:

**Where RDT is genuinely more accurate:**
- `variant` → correctly resolved to `"default" | "destructive" | "outline" | "secondary" | "ghost" | "link" | null` — it followed `VariantProps<typeof buttonVariants>` all the way through the `cva()` call using the TypeScript compiler
- `onClick` → `MouseEventHandler<HTMLButtonElement>` with the correct element type
- `ref` → `Ref<HTMLButtonElement>` with the correct element type
- It correctly tracked that `asChild` defaults to `false`

**Where it's not more accurate, just more verbose:**
- 292 props, 285 of which are inherited HTML attributes (`form`, `formAction`, `formEncType`...) that are not the component's API — they're structural noise
- The `| null` on variant/size is a quirk of how cva types optional variants — technically correct but confusing in a controls table

**The real accuracy question for us** is whether we match RDT on the meaningful props after filtering. That's our target:

```
variant:  "default" | "destructive" | "outline" | "secondary" | "ghost" | "link"
size:     "default" | "sm" | "lg" | "icon"
asChild:  boolean (default: false)
```

react-docgen only found `asChild` (1 prop). We need to do what RDT did for those three, but without running the TypeScript compiler. The `| null` from RDT is actually a good signal — it comes from cva's type signature, and whether we include it is a design decision (RDT users often see it as noise and filter it).

One more thing worth noting: RDT took **99–232ms per file**. That's on toy fixtures with no cross-package resolution. On a real monorepo with 200 components across packages, that's 20-45 seconds of cold start. That's the performance gap we're closing.

Phase 2a (the extractor) also just wrote `react_types.rs` — the notification came in while we were running this. Should be completing its full build/test pass shortly.
Is there a meaninful way to record the HTML attributes and where they came from without being overwhelming?
Is there a meaninful way to record the HTML attributes and where they came from without being overwhelming? Is it possible in the react-docgen format?

Yes, and there are a few layers to this. Let me think through it carefully:

**What RDT's format already supports — but doesn't use well**

Every prop has a `parent` field:
```json
{
  "onClick": {
    "type": "MouseEventHandler<HTMLButtonElement>",
    "parent": { "name": "ButtonHTMLAttributes", "fileName": "node_modules/@types/react/index.d.ts" }
  }
}
```

The `parent.fileName` is exactly how the standard propFilter works. The information is there — RDT just dumps everything flat and trusts users to filter. We could emit the same structure (HTML props with the real `@types/react` path as parent) and be fully propFilter-compatible.

**The better approach in our canonical format**

We already have the right shape in `ComponentEntry`:
```rust
pub html_element: Option<String>,       // "button"
pub omitted_html_props: Vec<String>,    // ["ref", "color"] etc.
pub composes: Vec<String>,              // unresolvable types
```

We could extend this to be genuinely useful:

```json
{
  "displayName": "Button",
  "props": {
    "variant": { ... },
    "size": { ... },
    "asChild": { ... }
  },
  "htmlElement": "button",
  "htmlInheritance": {
    "element": "button",
    "source": "ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement>",
    "omitted": [],
    "notable": ["onClick", "disabled", "type", "form", "name", "value"]
  }
}
```

The `notable` list is the key idea — we bake in knowledge of which HTML attrs are commonly used intentionally (disabled, type, form) vs pure noise (formEncType, formNoValidate). Storybook could render this as a collapsed "HTML button attributes" row in the controls table rather than 285 expanded rows.

**Three output tiers we could support:**

| Mode | HTML attrs | Parent info | Use case |
|------|-----------|-------------|----------|
| `canonical` | Collapsed into `htmlInheritance` + `notable[]` | ✅ structured | Our native format, Storybook custom block |
| `rdt` | Expanded flat, `parent.fileName` → `node_modules/@types/react/...` | ✅ RDT-compat | Existing propFilter setups, drop-in replacement |
| `rdt-filtered` | Omitted entirely | ❌ | Zero-config mode for teams who never want them |

**The `notable` list approach is genuinely new**

react-docgen doesn't do this. RDT doesn't do this. It's the answer to "I want to know Button accepts `disabled` and `onClick` without drowning in `formEncType`." We could ship a baked-in table of ~15 commonly-used attributes per element type that we always surface, with the rest collapsed behind the `htmlElement` reference.

Worth adding to `docs/08-OPEN-QUESTIONS.md` as a decided design direction. Want me to spec it out and add `htmlInheritance` + `notable` to the types?

Here's the categorized view — sorted by whether they block Phase 3 or can wait:

---

**Block Phase 3 — must decide now**

**1. Inheritance + Notable design** *(blocks Phase 3a)*
The resolver is what *populates* inheritance data. If `types.rs` doesn't have `InheritedLayer` and `NotableInheritedProps` before Phase 3a starts, the resolver can't write to them and we'd have to break the types contract later. We just spec'd this — needs to go into `types.rs` before Phase 3 launches.

**2. DTS cache design** *(blocks Phase 3a + 3b)*
`cache.rs` is a complete stub. `pipeline.rs` calls `DtsCache::load_from_disk()` and `cache.save_to_disk()`, and Phase 3a's resolver uses it for cross-package .d.ts files. Nobody has designed the actual struct, key format, or invalidation strategy yet.

**3. Watch mode incremental** *(blocks Phase 3b)*
`WatchSession::update_file` is `todo!()`. Phase 3b owns `pipeline.rs` including the watch session. Without a design, the agent will either skip it or invent something inconsistent with Phase 4a (NAPI depends on it).

---

**Already resolved by Phase 2a (just need doc update)**

- ~~displayName fallback~~ ✅ implemented
- ~~JSDoc @param / @default~~ ✅ implemented
- ~~Event handler inline types~~ ✅ handled

---

**Deferred — don't block Phase 3**

- **Compound components** (`Dialog.Trigger`) — Phase 2a doesn't detect them yet; Phase 3a resolver doesn't need to handle what it never receives. Can add in a Phase 2a follow-up.
- **Generic components** (`Table<T>`) — extractor emits `Named { name, args }`, resolver degrades gracefully. No decision needed now.
- **`defaultProps` in .d.ts** — Phase 3a can stub it as a `TODO` and implement later.
- **`Exclude<T,U>`, `ReturnType<>` etc.** — already decided: degrade to `Opaque` with diagnostic.
- All DX checklist items — Phase 4+.

---

**Recommended order of attack before launching Phase 3:**

1. Decide inheritance + notable design → update `types.rs` (20 min)
2. Design DTS cache → spec `cache.rs` interface (10 min)
3. Design watch mode incremental → spec `WatchSession::update_file` (15 min)
4. Launch Phase 3a + 3b in parallel

Want to work through all three now? The inheritance design is the most interesting one — the other two are more mechanical.

Let's think deeply about this, considering rust best practices, useful crates, examples from notable codebases, examples relevant to oxc and RDT. Consider our architecture, performance and quality of the results
Do we need to use rayon and mielle for anything here? Anything else?

Good question — let me be precise about what's actually needed where.

---

## Rayon

**Needed for:**
- **Pipeline** — parallel parse of source files, parallel resolve of components. Essential, already planned.
- **Watch mode incremental** — re-resolving affected components after a change. The BFS to find affected files is tiny and sequential, but the actual re-resolution of those components runs in parallel via rayon. This is where the 5ms SLO comes from.

**Not needed for:**
- DTS cache — just concurrent hash map reads/writes from rayon threads, handled by DashMap.
- Inheritance data structure — pure data, built during resolution.
- Building the reverse dep graph — sequential BFS over a small graph.

---

## miette

**Not needed in core for any of these.** The hard rule holds: `crates/core` has zero terminal/display deps. Our own `Diagnostic` type in `types.rs` is the in-core representation — a plain serializable struct. miette with `fancy` feature stays in `crates/cli` only, where it renders those `Diagnostic` structs to humans.

One nuance: miette IS in `crates/core`'s deps (without `fancy`) for structured error types via `miette::Diagnostic` derive. But for the DTS cache, a simple `thiserror` error enum is sufficient — we don't need miette's diagnostic machinery there.

---

## Other crates worth considering

**`tempfile`** — we should use this for atomic cache writes instead of rolling our own:
```rust
use tempfile::NamedTempFile;

// In DtsCache::save_to_disk():
let mut tmp = NamedTempFile::new_in(cache_dir)?;
rmp_serde::encode::write(&mut tmp, &self.store)?;
tmp.persist(cache_path)?;  // atomic rename — cross-platform, handles tmp cleanup on failure
```
Already in our dev-deps (showed up in the test build output). Worth making it a regular dep for this use.

**`tracing`** — already in deps, just not being used yet. The hot paths should be instrumented:
```rust
#[tracing::instrument(skip(source), fields(path = %path))]
pub fn parse_file(path: &Utf8Path, source: &str) -> SourceData { ... }

#[tracing::instrument(skip(session))]
pub fn update_file(session: &WatchSession, path: &Utf8Path) -> IncrementalUpdate { ... }
```
This gives us free spans in the Vite plugin's dev server output and in `tracing-indicatif`'s progress bars in the CLI — no extra cost at runtime when no subscriber is attached.

**`tokio::task::spawn_blocking`** — not a new dep (tokio is already in core's deps), but an important pattern. watchexec 8.x is fully async (tokio runtime). The CLI watch loop is async. The resolution work is sync rayon. The bridge:
```rust
// In CLI watch loop (async context):
let session = Arc::clone(&session);
let update = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
    session.update_file(&changed_path)
}).await?;
```
`spawn_blocking` hands rayon's sync work to tokio's blocking thread pool, keeping the async runtime unblocked. This is the standard pattern — used by sqlx, tantivy, and pretty much every mixed async/sync Rust codebase.

**tokio in core — worth revisiting.** Looking at `crates/core/Cargo.toml`, tokio is listed as a dependency. For the pipeline, we only need `std::fs::read_to_string` inside rayon threads — that's fine as blocking I/O in a CPU thread pool. We may not need tokio in core at all. Worth auditing before Phase 3b touches pipeline.rs — an unnecessary dep adds compile time and cognitive overhead.

**`papaya`** — already transitively in deps (pulled in by something). A lock-free concurrent HashMap that outperforms DashMap under high write contention. For the DTS cache, our access pattern is write-once-per-file then read-many — DashMap's shard-based locking is fine here. Papaya would matter if we had many concurrent writes, which we don't. No change needed.

**`crossbeam-channel`** — if we need to pass incremental update results from the rayon resolution back to the watchexec async loop, `tokio::sync::mpsc` is cleaner (already have tokio). Only reach for crossbeam if we hit contention issues, which is unlikely.

---

## Anything missing from the dep list?

One gap: **`tempfile`** as a proper dep (currently only dev-dep). Everything else we need is already there.

One thing to drop or scope-restrict: **tokio from `crates/core`** if we can confirm it's not actually needed there. Core should be as lean as possible — it's what users embed via NAPI or call from rolldown natively.

Ready to update `types.rs`, spec the cache interface, and write the watch mode design into `docs/08-OPEN-QUESTIONS.md`?
Let's also consider the design of the plugins for vite and rolldown as well as the standalone CLI using the best possible crates for a create CLI DX

Let me think through each delivery mechanism carefully.

---

## Vite Plugin

**The modern Vite plugin pattern is `Plugin[]`, not `Plugin`**

Every serious Vite plugin — `@vitejs/plugin-react`, `vite-plugin-solid`, unplugin's adapters — returns an array. This lets you split concerns cleanly without users having to compose:

```ts
export function oxcReactDocgen(options?: Options): Plugin[] {
  return [
    extractionPlugin(options),      // transform: inject __docgenInfo
    virtualModulePlugin(options),   // virtual:oxc-react-docgen → full typed map
    devServerPlugin(options),       // serves /~oxc-docgen/diagnostics endpoint
  ]
}
```

**Virtual module is the missing piece in the current spec**

Right now, docgen data only exists as injected `__docgenInfo` on each component. But design systems and Storybook custom blocks need to query the whole component library at once. A virtual module solves this:

```ts
// In any file:
import { components } from 'virtual:oxc-react-docgen'
// components: Record<string, ComponentEntry> — fully typed, HMR-aware

// In a custom Storybook doc block:
import { components } from 'virtual:oxc-react-docgen'
const Button = components['Button']
```

The virtual module plugin is 30 lines: resolve the virtual ID, return a module that imports from a second internal virtual ID (`\0oxc-react-docgen`), and invalidate that module in `handleHotUpdate`. This pattern is exactly how `vite-plugin-pages`, `unplugin-icons`, and others work.

**TypeScript types for the plugin options**

The `packages/napi/index.d.ts` already defines `ComponentEntry`, `PropItem` etc. The Vite plugin should re-export these — users who write custom doc blocks get autocompletion for free.

**`enforce: 'pre'` is non-negotiable and should be documented**

If a user also runs `@vitejs/plugin-react`, our plugin must run before it. `enforce: 'pre'` guarantees this. Worth a prominent comment in the plugin source because this is a subtle but load-bearing detail.

---

## Rolldown Plugin

**The honest answer: two implementations, feature-flagged**

Rolldown's Rust plugin API exists but is still moving. The safest design:

```
packages/
├── rolldown-plugin/          # TypeScript — works today, same as Vite plugin
└── crates/rolldown-plugin/   # Native Rust — activates when API stabilizes
```

The TS rolldown plugin is a nearly identical copy of the Vite plugin — Rolldown's plugin hooks mirror Rollup/Vite's. Main differences: no `handleHotUpdate` (Rolldown has a different HMR model), and `configResolved` becomes `buildStart`.

The native Rust plugin, when the API stabilizes, eliminates the entire JSON boundary. `ComponentEntry` goes from resolver → plugin → output without serialization. For a 200-component project this probably saves ~2ms total — not dramatic, but it's the right long-term architecture and demonstrates that our core is genuinely embeddable.

**For Phase 5b the recommendation is:** ship the TS wrapper, leave a clear `// TODO: migrate to native Plugin trait when rolldown_plugin crate stabilizes` with a link to the tracking issue.

---

## CLI — Where the DX ceiling is highest

This is the area with the most room to do something exceptional. Let me go through what the best Rust CLI tools do in 2026.

**Reference CLIs:** biome (fastest JS toolchain CLI), ruff (Python linting), cargo (gold standard), bun (speed + output quality)

### Output

**`comfy-table`** — not currently in deps, should be. The `inspect` command renders a prop table. `comfy-table` handles alignment, Unicode column widths, wrapping, and has a clean builder API. Nothing else comes close for Rust CLI tables.

```
  Button                                      /src/components/ui/Button.tsx
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  
  Prop          Type                                   Req   Default    From
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  variant       "default"|"destructive"|"outline"…     –     "default"  ButtonProps
  size          "default"|"sm"|"lg"|"icon"             –     "default"  ButtonProps
  asChild       boolean                                –     false      ButtonProps

  ↳ ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement>
    Notable: onClick  disabled  type  form  name  value  aria-label
```

**`crossterm`** — not in deps, should be. For watch mode `q` to quit, `r` to force re-extract. We don't need a TUI, just raw terminal input:

```rust
// Spawn a thread for keyboard input
std::thread::spawn(|| {
    crossterm::terminal::enable_raw_mode().ok();
    loop {
        if let Ok(Event::Key(k)) = crossterm::event::read() {
            match k.code {
                KeyCode::Char('q') | KeyCode::Char('c') => std::process::exit(0),
                KeyCode::Char('r') => { FORCE_REEXTRACT.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed); }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
    }
});
```

**`console::Term`** — already transitively in deps via `indicatif`. Use it for terminal width detection in the watch mode summary line, and for clearing+rewriting the status line without flickering.

### Diagnostics

**miette's source spans need to be wired up end-to-end**

The `RawProp` and `ComponentMapping` structs already carry `span_start`/`span_end`. The CLI needs to thread these through to miette's `SourceSpan` so errors look like this:

```
  × Cannot resolve type 'ButtonVariants'
   ╭─[src/components/ui/Button.tsx:12:17]
12 │ const Button: FC<ButtonVariants> = forwardRef(...)
   ·                  ──────────────  not found in this scope
   ╰────
  help: Did you mean 'ButtonProps'? (defined at line 4)
```

This is the output that makes a tool feel professional. The spans are already collected — the CLI just needs to read the source file and pass it to miette as a `NamedSource`.

### Watch mode output

```
  ⚡  oxc-react-docgen  watching src/  (q quit · r re-extract)
  
  47 components  ·  0 warnings  ·  0 errors  ·  12ms
  
  14:23:01  src/components/ui/Button.tsx
            Button  variant size asChild → updated
  14:23:04  src/components/ui/Input.tsx  
            Input  placeholder disabled → updated
```

The spinner uses `indicatif`'s `ProgressBar::new_spinner()`, the status line uses `console::Term::clear_last_lines()` to avoid flicker, and `tracing-indicatif` wires tracing spans to the spinner so extraction sub-tasks show progress automatically.

### Config loading

**`docgen.config.ts` needs to be evaluated, not parsed**

The config file is TypeScript, so from Rust we need to shell out to Node to evaluate it. The cleanest approach:

```rust
fn load_config(root: &Utf8Path) -> Option<PipelineOptions> {
    // Emit a tiny loader script, pipe config's default export as JSON to stdout
    let script = format!(
        "import cfg from '{}'; process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(cfg.default ?? cfg))",
        root.join("docgen.config.ts")
    );
    let out = std::process::Command::new("node")
        .args(["--import", "tsx/esm", "--input-type=module"])
        .current_dir(root)
        .stdin(std::process::Stdio::piped())
        // write script to stdin
        .output().ok()?;
    serde_json::from_slice(&out.stdout).ok()
}
```

This requires `tsx` to be available (it's a peer dep of the vite plugin anyway). Fail gracefully if not present — config file is optional.

### Shell completions

**Add nushell to the completion targets**

`clap_complete` covers bash/zsh/fish/powershell. Nushell has become mainstream enough (used heavily in the Rust tooling world) to warrant first-class support. `clap_complete_nushell` is the crate.

### Version output

`oxc-react-docgen --version` should include the git commit hash in debug builds. `shadow-rs` embeds this at compile time — adds ~2s to clean builds but is invisible in incremental builds. Optional but professional:

```
oxc-react-docgen 0.1.0 (abc1234 2026-06-13)
```

---

## Crate additions summary

| Crate | Where | Why |
|-------|-------|-----|
| `comfy-table` | `crates/cli` | prop table in `inspect` command |
| `crossterm` | `crates/cli` | raw input for watch mode (`q` quit, `r` re-extract) |
| `tempfile` | `crates/core` | atomic cache writes (promote from dev-dep) |
| `clap_complete_nushell` | `crates/cli` | nushell completions |
| `shadow-rs` | `crates/cli` | git hash in `--version` (optional) |

**Remove from `crates/core`:** `tokio` — confirm it's not needed before Phase 3b writes pipeline.rs. Core should be async-free; the tokio bridge belongs in `crates/cli`.

**Use better in `crates/cli`:** `console::Term` (terminal width + line clearing), `tracing-indicatif` (wire spans to spinner), `miette::NamedSource` (source spans in errors).

---

Want me to update the workspace `Cargo.toml` and `docs/08-OPEN-QUESTIONS.md` with all of this before we launch Phase 3?

How can we make the plugin DX/config world class? Opinionated so we can run out of the box with good defaults but configurable to allow for complciated setups. Consider monorepos, the possible CSS libraries that are common, component libraries a design system might use, etc. THings liek react-aria types, etc

This is worth thinking through from first principles. The best analogy is Vite itself — zero config for standard projects, progressively more explicit for complex ones, and a preset/plugin ecosystem that means "my library" scenarios are handled by the library, not the user.

---

## The zero-config story

A Storybook user switching from RDT should need to write exactly this:

```ts
// .storybook/main.ts
viteFinal: (config) => ({
  ...config,
  plugins: [...config.plugins, oxcReactDocgen()]
})
```

Nothing else. We auto-detect everything from the file system at startup.

---

## Auto-detection at `configResolved`

Before any extraction, the plugin scans the project root once and builds a `DetectedContext`. This runs entirely in TypeScript — no Rust needed:

```ts
interface DetectedContext {
  reactVersion: '18' | '19'
  isMonorepo: boolean
  monorepoTool: 'pnpm' | 'turbo' | 'nx' | 'moon' | 'lerna' | null
  pandaOutdir: string | false
  vanillaExtract: boolean
  variantFunctions: string[]           // ['cva', 'tv', 'defineRecipe', 'recipe', ...]
  installedLibraries: Set<LibraryKey>  // 'radix' | 'mui' | 'chakra' | 'mantine' | 'react-aria' | ...
  tsconfigPath: string | null
  workspacePackages: string[]          // absolute paths to local packages in monorepo
}
```

**What each signal tells us:**

| Signal | Source | Action |
|--------|--------|--------|
| `react` version in package.json | `dependencies` | Set `reactVersion` |
| `pnpm-workspace.yaml` / `turbo.json` / `nx.json` / `.moon/workspace.yml` | Root files | Enable `crossPackage`, discover workspace packages |
| `panda.config.ts` + `styled-system/` | Root files | Set `pandaOutdir`, add styled-system to parse paths |
| `@vanilla-extract/recipes` in deps | package.json | Add `RecipeVariants` to variant function table |
| `tailwind-variants` in deps | package.json | Add `tv` to variant functions |
| `@radix-ui/*` / `@mui/*` / `@chakra-ui/*` etc. | package.json | Activate library-specific presets |
| `react-aria` / `react-aria-components` | package.json | Activate ARIA-specific known types |
| `tsconfig.json` `paths` | tsconfig | Feed to `oxc_resolver` for alias resolution |

The monorepo case is the most important. When `pnpm-workspace.yaml` is detected, we resolve all workspace package directories and add them to the resolver's search paths. This means `import { ButtonProps } from '@company/design-tokens'` resolves to `packages/design-tokens/src/index.ts` without any user configuration.

---

## The config file — `docgen.config.ts`

`defineConfig` is an identity function that exists purely for TypeScript inference, same as `vite.defineConfig`:

```ts
import { defineConfig, presets } from '@oxc-react-docgen/core'

export default defineConfig({

  // ── Source ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  
  include: ['./src', '../packages/components/src'],  // overrides auto-detected srcDirs
  exclude: ['**/internal/**', '**/*.private.*'],

  // ── React ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  
  react: '19',  // auto-detected from package.json if omitted

  // ── CSS / styling ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  
  panda: { outdir: './styled-system' },   // or false to disable
  vanillaExtract: true,                   // enables RecipeVariants<> resolution
  variantFunctions: ['myCustomVariants'], // merged with auto-detected list

  // ── Resolution ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  crossPackage: true,  // auto-detected from monorepo signals if omitted
  
  // Additional path aliases beyond tsconfig.json
  paths: {
    '@company/tokens': ['../packages/tokens/src'],
  },
  
  // ── Output ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  // Mirrors react-docgen-typescript propFilter — same signature for drop-in compat
  propFilter: (prop, component) => {
    if (prop.parent?.fileName.includes('node_modules')) return false
    if (prop.tags?.deprecated) return false
    return true
  },

  // Override the built-in notable HTML attrs table per element
  notableProps: {
    button: ['onClick', 'onKeyDown', 'disabled', 'type', 'aria-label'],
    input: ['onChange', 'value', 'defaultValue', 'placeholder', 'type'],
  },
  
  // ── Performance ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  
  cache: './node_modules/.cache/oxc-react-docgen',  // or false

  // ── Extensibility ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  
  presets: [
    presets.shadcn(),
    presets.reactAria(),
  ],
  
  plugins: [
    myInternalStyleSystemPlugin(),
  ],
})
```

---

## Presets — library-specific configs bundled as first-class options

Presets are just functions returning partial config, composed in order. We ship these:

**`presets.shadcn()`**
- Adds `asChild` to always-surface props (never filtered out)
- `VariantProps` resolution already built-in; preset just tunes notable props for Tailwind components

**`presets.mui()`**
- `SxProps` → opaque ✅
- `OverridableStringUnion` → union + opaque ✅
- `slotProps` → opaque with description "per-slot prop overrides"
- `styled()` component detection: `const Button = styled(MuiButton)<ButtonProps>` — new pattern not in current spec
- Emit a synthetic `sx` prop of type `SxProps` on any component that inherits MUI base types

**`presets.chakra()`**
- `HTMLChakraProps` / `HTMLArkProps` ✅
- `ThemingProps` ✅  
- Compound component name normalization: `MenuTrigger` → display as `Menu.Trigger`

**`presets.mantine()`**
- `StylesApiProps` ✅
- `PolymorphicFactory` components: detect `component` prop, type it as `React.ElementType`
- `MantineColor` → string union of common colors (from their theme type)

**`presets.reactAria()`**
This is the most interesting one. React Aria has two layers:

*Hooks layer* (`react-aria`): `useButton(props, ref)` — not components, we skip these.

*Components layer* (`react-aria-components`): `<Button>`, `<TextField>` etc. These ARE components. Their props follow `AriaXxxProps` naming:
- `AriaButtonProps` — extends `ButtonHTMLAttributes` minus `onClick` (replaced with `onPress`)
- Aria-specific props: `isDisabled` (not `disabled`), `excludeFromTabOrder`, `onPress`, `onPressStart`, `onPressEnd`, `onHover*`
- `RenderProps<ButtonRenderProps>` for className/style as functions

The preset needs to:
- Map `isDisabled` display → label "Disabled" (not "Is Disabled")
- Mark `onPress` as the primary event handler (not `onClick`)
- Recognize `RenderProps<T>` → expand to `className`, `style` ✅ already in known.rs
- Add `AriaButtonProps`, `AriaCheckboxProps` etc. to the react builtins table so they're recognized as terminal types

**`presets.radixThemes()`**
Radix Themes (the higher-level layer above primitives) adds:
- `color` prop typed as `AccentColor` (union of ~30 color names)
- `radius` as `Radius` enum
- `variant` as library-specific strings
- These are declared as type aliases in `@radix-ui/themes` — should resolve naturally

---

## The plugin system — split across the boundary

This is the hard part. Our resolution happens in Rust but config lives in TypeScript. The solution: **declarative patterns (Rust side) + function transforms (TypeScript side)**.

**Rust side — declarative `knownTypeOverrides`:**

```ts
// In docgen.config.ts:
knownTypeOverrides: {
  'StyledSystemProps': { kind: 'opaque', label: 'Style system props' },
  'ThemeTokens': { kind: 'alias', argIndex: 0 },          // alias to first generic arg
  'PickTheme': { kind: 'opaque', reason: 'conditional' },
}
```

These serialize to JSON, cross the NAPI boundary as part of `JsExtractOptions`, and get merged into the Rust resolver's `known.rs` dispatch table at run time. No code generation, no WASM.

**TypeScript side — function transforms run after NAPI returns:**

```ts
// In docgen.config.ts or in a plugin:
plugins: [{
  name: 'my-style-system',
  
  // Runs per-component after full resolution
  transformComponent(component) {
    // Remove internal implementation props
    delete component.props['__internalRef']
    // Rename isDisabled → disabled for display
    if (component.props['isDisabled']) {
      component.props['disabled'] = {
        ...component.props['isDisabled'],
        name: 'disabled',
      }
      delete component.props['isDisabled']
    }
    return component
  },
  
  // Runs once on the full output
  transformOutput(output) {
    // Merge variant enums into component prop descriptions
    return output
  },
}]
```

This is the same pattern that PostCSS, Vite, and unified.js use. The boundary is clear: Rust handles type resolution (fast, parallel), TypeScript handles post-processing (flexible, ecosystem access).

---

## Monorepo — the real complexity

A typical design system monorepo:
```
company-design-system/
├── packages/
│   ├── tokens/          # CSS variables, theme values — TYPES needed by resolver
│   ├── icons/           # Icon components — should appear in docgen
│   ├── components/      # Main components
│   │   ├── src/
│   │   │   ├── Button.tsx
│   │   │   └── types.ts    ← ButtonProps lives here
│   │   └── package.json    # { "name": "@company/components" }
│   └── react-utils/     # Hooks, higher-order components
└── apps/
    └── storybook/
        ├── .storybook/
        └── package.json    # { "devDependencies": { "@company/components": "workspace:*" } }
```

**The resolver path**:
1. Storybook Vite runs from `apps/storybook/`
2. Plugin detects monorepo via `pnpm-workspace.yaml`
3. Discovers workspace packages: `packages/tokens`, `packages/icons`, `packages/components`
4. Passes all src dirs to extraction pipeline
5. `oxc_resolver` resolves `import { ButtonProps } from '@company/components'` → `packages/components/src/index.ts`
6. No configuration required

**Where it gets complicated — barrel files:**

Design systems almost always have `packages/components/src/index.ts` that re-exports everything. Our `import_map.rs` already handles `export { Button } from './Button'` chains. The resolver walks the chain to find where `ButtonProps` actually lives.

**Where it gets very complicated — `.d.ts`-only packages:**

Some packages ship pre-compiled: `dist/index.d.ts` only, no source. The DTS cache is essential here. These files are parsed once, cached, and reused. `oxc_resolver` with `condition_names: ["types", "typings"]` finds the `.d.ts` entry point.

**The `paths` config option bridges the gap:**

When a workspace package isn't in `node_modules` (during active development before build), explicit `paths` lets users tell us where to look:
```ts
paths: {
  '@company/tokens': ['../../packages/tokens/src'],
}
```

This feeds directly into `oxc_resolver`'s alias configuration.

---

## Libraries that need special extractor handling (not just resolver)

**Styled Components / Emotion** — currently unhandled at the extractor level:
```ts
const Button = styled.button<ButtonProps>`...`
const Button = styled(BaseButton)<ButtonProps>`...`
```

These patterns need new detection in Phase 2a (or a follow-up). The generic type param IS the props type. Not in the current spec at all.

**`@vanilla-extract/recipes`:**
```ts
const buttonRecipe = recipe({
  variants: { size: { sm: '...', lg: '...' } }
})
type ButtonVariants = RecipeVariants<typeof buttonRecipe>
```
`RecipeVariants` → same as `VariantProps`. Add to `known.rs`. The extractor also needs to detect `recipe()` calls (like it detects `cva()` calls) to populate the enums table.

**React Aria Components `RenderProps` children:**
```ts
<Button>
  {({ isHovered, isPressed }) => `Button ${isPressed ? 'pressed' : ''}`}
</Button>
```
The `children` prop is `ReactNode | ((values: ButtonRenderProps) => ReactNode)`. We should surface this as a `RenderProps` type rather than a raw union.

---

## What changes in Rust

**`PipelineOptions` additions:**
```rust
pub struct PipelineOptions {
    // ... existing ...
    pub known_type_overrides: FxHashMap<String, KnownTypeOverride>,
    pub ts_config_path: Option<Utf8PathBuf>,
    pub extra_paths: FxHashMap<String, Vec<Utf8PathBuf>>,  // for monorepo aliases
    pub detect_styled_components: bool,
    pub vanilla_extract: bool,  // enables RecipeVariants<> in known.rs
}

pub enum KnownTypeOverride {
    Opaque { label: Option<String> },
    Alias { arg_index: usize },
    Skip,  // pretend the type doesn't exist — removes it from output
}
```

**`known.rs` additions:**
- `RecipeVariants` (vanilla-extract) → same handler as `VariantProps`
- `recipe` call detection for enum population (same as `cva`)
- User overrides from `PipelineOptions.known_type_overrides` checked first, before built-in table

**`react_types.rs` additions:**
- `AriaButtonProps`, `AriaCheckboxProps`, `AriaTextFieldProps` etc. → add to `is_react_builtin()` so they're recognized as terminal (the RAC layer extends them — that's what we resolve)
- `AccentColor`, `Radius` from Radix Themes → NOT built-in, resolve normally (they're string unions in the package)

---

## The Vite plugin — updated architecture

```ts
export function oxcReactDocgen(userOptions: Options = {}): Plugin[] {
  const ctx = new PluginContext(userOptions)  // holds session, detection results, options
  
  return [
    extractionPlugin(ctx),    // enforce: 'pre', transform, handleHotUpdate
    virtualPlugin(ctx),        // virtual:oxc-react-docgen → ComponentEntry map
    diagnosticsPlugin(ctx),    // /__oxc_docgen/diagnostics endpoint in dev
  ]
}
```

The three-plugin split means each concern is independently testable and users can opt out of specific pieces if needed.

The `virtual:oxc-react-docgen` module is the most valuable addition for design system teams — it lets them build custom documentation sites, automated prop table generators, and design token viewers that query the live extraction result:

```ts
// In a Storybook custom block or documentation site:
import type { ExtractionOutput } from '@oxc-react-docgen/core'
// @ts-expect-error — virtual module
import docgen from 'virtual:oxc-react-docgen'
const output = docgen as ExtractionOutput
```

## Vite & Rolldown Roadmap Report for Plugin Authors (2026)

### 1. Vite 6 → 7 → 8 Plugin API Evolution

**Released Timeline:**
- **Vite 6** (2024): Formalized the Environment API for multi-environment support (client, SSR, custom)
- **Vite 7** (2025): Major stability push on Environment API
- **Vite 8** (March 2026): Full Rolldown integration as replacement for Rollup + esbuild

**Critical Plugin Hook Changes:**

The biggest shift is **`this.environment` context** replacing the old `ssr` boolean. Hooks now receive:
- `this.environment.name` - environment identifier
- `this.environment.config` - environment-specific configuration
- `this.environment.moduleGraph` - module graph for that environment

This affects: `resolveId`, `load`, `transform`, `transform`, `moduleParsed`, `renderChunk`, `generateBundle`, etc.

### 2. Rolldown Integration Status

**Timeline Met:** Rolldown was integrated into Vite 8 (March 12, 2026) with 10–30x faster builds. The temporary `rolldown-vite` repository was archived March 19, 2026, indicating the work is complete.

**For Plugin Authors:**
- Rolldown's plugin API is **nearly 100% compatible with Rollup** but with key differences:
  - **Sequential execution:** Parallel hooks run sequentially
  - **Output handling:** Each output generates separately (affects plugin state)
  - **Watch mode:** The `options` hook runs once at watcher creation, not per rebuild
  - **Missing hooks:** `shouldTransformCachedModule`, `resolveImportMeta`, `resolveFileUrl`, `renderDynamicImport` are unsupported

### 3. Vite Environment API (Critical for TSDoc Analysis Plugin)

The Environment API allows a single Vite dev server to handle multiple concurrent environments:

**For Your Use Case (TypeScript Source Analysis):**
- Use `configEnvironment` hook to configure environment-specific settings (e.g., which environments should have `__docgenInfo` injected)
- Use `applyToEnvironment` hook to control which environments your plugin operates on
- Access `this.environment.moduleGraph` to inspect the module dependency tree for docgen purposes
- Store per-environment state using `Map<Environment, State>` to separate client vs. SSR docgen metadata

**Breaking Pattern:** The old pattern of checking `ssr` option is deprecated. Replace with:
```javascript
// Old (deprecated)
if (options.ssr) { ... }

// New
if (this.environment.name === 'ssr') { ... }
```

### 4. Rolldown Native Rust Plugin API

**Stability:** Rolldown 1.0 RC signals API stability with semantic versioning lock. The `^1.0.0` API is backward-compatible with no breaking changes planned pre-1.0.

**Performance Features:**
- Hook filters skip the Rust-to-JS boundary when filters don't match (no linear slowdown per plugin)
- Native MagicString (Rust) generates source maps in background threads
- Built-in plugins in Rust (replace, esmExternalRequire) avoid JavaScript overhead

**Important:** When implementing for Rolldown, you're constrained by the hook subset above—you cannot rely on missing Rollup hooks.

### 5. Hook Changes: handleHotUpdate → hotUpdate

**Timeline:** `hotUpdate` introduced in v6.0; `handleHotUpdate` deprecation planned for a future major (not yet enforced).

**Migration Path Available:** Set `future.removePluginHookHandleHotUpdate: "warn"` in config to preview the deprecation.

**Key Differences:**
- **`hotUpdate`** is called once per environment with environment-specific module nodes
- **`hotUpdate`** handles `create`, `delete`, and `update` watch events (not just `update`)
- **`handleHotUpdate`** is environment-agnostic and mixed across all environments

For a multi-environment docgen plugin, `hotUpdate` is essential—you need to invalidate docgen metadata per environment when source files change.

### 6. Module Federation in Vite/Rolldown

**Status:** Multiple implementations exist in 2026:
- `@module-federation/vite` supports Vite 8 + Rolldown
- `vite-plugin-federation` supports Vite 5–8 with Rolldown

**Native Support Planned:** When Vite fully switched to Rolldown, a plan emerged for native MF support integrated directly into Vite (status: in progress).

**Impact on Your Plugin:** If used with Module Federation, be aware that named exports for remote modules now preserve correctly in Rolldown (fixed in 2026).

### 7. Virtual Module API (Stable, No Changes)

The virtual module pattern remains stable:
- Prefix resolved IDs with `\0` to prevent other plugins from processing them
- Use `resolveId` hook to detect virtual module patterns and return `\0` prefixed IDs
- Use `load` hook to return module content
- Convention: prefix user-facing IDs with `virtual:` (e.g., `virtual:my-plugin:docgen-info`)

**Encoding:** In dev, `\0{id}` becomes `/@id/__x00__{id}` in the browser but is decoded before the plugin pipeline.

### 8. Deprecations Your Plugin Must Avoid

**Critical for Vite 8+:**

1. **`moduleType` in load/transform:** If your `load` or `transform` hook returns content, you **must** add `moduleType: 'js'` to the return value. Rolldown requires this.

2. **`options.esbuild` → `options.oxc`:** JavaScript transformation now uses Oxc instead of esbuild. If you call `transformWithEsbuild` directly, switch to `transformWithOxc`.

3. **`build.rollupOptions` → `build.rolldownOptions`:** Config for bundler is now `rolldownOptions`.

4. **`resolve.alias[].customResolver` removed:** Implement a custom plugin with `resolveId` hook + `enforce: 'pre'` instead.

5. **CJS Node API deprecated:** If your plugin uses Vite's Node API, migrate to ESM-only imports.

### 9. Recommendations for Your TypeScript Docgen Plugin

**For Vite 8+ Compatibility:**
1. Add `moduleType: 'js'` to all transform/load hook returns
2. Use `this.environment` to manage per-environment docgen metadata
3. Implement `hotUpdate` hook (not `handleHotUpdate`) for environment-aware invalidation
4. Use `configEnvironment` hook if you need environment-specific docgen settings
5. Avoid the missing Rolldown hooks; implement custom solutions if needed
6. Consider native Rust plugin if performance becomes critical (future-proofing)

**For Virtual Module Approach:**
Keep your `virtual:plugin-name:docgen-info` pattern—it's stable and widely used.

7	 * render any element/component as the button root while keeping full type
8	 * safety. Supporting types from @mantine/core are stubbed inline so this
9	 * file is self-contained.

12	 *   - `MantineColor` is a string alias (supports theme color keys like
13	 *     `'blue'`, `'red.5'`, or arbitrary CSS colors)
14	 *   - `MantineSize` / `MantineRadius` are theme-token string | number types
15	 *   - `StylesApiProps` provides `classNames`, `styles`, and `unstyled` for
16	 *     deep component customisation via the Styles API
17	 *   - `gradient` is a structured object used when `variant='gradient'`
18	 *   - `loaderProps` forwards to the internal Loader component
19	 *   - `leftSection` / `rightSection` (Mantine v7 naming, replaces leftIcon/rightIcon)
20	 *   - `component` enables polymorphic rendering (e.g. as an `<a>` or Next.js Link)
21	 */

24	// Mantine theme token types (simplified stubs)

29	 * a key with shade index (e.g. `'blue.5'`), or any valid CSS color string.

39	 * Border-radius token: one of the predefined size keys, a number (pixels),
40	 * or an arbitrary CSS string.

68	  Record<Selectors, React.CSSProperties>
