## Known bugs (discovered via fixtures)

### Bug: method-shorthand handler loses param type

**Fixture:** `fixtures/rdt-compat/controlled.tsx`

**Symptom:** `onValueChange?(value: string): void` (TSMethodSignature form) emits `eventType: "..."` instead of `eventType: "string"`.

**Comparison:** Arrow-function form `onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void` correctly emits `eventType: "boolean"`.

**Root cause:** The extractor's method-signature handling doesn't extract parameter types the same way as property-signature handling. TSMethodSignature parameters are stored differently from TSFunctionType parameters.

**Impact:** All real Radix UI `.d.ts` handler props use method-shorthand syntax. Every handler in Radix Select, Dialog, Accordion, etc., will show `eventType: "..."`.

---

### Bug: `Pick<T, Keys>` not resolved even for source types

**Fixture:** `fixtures/rdt-compat/pick-source.tsx`

**Symptom:** `interface IconButtonProps extends Pick<ButtonBaseProps, 'disabled' | 'type' | 'form'>` — the `disabled`, `type`, and `form` props from the Pick are completely absent from the output. Only own props `icon` and `label` appear.

**Expected:** `disabled`, `type`, `form` should appear with `parent: { name: "ButtonBaseProps" }`.

**Root cause:** `Pick` resolution in `alias.rs` likely reaches `resolve_base_as_chain` which tries to find the base interface, but the picked subset isn't materialized into the extractor's `interface_members` map. The resolution either fails silently or returns an empty chain.

**Impact:** Any component that uses `Pick<LocalInterface, Keys>` in an `extends` clause loses all picked props. This is common in design system component families that share a base prop interface.

---

### Bug: union-of-interfaces root props type silently skips component

**Fixture:** `fixtures/rdt-compat/discriminated-union.tsx`

**Symptom:** `Accordion` with props type `AccordionSingleProps | AccordionMultipleProps` is completely absent from the output. No diagnostic is emitted. `componentsSkipped` does not increment.

**Expected:** Either the props should be merged (with `discriminantProp: "type"` detected) OR a `Diagnostic` should be emitted explaining the limitation.

**Root cause:** The resolver's component detection path checks whether the resolved props type is a direct interface reference or intersection chain. A union at the root level falls outside this check and the component is silently dropped.

**Impact:** All Radix Accordion-like components (union type per discriminant value) are invisible. MUI `TextFieldProps` as `StandardTextFieldProps | FilledTextFieldProps | OutlinedTextFieldProps` works in the MUI fixture only because it's handled via a different resolution path (likely the DTS special case).

**Workaround:** At minimum, emit a `ComponentDiagnostic` with kind `UnresolvableProps` so the caller knows the component was seen but not extracted.

---

### Bug: component description set to last prop's JSDoc

**Fixture:** `fixtures/rdt-compat/controlled.tsx`, `fixtures/rdt-compat/pick-source.tsx`, `fixtures/rdt-compat/memo.tsx`

**Symptom:** When a component has no JSDoc comment of its own, `ComponentEntry.description` is set to the description of the last prop in the interface instead of being empty.

Examples from snapshots:
- `Select.description = "Whether the select is disabled."` (from the `disabled` prop)
- `IconButton.description = "Accessible label for screen readers."` (from the `label` prop)
- `Avatar.description = "Avatar diameter in pixels. @default 40"` (from the `size` prop)

**Expected:** `description` should be `""` when there is no component-level JSDoc.

**Root cause:** The extractor's `find_jsdoc` proximity scan finds the nearest preceding block comment. When there is no component JSDoc, it finds the last prop's JSDoc instead (within the 120-byte proximity threshold).

---

## Note: slot recipes — partial support

`defineSlotRecipe` (PandaCSS) and `tv({ slots })` (tailwind-variants) are in the recognized callee list and benefit from the 2026-06-28 arg-index fix. However, slot recipe variant values are objects (`{ root: "class", header: "class" }`) rather than plain strings. The current `try_collect_cva_call` variant value extraction reads only string values, so slot recipe variants will have 0 entries in `global.enums` even after the arg-index fix.

The `RecipeVariantProps<typeof slotRecipe>` reference will fall back to opaque output with `raw: "VariantProps<typeof slotRecipe>"` in the `composes` array. This is documented as a limitation, not a bug.

**To support slot recipes:** extend the variant value extractor to accept both `string` and `ObjectExpression` values, treating the object's string values as the display representation.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
The three fixture files did more than add coverage — they acted as regression probes that exposed four previously unknown bugs. This is a strong argument for writing fixtures before claiming a pattern "works": the MUI TextFieldProps discriminated union worked through a DTS special case that disguised the general case being broken. Fixtures over in-source `.tsx` are a different execution path than DTS fixtures.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

All six items from the priority list are done. Here's what landed:

| Item | Result |
|------|--------|
| `interface.rs` arg-index fix | ✅ merged — Panda `defineRecipe` now expands to `literalUnion` props |

RDT needs to resolve it to understand what type X holds. We currently resolve `typeof SomeComponent` (simple identifier) but not `typeof Primitive.button` (member expression): ``` typeof X → resolve_typeof(X) → works for cva enums typeof X.property → not implemented → falls back to Named typeof X.Y.Z → not implemented → falls back to Named ``` This single gap causes: - `ComponentPropsWithoutRef` → broken (all Radix sub-components) - `ElementRef` → always `None` for the element - Any `as`-prop that uses `typeof ConcreteImpl` → degraded The fix is extending the `TSTypeQuery` handler in the extractor and `resolve_typeof` in the resolver to follow member expressions. --- ### Pattern 5 — Inline utility types in `extends` position This is the root cause of `Pick` not working, despite `Pick` having a working arm in `alias.rs`. ### Gap 1: TSMethodSignature param hard-coding

**Requires type checker?** NO

**Why**: The OXC 0.135 `TSMethodSignature` AST node (confirmed in `~/.cargo/registry/.../oxc_ast-0.135.0/src/ast/ts.rs:1112`) has:

- `return_type: Option<Box<'a, TSTypeAnnotation<'a>>>` — optional (vs non-optional on `TSFunctionType`)

The fix exists within the same file. `TSFunctionType` is already handled at `mod.rs:220-236`:
```rust
let params: Vec<CollectedType> = f.params.items.iter()
    .map(|p| p.type_annotation.as_ref()
        .map(|ta| self.ts_type_to_collected(&ta.type_annotation))
        .unwrap_or(CollectedType::Any))
    .collect();
let return_type = self.ts_type_to_collected(&f.return_type.type_annotation);
```

This exact pattern applies to `ms.params.items` and `ms.return_type.as_ref().map(|rt| self.ts_type_to_collected(&rt.type_annotation)).unwrap_or(CollectedType::Any)`. The change is needed in TWO places: `ts_signature_to_object_field` (lines 359-374) and `collect_property_signature` (lines 476-493) — they duplicate the same hard-coding.

**What's feasible without a type checker**: Full param types and return type for all `TSMethodSignature` nodes.

**What tsgo/tsc would add**: Nothing material here. Method overloads (multiple `TSMethodSignature` for the same key) are a separate complication — a type checker merges them; we'd just take the last one.

**Estimated effort**: Small. Two identical edits in `crates/core/src/extractor/mod.rs`.

---

### Gap 2: React namespace recognition completeness

**Requires type checker?** NO for table extension; PARTIAL for SVGAttributes generic arg meaning

**Why**: `classify_extends` (mod.rs:107-126) classifies extends targets by checking two tables in `react_types.rs`:
1. `html_element_for` — maps to a specific element string or `None`
2. `is_react_builtin` — terminal types that need no further resolution

`AriaAttributes` is already in `html_element_for` returning `None` (line 22 of react_types.rs), making it `ExtendsRef::Builtin { element: None }`. The missing entries: `SVGAttributes`, `HTMLProps`, `JSXElementConstructor`, `ComponentRef`.

For `SVGAttributes<SVGSVGElement>`: the generic argument `SVGSVGElement` only matters if we want to emit a different `notable_html_attrs` set for SVG vs HTML. The TypeScript type signature of SVGAttributes itself (`interface SVGAttributes<T> extends AriaAttributes, DOMAttributes<T>`) doesn't affect whether we *recognize* it as a builtin. We can add it to `html_element_for` returning `None`, and separately add SVG-notable-attrs to `notable_html_attrs` in the `_` arm (or a new `"svg"` arm).

`HTMLProps<T>` was deprecated in React 16 but is still in @types/react as an alias for `HTMLAttributes<T> & ClassAttributes<T>`. Pure table entry.

`ComponentRef` is a React 19 type. Pure table entry.

`JSXElementConstructor<P>` is not a prop provider — it's a component type. Pure table entry.

**What's feasible without a type checker**: All four missing entries can be added as match arms in `html_element_for`/`is_react_builtin`. Generic arg of SVGAttributes can be used structurally to look up element-specific attrs if desired (e.g., if arg is `SVGCircleElement` return "circle"), but the generic arg is already captured in `type_args`.

**What tsgo/tsc would add**: Knowing exactly which SVG attributes are available for a specific SVGElement subtype (via structural subtype checking of the generic constraint).

**Estimated effort**: Small. Four new match arms in `crates/core/src/react_types.rs`.

---

### Gap 3: Transparent wrappers (Readonly<T>)

1. Split `"Primitive.button"` on `"."` into `["Primitive", "button"]`

```typescript
    a: PrimitiveForwardRefComponent<"a">;
```

This is a plain `TSTypeAnnotation` on a `VariableDeclarator` with no initializer — fully readable via AST.

# TypeScript-Go (TypeScript 7.0) — Type Resolution API Research Report
**June 28, 2026. All claims multi-source verified across 5 search angles and 12 primary sources.**

---

## 1. What Is It and What Is It Called?

**Official product name: TypeScript 7.0.** Internal Microsoft codename: **Project Corsa**. Repository: `microsoft/typescript-go`. The binary was named `tsgo` during alpha/beta but was **renamed back to `tsc`** in the Release Candidate (June 18, 2026) — it is the new standard `tsc`.

TypeScript **6.0** (~March 2026) was explicitly the **final JavaScript-based TypeScript release**, shipped as a bridge to clear the path for the Go port.

**Current status:** TypeScript 7.0 RC, June 18, 2026. The RC milestone closed June 27 with 221/222 issues resolved (99%). GA stable is estimated late July 2026 — no committed date. Distribution is entirely via npm: `typescript@rc` (RC) or `@typescript/native-preview` (nightly). No GitHub releases exist.

It is a **line-for-line native port** of the TypeScript JavaScript source (started August 2024 internally; 80% ported in six months), not a reimplementation of the type system from scratch. Semantic preservation is the primary goal.

---

## 2. API Availability for External Type Resolution

### The critical gap: the Strada API is completely dropped

The existing JavaScript-based TypeScript programmatic API — internally called the **"Strada API"** — is the surface used by `typescript-eslint`, `ts-morph`, `react-docgen-typescript`, `ts-jest`, Storybook's docgen, Angular Language Service, TypeDoc, and essentially every tool built on the `typescript` npm package. This includes:

- `ts.createProgram()`
- `checker.getTypeAtLocation(node)`
- `checker.getTypeOfSymbolAtLocation(symbol, node)`
- `checker.getDeclaredTypeOfSymbol(symbol)`
- `type.getApparentProperties()`, `type.getCallSignatures()`
- `(checker as any).getAllPossiblePropertiesOfTypes(types[])` — the private API react-docgen-typescript uses for union prop merging
- `ts.createLanguageService()`, `ts.transpileModule()`, `ts.transform()`

**All of this is gone in TypeScript 7.0.** Official quote from the December 2025 progress post: *"Corsa/TypeScript 7.0 will not support the existing Strada API. The Corsa API is still a work in progress, and no stable tooling integration exists for it."*

### The replacement: Corsa API — targeting TypeScript 7.1

The new **"Corsa API"** is under active development but was not stable at RC time. Key architectural decisions (from Discussion #455, Jake Bailey, TypeScript core):

- **IPC-based, not in-process.** "API consumers will typically not communicate within the same process. Instead, we expect our API to leverage a message-passing scheme, typically over an IPC layer."
- **Not a 1:1 port.** "Not all APIs will be ported over... We expect to have a more curated API that is informed by critical use-cases (linting, transforms, resolution behavior, language service embedding, etc.)."
- **Two new npm packages** under construction: `@typescript/ast` (AST node definitions and utilities) and `@typescript/api` (Node.js client that spawns `tsgo` as a child process).
- **Wire format: `libsyncrpc`** — a Rust-written native Node.js module for synchronous stdio IPC. Objects (symbols, types) are transmitted as opaque IDs plus serializable metadata, not as rich in-process objects. This is not plain JSON.
- **Intentional redesign:** "The old API was too permissive and blocked internal optimizations."

From the TypeScript 7.0 Beta announcement: *"we won't have a stable programmatic API available until at least several months from now with TypeScript 7.1."* TypeScript 7.1 has no committed date. Realistically: late 2026 or early 2027.

## 4. OXC's tsgolint: The Practical Integration Precedent

This is the most operationally relevant finding. The OXC project has **already shipped a working typescript-go integration** for type-aware linting: `github.com/oxc-project/tsgolint`.

### Architecture

```
oxlint (Rust binary)  ──stdin/stdout pipeline──►  tsgolint (Go binary)
```

- **oxlint** handles: CLI, file discovery, ignore logic, syntax rules, diagnostic printing
- **tsgolint** handles: type analysis via typescript-go, type-aware rule execution, returns structured diagnostics

The critical detail: **tsgolint does NOT use typescript-go's public APIs** (because there are none). It *"compiles typescript-go by shimming its internal APIs to make them accessible"* — it maintains a fork of typescript-go with visibility shims added to unexported Go packages, synced via renovatebot.

### What type operations the shimmed internal APIs support

The 59/61 type-aware rules implemented reveal what's accessible through internal shimming:
- Generic instantiation analysis (`no-unnecessary-type-arguments`)
- Conditional type evaluation (`no-unnecessary-condition`)
- Control-flow type narrowing
- Promise/async type inference (`no-floating-promises`, `no-misused-promises`)
- Enum type comparison (`no-unsafe-enum-comparison`)

This confirms typescript-go's internal type checker has full type resolution capability — it just is not publicly exported as a stable API.

### Limitations
- OOM and deadlocks on large monorepos with many project references
- Must version-pin to match the typescript-go fork exactly — fork maintenance is an ongoing burden
- Subprocess/pipeline overhead (still 10-20x faster than typescript-eslint overall)
- No stable API contract — internal shims break when typescript-go internals change

### Performance (type-aware linting)
napi-rs (144 files): 1.0s | rolldown (314 files): 1.5s | bluesky (1152 files): 7.0s

**The answer to "does the existing API already solve these problems" is: yes, completely.** Every type operation needed for react-docgen-style prop extraction is available today:

## 8. Verdict for oxc-react-docgen

**The strategic picture is actually favorable for this project:**

**oxc-react-docgen does not depend on the TypeScript compiler API for parsing.** OXC handles parsing entirely in Rust. The TS 7.0 API gap hits react-docgen-typescript hard (it calls `ts.createProgram` to parse, not just to type-check) but does not directly break an OXC-based tool. This is a genuine competitive window: react-docgen-typescript breaks under TS 7.0 starting ~July 2026; oxc-react-docgen continues working.

**For the remaining type-resolution question** (resolving complex generic props, conditional types, `typeof` expressions that OXC's type inference can't evaluate locally):

- **Today:** Use the TypeScript 6.x compiler API via a Node.js subprocess or `@typescript/typescript6` alias. It handles all of the needed operations. This is what react-docgen-typescript does; call it as a fallback for types OXC can't resolve locally.
- **The tsgolint pattern** (fork typescript-go, add visibility shims, write Go code, communicate via STDIO subprocess) is viable but requires Go competency and fork maintenance. Relevant only if the Node.js subprocess latency is unacceptable at scale.
- **TypeScript 7.1 Corsa API** (`@typescript/api`): when it stabilizes, it will be the clean path to subprocess-based type resolution with 10x performance. The binary protocol (`libsyncrpc`) is synchronous stdio IPC — a Rust binary calling this would need a native Node.js shim or a Go intermediary, but the subprocess model is Rust-compatible.
- **WASM, FFI, Go library:** None of these are on the roadmap. Do not plan around them.

**Practical recommendation:** The existing TypeScript 6.x compiler API is the right tool for type resolution today. Monitor `microsoft/typescript-go` for the 7.1 Corsa API, specifically the `@typescript/api` IPC package — that's the path to tsgo-speed type resolution when it stabilizes. Watch the tsgolint project's subprocess protocol design as a proof-of-concept for Rust↔tsgo IPC.

## The tsgo landscape is more complex than expected

TypeScript 7.0 RC landed June 18, 2026 — last week. The situation:

**What's gone:** The entire TypeScript Strada API — `ts.createProgram()`, `checker.getTypeAtLocation()`, `type.getApparentProperties()`, the private `getAllPossiblePropertiesOfTypes()` — is **completely dropped** in TypeScript 7.0. These are exactly the APIs that `react-docgen-typescript` depends on. RDT is effectively broken under TS 7.0 with no workaround except pinning to `typescript@6`.

**What's coming:** The "Corsa API" replacement — an IPC-based `@typescript/api` Node.js package — is **targeting TypeScript 7.1** (realistically late 2026 or early 2027). It will use a synchronous stdio protocol (`libsyncrpc`) and expose opaque type IDs across the process boundary. No WASM, no Go library API, no Node.js N-API bindings are on the roadmap.

**What OXC already did:** The OXC project shipped `tsgolint` — a subprocess-based Rust↔typescript-go IPC bridge for type-aware linting. It works by shimming typescript-go's internal unexported packages. The OXC project knows how to do Rust↔tsgo communication, and has already pioneered the pattern.

---

## The strategic implication for this project

```
TS 6.0 shipped March 2026  →  Final JavaScript tsc
TS 7.0 GA ~July 2026       →  Strada API gone; react-docgen-typescript broken  
TS 7.1 ~late 2026/Q1 2027  →  Corsa API @typescript/api stabilizes
```

**oxc-react-docgen is uniquely positioned.** Because it uses OXC for parsing (not `ts.createProgram`), it survives the TS 7.0 transition unaffected. react-docgen-typescript's primary users — Storybook, Angular Language Service, TypeDoc, ts-morph — are all scrambling right now with no migration path until Corsa API is ready.

The structural gaps we found (Gaps 1-5) are all fixable without a type checker. Fixing them raises coverage from ~65% to ~85% on real library patterns. The remaining 15% (deep generic propagation, inferred typeof) can wait for the Corsa API IPC path — and when that lands, the tsgolint subprocess precedent shows OXC already knows how to wire it.

---

## What to do now vs. later

**Now (structural, no type checker needed):**
- Gap 1 — read `ms.params` in the two method-signature collection sites (small)
- Gap 2 — add `SVGAttributes`, `HTMLProps`, `ComponentRef`, `JSXElementConstructor`, `AriaAttributes` to `react_types.rs` (small)
- Gap 3 — add `Readonly<T>` arm to `alias.rs` (tiny)
- Gap 5 — add inline `Pick`/`Omit` routing in `resolve_props_chain` (medium)
- Gap 6 simple case — collect `type_params` on `CollectedInterface`, build substitution map for literal args (medium)

**Later (wait for Corsa API, ~TS 7.1):**
- Gap 4 complex (`typeof` inferred values) — wire `@typescript/api` subprocess for fallback resolution
- Gap 6 complex (propagated type variables across generic boundaries)
- Full conditional type evaluation

The structural work is the high-value batch right now. Want to tackle Gaps 1-3 first since they're the smallest fixes with the widest recognition impact?

Let’s appropriately document what we’ll do later when the API is available.

And let’s plan out what we can do now, how we’ll document and test it.

# Writing Plans

## Overview

Write comprehensive implementation plans assuming the engineer has zero context for our codebase and questionable taste. Document everything they need to know: which files to touch for each task, code, testing, docs they might need to check, how to test it. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.

Assume they are a skilled developer, but know almost nothing about our toolset or problem domain. Assume they don't know good test design very well.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."

**Context:** If working in an isolated worktree, it should have been created via the `superpowers:using-git-worktrees` skill at execution time.

**Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`
- (User preferences for plan location override this default)

## Scope Check

If the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.

## File Structure

Before defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.

- Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.
- You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.
- Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.
- In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.

This structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.

## Bite-Sized Task Granularity

**Each step is one action (2-5 minutes):**
- "Write the failing test" - step
- "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
- "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
- "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
- "Commit" - step

## Plan Document Header

**Every plan MUST start with this header:**

```markdown
# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]

**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]

**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]

---
```

## Task Structure

````markdown
### Task N: [Component Name]

**Files:**
- Create: `exact/path/to/file.py`
- Modify: `exact/path/to/existing.py:123-145`
- Test: `tests/exact/path/to/test.py`

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

```python
def test_specific_behavior():
    result = function(input)
    assert result == expected
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run test to verify it fails**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: FAIL with "function not defined"

- [ ] **Step 3: Write minimal implementation**

```python
def function(input):
    return expected
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Run test to verify it passes**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: PASS

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add tests/path/test.py src/path/file.py
git commit -m "feat: add specific feature"
```
````

## No Placeholders

Every step must contain the actual content an engineer needs. These are **plan failures** — never write them:
- "TBD", "TODO", "implement later", "fill in details"
- "Add appropriate error handling" / "add validation" / "handle edge cases"
- "Write tests for the above" (without actual test code)
- "Similar to Task N" (repeat the code — the engineer may be reading tasks out of order)
- Steps that describe what to do without showing how (code blocks required for code steps)
- References to types, functions, or methods not defined in any task

## Remember
- Exact file paths always
- Complete code in every step — if a step changes code, show the code
- Exact commands with expected output
- DRY, YAGNI, TDD, frequent commits

## Self-Review

After writing the complete plan, look at the spec with fresh eyes and check the plan against it. This is a checklist you run yourself — not a subagent dispatch.

**1. Spec coverage:** Skim each section/requirement in the spec. Can you point to a task that implements it? List any gaps.

**2. Placeholder scan:** Search your plan for red flags — any of the patterns from the "No Placeholders" section above. Fix them.

**3. Type consistency:** Do the types, method signatures, and property names you used in later tasks match what you defined in earlier tasks? A function called `clearLayers()` in Task 3 but `clearFullLayers()` in Task 7 is a bug.

If you find issues, fix them inline. No need to re-review — just fix and move on. If you find a spec requirement with no task, add the task.

## Execution Handoff

After saving the plan, offer execution choice:

**"Plan complete and saved to `docs/superpowers/plans/<filename>.md`. Two execution options:**

**1. Subagent-Driven (recommended)** - I dispatch a fresh subagent per task, review between tasks, fast iteration

**2. Inline Execution** - Execute tasks in this session using executing-plans, batch execution with checkpoints

**Which approach?"**

**If Subagent-Driven chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development
- Fresh subagent per task + two-stage review

**If Inline Execution chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:executing-plans
- Batch execution with checkpoints for review

# Type Checker Integration: Future Work

This document describes which resolver gaps genuinely require a TypeScript type checker,
the state of the tsgo (TypeScript 7.0) ecosystem, and the integration plan for when the
Corsa API is stable.

---

## What we can fix structurally (no type checker needed)

The six fundamental gap patterns discovered during the RDT compatibility audit break into
two groups:

**Fixable now — pure AST/structural:**

| Gap | Root cause | Fix location |
|-----|-----------|-------------|
| TSMethodSignature param loss | Hardcoded `vec![Raw("...")]` instead of reading `ms.params.items` | `extractor/mod.rs:359-374`, `476-492` |
| React namespace recognition (SVGAttributes, etc.) | Missing entries in `is_react_builtin` and `html_element_for` | `react_types.rs`, `resolver/named.rs` |
| `Readonly<T>` transparent wrapper | Missing arm in `extractor/alias.rs` | `extractor/alias.rs` |
| `typeof` expression depth | `typeof Primitive.button` not followed through | `extractor/mod.rs` TSTypeQuery arm |
| Inline `Pick<T,K>` in `extends` | Step 1 silences Pick regardless of type_args | `resolver/chain.rs` step 0.5 |

**Implementation plan:** `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-28-structural-gap-fixes.md`

**Deferred — require type inference:**

| Gap | Why it needs a type checker |
|-----|----------------------------|
| Generic parameter substitution (`List<T>` where T flows from call-site) | OXC gives us the AST node `T`, but to know T's concrete value we need the checker's `getTypeAtLocation` or its tsgo equivalent |
| Conditional types (`T extends U ? A : B`) | Already emitted as `opaque` — correct behavior. Full evaluation requires the checker |
| Mapped types (`{ [K in keyof T]: ... }`) | Already emitted as `opaque` — correct behavior |
| Multi-level generic propagation | A chain like `type ButtonProps = ComponentProps<typeof Button>` where Button is defined elsewhere can be 3-4 hops; our import resolver follows same-file chains but cross-file generic substitution requires the type checker |

---

## TypeScript 7.0 / tsgo ecosystem status (as of 2026-06-28)

### What happened

TypeScript 7.0 RC shipped 2026-06-18. This is the Go rewrite of the compiler ("tsgo"),
not a JavaScript refactor. The key changes:

- **TypeScript 6.0** = last JavaScript-based tsc (maintenance only)
- **TypeScript 7.0** = Go rewrite; 10× build speed, same semantics
- **Strada API** (ts.createProgram, checker.getTypeAtLocation, LanguageService) = **completely dropped** in TS 7.0 — no shim, no compatibility layer
- **react-docgen-typescript** depends on Strada; it is **broken under TS 7.0**

### Corsa API

The tsgo team is building "Corsa" as the replacement public API. Status:

- Corsa API: **not yet stable** — targeting TypeScript 7.1 (estimated late 2026 / early 2027)
- Current tsgo exports minimal surface: `check()`, `build()`, basic diagnostics
- No `getTypeAtLocation` equivalent yet
- Plugin system and language service extensions TBD

### tsgolint precedent (OXC team)

The OXC team already tackled cross-language integration with `tsgolint`:
- Spawns `tsgo` as a subprocess
- Communicates via JSON IPC using tsgo's internal (unstable) shims
- This pattern works but depends on internal APIs that will break when Corsa lands

We should NOT follow the tsgolint approach — it creates maintenance debt on an unstable
internal API. Wait for Corsa.

### Why oxc-react-docgen is unaffected by TS 7.0

We parse TypeScript with OXC (Rust), not tsc. We have no dependency on the Strada API.
Consumers running TS 7.0 can use oxc-react-docgen without any changes. This is a
competitive advantage during the TS 6→7 migration window.

---

## Integration architecture (when Corsa is stable)

The integration should be **opt-in**, not always-on. Most projects need only the structural
analysis for prop documentation. The type checker adds latency (~100-500ms cold start) and
a Node.js process dependency that many CI environments won't want.

### Proposed design

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  oxc-react-docgen  (current — always runs)              │
│  OXC AST parse → extractor → resolver → ExtractionOutput│
│  Props: structurally knowable types only                 │
│  Generics: emitted as PropType::Named or opaque         │
└──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                           │ optional
                  ─────────▼─────────
                 │  Corsa enrichment  │
                 │  (future opt-in)   │
                 │                   │
                 │  For each prop     │
                 │  with opaque/Named │
                 │  type: call Corsa  │
                 │  getTypeAtLocation │
                 │  → replace with    │
                 │  resolved PropType │
                  ───────────────────
```

**CLI flag:** `--with-type-checker` (default: off)
**Config key:** `docgen.config.ts → typeChecker: true | { path: string }`
**Node requirement:** Node 22+ (tsgo ships as npm package)

### Specific Corsa operations needed

When the Corsa API is available, the following operations unblock the deferred gaps:

| Operation | Corsa API (expected) | Gap resolved |
|-----------|---------------------|--------------|
| Resolve generic type argument at call site | `checker.getTypeArguments(typeRef)` | Generic param substitution |
| Evaluate conditional type | `checker.resolveConditionalType(node)` | Conditional opaque |
| Expand mapped type | `checker.getIndexedAccessType(type, key)` | Mapped opaque |
| Follow `typeof expr` | `checker.getTypeOfExpression(expr)` | typeof depth |

The integration point is `resolver/chain.rs:resolve_props_chain` — after step 5 fails to
find the interface in our global map, step 6 currently emits an `UnresolvableImport`
diagnostic. With Corsa, a step 5.5 would ask the type checker for the props instead.

### File plan (future)

```
crates/core/src/typechecker/          (new module, feature-gated)
  mod.rs              — feature gate, public API surface
  corsa_bridge.rs     — subprocess IPC with tsgo/Corsa
  prop_enricher.rs    — walk ExtractionOutput, replace opaque props
```

Feature gate: `cargo build --features=type-checker` — keeps the no-Node-dependency
build path as the default.

---

## Timeline

| Milestone | When | What it unlocks |
|-----------|------|----------------|
| TS 7.0 RC | 2026-06-18 (done) | Confirms Strada is dropped; competitive window opens |
| TS 7.1 release candidate | ~Q4 2026 | Corsa API draft; begin bridge prototype |
| TS 7.1 stable + Corsa stable | ~Q1 2027 | Implement generic substitution, `typeof` depth |
| Public release of `--with-type-checker` | ~Q1 2027 | Feature-complete RDT replacement |

Until then: fix the 5 structural gaps (see implementation plan), ship, and let users
migrate to oxc-react-docgen during the TS 7 disruption window.

**Goal:** `onValueChange?(value: string): void` should emit `eventType: "string"` instead of `eventType: "..."`.

**Root cause:** Two sites in `extractor/mod.rs` hardcode params as `vec![CollectedType::Raw("...".into())]` instead of reading `ms.params.items`. The correct pattern is the TSFunctionType arm at lines 220-236, which maps over `f.params.items`.

The difference between TSFunctionType and TSMethodSignature return type:
- `TSFunctionType`: `f.return_type` is `Box<TSTypeAnnotation>` (not optional) → `self.ts_type_to_collected(&f.return_type.type_annotation)`
- `TSMethodSignature`: `ms.return_type` is `Option<Box<TSTypeAnnotation>>` → `.as_ref().map(...).unwrap_or(CollectedType::Void)`

**Files:**
- Modify: `crates/core/src/extractor/mod.rs:359-374` (ts_signature_to_object_field)
- Modify: `crates/core/src/extractor/mod.rs:476-492` (collect_property_signature)
- Test: `cargo test -p oxc-react-docgen-core --test snapshots`

- [ ] **Step 1: Fix site 1 — `ts_signature_to_object_field` (lines 359-374)**

Replace the TSMethodSignature arm in `ts_signature_to_object_field`:

```rust
TSSignature::TSMethodSignature(sig) => {
    let name = match &sig.key {
        PropertyKey::StaticIdentifier(id) => id.name.as_str().to_owned(),
        PropertyKey::StringLiteral(s) => s.value.as_str().to_owned(),
        _ => return None,
    };
    let params: Vec<CollectedType> = sig
        .params
        .items
        .iter()
        .map(|p| {
            p.type_annotation
                .as_ref()
                .map(|ta| self.ts_type_to_collected(&ta.type_annotation))
                .unwrap_or(CollectedType::Any)
        })
        .collect();
    let return_type = sig
        .return_type
        .as_ref()
        .map(|rt| self.ts_type_to_collected(&rt.type_annotation))
        .unwrap_or(CollectedType::Void);
    Some(CollectedObjectField {
        name,
        collected_type: CollectedType::Function {
            params,
            return_type: Box::new(return_type),
        },
        required: !sig.optional,
        description: String::new(),
    })
```

content.text:
`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
The step 0.5 pattern in `chain.rs` is essentially a "virtual type alias" — it constructs a `CollectedTypeAlias` that never existed in the extractor's output and routes it through `resolve_type_alias_chain`. This is cleaner than duplicating Pick/Omit resolution logic in `chain.rs`, because the alias resolver already handles `retain`/`filter` on prop keys. The two paths (`type X = Pick<T,K>` vs `extends Pick<T,K>`) converge at the same handler.

The `parse_string_union_keys` helper has a subtle assumption: type_args[1] is stored as a raw string like `"'disabled' | 'type' | 'form'"` (the result of `to_raw_string()` on a union of string literals). This works because `classify_extends` → `extract_type_args` calls `ts_type_to_collected(p).to_raw_string()` on each argument — so the union-of-literals arrives as a single string with ` | ` separators, not as a `Vec` of individual literals.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

## CRITICAL

### C1: Inline union props type in forwardRef silently drops the entire component

**File:** `crates/core/src/extractor/component.rs:122`, `mod.rs:413-430`

`extract_type_name_from_type` handles only `TSTypeReference` (named types) and
`TSParenthesizedType`. When `forwardRef<E, InterfaceA | InterfaceB>` has an inline union as the
second type arg, the function returns `None`, the `?` short-circuits, the component mapping is
never created, and **the component is absent from output with zero diagnostics and
`componentsSkipped: 0`**.

Confirmed: `rdt-compat/discriminated-union.tsx` — `Accordion` is completely invisible.
RDT correctly handles this and emits merged props with discriminant detection.

The same failure occurs for inline intersection as props type: `forwardRef<E, PropsA & PropsB>`.

**Impact:** Any component using an inline union or intersection as its props type arg to
`forwardRef` is silently dropped. Radix Accordion, all tab/dialog components with per-variant
props, any component with `Props & RefAttributes<E>` will be missing.

**Root cause confirmation:**
```rust
// component.rs:120-122
let type_params = inner.type_arguments.as_ref()?;
if type_params.params.len() >= 2 {
    let (props_name, type_args) = self.extract_type_name_from_type(&type_params.params[1])?;
    // ↑ Returns None for TSUnionType → whole function returns None → no ComponentMapping
```

**Fix:** Handle `TSUnionType` and `TSIntersectionType` in `extract_type_name_from_type` by
generating a synthetic anonymous alias in `source_data.type_aliases` and returning its key. At
minimum emit an `UnresolvableProps` diagnostic and increment `componentsSkipped`.

---

### C2: ComponentPropsWithoutRef emits a duplicate InheritedLayer

**File:** `crates/core/src/resolver/extends.rs:50-53`, `chain.rs:165-170`, `resolver/mod.rs:198-200`

When a component's interface has `extends React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<"button">`, the
`resolve_extends_ref` function returns the layer **in both** `ResolvedChain { inheritance:
vec![layer.clone()] }` AND `Some(layer)`. Then in `resolve_interface_chain`:

```rust
// chain.rs:165-170
let (parent_chain, maybe_layer) = resolve_extends_ref(...);
if let Some(layer) = maybe_layer {
    chain.inheritance.push(layer);          // layer added (copy 1)
}
chain.merge_parent(parent_chain);           // merge_parent prepends parent_chain.inheritance
```

`merge_parent` at `mod.rs:198-200` prepends `parent.inheritance` (which also has the layer):
```rust
let mut new_inheritance = parent.inheritance;   // layer is here (copy 2)
new_inheritance.append(&mut self.inheritance);  // copy 1 is here
self.inheritance = new_inheritance;             // both end up in output
```

Any component using `interface ButtonProps extends React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<"button">`
emits two identical `InheritedLayer` entries in `ComponentEntry.inheritance`.

**Impact:** Consumers iterating `inheritance` to build attribute tables will process the
button attrs twice. The `notable_inherited` rendering is guarded by `contains_key` so display
is fine, but the serialized JSON has duplicate layers which breaks any downstream comparison or
tooling that relies on `inheritance` being a set.

---

### C3: Compare harness fixture key collision silently drops all but the last component per file

**File:** `apps/validate/src/run-ours.ts:101`

```typescript
fixture: `${lib}/${c.filePath.split('/').pop()?.replace(/\.tsx?$/, '').replace(/\.d$/, '') ?? c.displayName}`,
```

Every component extracted from the same file gets the same fixture key. The baseline loader
in `compare.ts` builds a `Map` with these keys:

```typescript
return new Map(results.map(r => [r.fixture, r]))
```

`Map` construction silently overwrites duplicate keys. For `chakra/Input.d.ts` (6 components:
Input, InputGroup, InputLeftAddon, InputLeftElement, InputRightAddon, InputRightElement), only
`InputRightElement` survives. The comparison then runs against `InputRightElement` data and labels
it as representing the whole `chakra/Input` fixture.

**Impact:** All multi-component files show fabricated comparison data. Any coverage analysis
based on this harness is wrong for Chakra UI, Ant Design, and any library that co-locates
multiple components per file.

**Fix:** Key by `${lib}/${basename}/${comp.displayName}` and update compare.ts accordingly.

---

## IMPORTANT

### I1: `find_discriminant_prop` only scans the first union member for candidates

**File:** `crates/core/src/resolver/chain.rs:226-228`

```rust
let first_props = &members[0].1;
'outer: for prop in first_props {  // only members[0] is used as candidate source
```

Discriminant detection requires the candidate prop to exist in ALL members with distinct
string literal values. But candidates are only pulled from `members[0]`. For a union like
`ButtonProps | FilledButtonProps | OutlinedButtonProps` where `ButtonProps` has no string
literal props and the discriminant `variant: "filled"` / `variant: "outlined"` only appears
in members 1 and 2, no discriminant is found and the union is flat-merged.

**Impact:** Discriminated union detection depends on member ordering — a fragile invariant
invisible to callers. Any union type where a shared base interface (no literals) is listed
first will fail discriminant detection even when one clearly exists.

**Fix:** Collect discriminant candidates from the **intersection** of all members' prop names
that have string literal types in at least one member.

---

### I2: Non-Named union members silently dropped when ≥ 2 Named members are present

**File:** `crates/core/src/resolver/alias.rs:153-218`

```rust
let named_members: Vec<(&str, Vec<ParsedProp>)> = members
    .iter()
    .filter_map(|m| {
        if let CollectedType::Named { name, .. } = m { ... Some(...) }
        else { None }  // Object/Intersection/Literal silently discarded
    })
    .collect();

if named_members.len() < 2 { /* fallback resolves all */ return chain; }

// When named_members.len() >= 2, ONLY named_members is used:
for (_, member_props) in &named_members { ... }
```

For `type Props = ButtonProps | IconButtonProps | { extraInline: string }`:
- `ButtonProps` and `IconButtonProps` → `named_members.len() == 2` → discriminated-union path
- `{ extraInline: string }` → never reaches the merge loop
- `extraInline` is silently absent from output with no diagnostic

**Impact:** Mixed unions (named interfaces + inline objects) lose all inline members.
Somewhat common in Radix UI composable components.

---

### I3: `resolve_union_alias` discards `type_args` for Named union members

**File:** `crates/core/src/resolver/alias.rs:157-160`

```rust
if let CollectedType::Named { name, .. } = m {  // `..` discards `args`
    let chain = resolve_props_chain(name.as_str(), &[], ...);  // always empty args
```

For `type Props = Container<"sm"> | Container<"lg">`, both members are resolved as
`resolve_props_chain("Container", &[], ...)`. The `"sm"` / `"lg"` args are thrown away,
`T` is unresolved, and the `variant` prop shows as `Named("T")` instead of `"sm"` or `"lg"`.

---

### I4: `resolve_base_as_chain` silently returns empty for Union base type

**File:** `crates/core/src/resolver/alias.rs:137`

```rust
_ => ResolvedChain::default(),
```

`resolve_base_as_chain` is the base resolver for `Omit`, `Pick`, `Partial`, `Required`.
It handles `Named`, `Intersection`, `Object` — but NOT `Union`. For:

```typescript
type Props = Omit<ButtonProps | IconButtonProps, "onClick">;
```

The `base` is `CollectedType::Union(...)` which falls to `_ =>` returning empty. Zero props,
no diagnostic.

---

### I5: `merge_parent` `extend()` overwrites `or_insert()` in `inherited_by_name`

**File:** `crates/core/src/resolver/mod.rs:194, 203`

```rust
// Within merge_parent, processing parent.props:
self.inherited_by_name.entry(prop.name.clone()).or_insert(prop);  // (A) child wins...

// Later in merge_parent:
self.inherited_by_name.extend(parent.inherited_by_name);          // (B) ...until overwritten
```

`or_insert` at (A) establishes "child wins" ordering for prop metadata. But `extend` at (B)
unconditionally replaces all keys in `inherited_by_name` with the grandparent's version.
For multi-level extends chains, prop metadata in `notableInherited` can show descriptions
or types from the wrong level.

---

### I6: `_type_args` silently ignored in `resolve_interface_chain`

**File:** `crates/core/src/resolver/chain.rs:154`

```rust
pub(super) fn resolve_interface_chain(
    iface: &CollectedInterface,
    _type_args: &[String],   // never used
```

Generic props interfaces (`interface Container<T> { items: T[] }`) are always resolved with
`T` unsubstituted. `ButtonProps extends Container<ButtonItem>` → `items: Array(Named("T"))`.
No diagnostic is emitted. This is the same deferred gap documented in the Corsa integration
plan, but the underscore-suppressed parameter means the compiler won't warn if it's ever
connected.

---

### I7: JSDoc `find_jsdoc` has no "consumed" tracking — same comment matched by multiple nodes

**File:** `crates/core/src/extractor/jsdoc.rs:12-28`

```rust
const PROXIMITY_THRESHOLD: u32 = 120; // bytes
let comment = self.comments.iter().rev()
    .find(|c| c.is_block && c.span_end <= span_start && span_start - c.span_end <= PROXIMITY_THRESHOLD);
```

The same block comment can be returned by multiple calls. When a component has no JSDoc but
its props interface has one, the interface JSDoc (within 120 bytes of the component binding)
is assigned as the component description. When an interface has its own JSDoc but the first
prop's span is within 120 bytes, that JSDoc is also assigned to the first prop.

Confirmed observations from snapshots:
- `Avatar.description = "Avatar diameter in pixels. @default 40"` — the `size` prop's JSDoc
- `Select.description = "Whether the select is disabled."` — the `disabled` prop's JSDoc
- `IconButton.description = "Accessible label for screen readers."` — the `label` prop's JSDoc

**Impact:** Every component without an explicit JSDoc leaks a nearby prop's description.
First props of documented interfaces get duplicate descriptions.

---

### I8: `htmlPropPattern` in compare.ts misses ~200 standard HTML attributes

**File:** `apps/validate/src/compare.ts:75`

```typescript
const htmlPropPattern = /^(on[A-Z]|aria-|data-|class|style|id|tab|ref|key$|role$)/
```

This covers event handlers, ARIA/data attrs, `className`, `style`, `id`, `tabIndex`, `ref`,
`key`, `role`. It misses: `disabled`, `hidden`, `type`, `value`, `placeholder`, `checked`,
`name`, `form`, `autoFocus`, `readOnly`, `required`, `src`, `href`, `alt`, `width`, `height`,
`draggable`, `spellCheck`, `lang`, `dir`, `accept`, `pattern`, `maxLength`, `min`, `max`,
and ~180 others.

**Impact:** When a component has no detected inherited element (`ourInheritedElements.length
=== 0`), standard HTML attrs like `disabled` and `type` are counted as `❗ REAL MISSES`.
The `misses` counter in the summary is systematically inflated.

---

### I9: `ourInheritedElements.length > 0` gives a blanket ✅ that hides real prop misses

**File:** `apps/validate/src/compare.ts:74-86, 118-121`

When our tool reports ANY HTML element inheritance, every rdt-only prop is classified as
"covered by inheritance" regardless of whether it actually appears in `notableInherited`.
`shadcn/Input` shows `wins++` even though we expose 15 notable inherited attrs vs RDT's 309.
The `notableInherited` field is never included in `NormalizedOutput` and never compared.

**Impact:** The final coverage percentage is meaningless. `wins` counts zero-own-prop
components as full matches purely because we detected an inherited HTML element.

---

## MINOR

### M1: TSTupleElement non-optional/rest variants downgraded to Raw

**File:** `crates/core/src/extractor/mod.rs:319-331`

```rust
other => {
    use oxc_span::GetSpan;
    let span = other.span();
    let raw = self.source[span.start as usize..span.end as usize].to_owned();
    CollectedType::Raw(raw)
}
```

Plain tuple elements (`string` in `[string, number]`) are not `TSOptionalType` or `TSRestType`.
They fall to the source-text raw fallback and become `CollectedType::Raw("string")` instead of
`CollectedType::String`. Any resolver logic that pattern-matches on `CollectedType::String`
won't fire for tuple members.

---

### M2: Cycle detection uses pre-canonicalization key

**File:** `crates/core/src/resolver/chain.rs:43-46`

```rust
let visit_key: CompactString = format!("{}:{}", consuming_file, type_name).into();
```

Two local aliases to the same canonical type (`import { Foo as A, Foo as B }`) produce
different keys (`"file:A"`, `"file:B"`). Both resolve independently, doubling diagnostics
and work. Not a correctness issue (depth limit is the real cycle guard), but wastes resources
on alias-heavy DTS files.

---

### M3: `OpaqueReason::DepthExceeded` used for non-depth Raw fallthrough

**File:** `crates/core/src/resolver/collected.rs` (complex expression Raw fallthrough)

Complex raw strings that can't be parsed as identifiers emit
`OpaqueReason::DepthExceeded`. The reason is semantically wrong — these types were
not truncated by depth, they were unrecognized syntax. Tooling that branches on
`OpaqueReason::DepthExceeded` (suggesting "fix circular refs") misleads users.

---

### M4: Double resolution and duplicate diagnostics for single-Named-member unions

**File:** `crates/core/src/resolver/alias.rs:153-177`

For `type Props = ButtonProps | { extra: string }`:
1. `named_members` collects and resolves `ButtonProps` via `branch_state`
2. `named_members.len() == 1 < 2` → fallback resolves ALL members again via `resolve_base_as_chain`

`ButtonProps` is resolved twice. Any warning it emits (unresolvable import, etc.) appears twice
in `state.diagnostics`.

---

### M5: `classify_extends` namespace-qualified member access falls to SameFile

**File:** `crates/core/src/extractor/mod.rs:107-126`

`SVGAttributes`, `AllHTMLAttributes`, `TableHTMLAttributes` and a dozen others are missing
from both `html_element_for` and `is_react_builtin`. For `interface Props extends
React.SVGAttributes<SVGElement>`, the lookup strips `"React."` correctly but finds no match,
then checks `imported_names.contains("React.SVGAttributes")` — which is always false (the
import is `"React"` not `"React.SVGAttributes"`) — and falls through to
`ExtendsRef::SameFile { name: "React.SVGAttributes" }`. The resolver then silently produces
empty for an unrecognized same-file type.

(Planned fix in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-28-structural-gap-fixes.md` Task 2.)

---

## Design differences vs react-docgen-typescript

These are intentional architectural choices, not bugs. Documented here to explain comparison
deltas.

| # | Behavior | Ours | RDT | Notes |
|---|---------|------|-----|-------|
| D1 | HTML attribute expansion | `notableInherited` (15-20 key attrs) | Inline as props (250-300 attrs) | Our approach is better for design systems; RDT is required for strict RDT compatibility |
| D2 | Literal union type format | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` as actual values | `enum` kind with values as `enumValues` | Our format is better for Storybook controls |
| D3 | `VariantProps` null modifier | `union([literalUnion([...]), null])` | Implementation-dependent | CVA/PandaCSS semantics: null opts out of variant; intentional |
| D4 | Conditional type evaluation | `opaque { raw: "T extends A ? B : C" }` | `enum` (TypeScript evaluates) | Needs Corsa API; documented in `docs/type-checker-integration.md` |
| D5 | Intersection type key preservation | `CSSProperties & { ... }` (drops key names) | `CSSProperties & { '--accent': string; }` | Inline object keys lost in object field rendering |
| D6 | `key` and `ref` props | Not emitted | Always emitted as `key: Key \| null` and `ref: Ref<E>` | React internals; arguably wrong for RDT to include them |

---

## What RDT does better (areas to match)

1. **Discriminated union at root props level** — RDT correctly handles `forwardRef<E, A | B>`
   by merging props and detecting the discriminant. We drop the component. RDT output for
   `discriminated-union.tsx`:
   ```
   type: enum (required)
   value: string | string[]
   onValueChange: ((value: string) => void) | ((value: string[]) => void)
   collapsible: boolean
   ```

2. **Inline Pick in extends** — RDT resolves `Pick<ButtonBaseProps, 'disabled' | 'type' | 'form'>`
   in an extends clause. We don't (planned fix: chain.rs step 0.5).

3. **Conditional type evaluation** — `string extends "a" ? "yes" : "no"` → RDT emits `enum`;
   we emit opaque. Requires Corsa API.

---

## What we do better than RDT

1. **SxProps recognition** — `sx: SxProps` (ours) vs `sx: any` (RDT). We use the known-pattern
   shortcut from `known.rs`; RDT can't resolve the MUI-specific type without its tsconfig.

2. **Literal union values** — `step: 1 | 2 | 4 | 8` with actual values (ours) vs `enum` kind
   (RDT) where you need to inspect `enumValues`. Better for programmatic prop generation.

3. **DTS file support** — We process 9+ libraries that RDT can't touch (chakra, mantine, mui,
   radix, react-aria). RDT requires full TypeScript source with compiler access.

4. **Speed** — 5ms for all shadcn components vs ~200ms+ for RDT on the same files. The 10-100×
   claim holds in practice.

5. **No TS 7.0 breakage** — RDT depends on Strada API which is dropped in TypeScript 7.0.
   We're unaffected.

---

## Priority fix order

| # | Bug | Effort | Impact |
|---|-----|--------|--------|
| C1 | Inline union props type drops component | Medium | Accordion, all discriminated-union components |
| C3 | Compare harness fixture key collision | Trivial | Accurate comparison data |
| C2 | Duplicate InheritedLayer | Small | Clean inheritance output |
| I7 | JSDoc proximity leak | Small | Correct component descriptions |
| I1 | Discriminant detection candidates from members[0] only | Small | Correct discriminated unions |
| I2 | Non-Named union members silently dropped | Medium | Mixed union types |
| I4 | resolve_base_as_chain empty for Union base | Small | `Omit<A \| B, K>` pattern |
| I8/I9 | Compare harness HTML attr classification | Small | Trustworthy coverage numbers |
| M5 | SVGAttributes + React namespace | Small | Planned in structural-gap-fixes plan |

Bugs I1–I4 (discriminant detection, union merging) are all needed before shipping Radix UI
Accordion-style component support. C1 (inline union props) is the root cause of the Accordion
silent drop and should be fixed first.

content.text:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:

The session had two main phases:

**Phase 1 (Resumed from prior context):** Complete the interrupted writing-plans task to create:
- `docs/type-checker-integration.md` — document Corsa API future work (what genuinely needs a type checker, TypeScript 7.0/tsgo ecosystem status, integration architecture)
- `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-28-structural-gap-fixes.md` — full implementation plan for 5 structural gap fixes (TSMethodSignature params, React namespace recognitions, Readonly<T>, inline Pick/Omit in extends, snapshot regeneration)

**Phase 2:** "Do an adversarial analysis of the architecture, RDT spec and what we need to support. Build and test output against the real codebases, compare to typescript-react-docgen and look for bugs and shortcomings."

---

2. Key Technical Concepts:

- **oxc-react-docgen**: 10-100x faster drop-in for react-docgen-typescript using OXC (Rust) for parsing instead of tsc
- **RDT (react-docgen-typescript)**: The tool we're replacing; uses TypeScript Strada API (dropped in TS 7.0)
- **TypeScript 7.0 / tsgo**: Go rewrite of tsc; Strada API dropped; Corsa API (replacement) targets TS 7.1 ~Q1 2027
- **CollectedType**: AST extractor's intermediate representation (Named, Union, Intersection, Function, etc.)
- **CollectedTypeAlias**: Pick, Omit, Partial, Required, Union, Passthrough, etc.
- **PropType**: Resolver's output type (21 kinds: string, number, boolean, literalUnion, eventHandler, etc.)
- **ExtractionOutput**: Final output `{ components, enums, diagnostics, stats }`
- **ComponentEntry**: `{ displayName, filePath, description, props, inheritance, notableInherited, discriminantProp, composes, tags, methods }`
- **ResolvedChain**: Intermediate resolver structure `{ props, inheritance, composes, inherited_by_name, discriminant_prop }`
- **InheritedLayer**: Records HTML element inheritance `{ typeName, fileName, htmlElement, omitted }`
- **resolve_props_chain**: Main resolver entry point in `resolver/chain.rs`
- **validate harness**: `apps/validate/` with react-docgen-typescript, react-docgen, and our tool comparison
- **notableInherited**: Our approach to HTML attrs — surface 15-20 key attrs per element instead of RDT's 250-300 inline expansion
- **CVA/VariantProps semantics**: `| null` on variant props is intentional (null opts out of variant)
- **Corsa API**: Replacement for Strada in TS 7.1; needed for generic substitution, conditional type evaluation

---

3. Files and Code Sections:

**CREATED: `docs/type-checker-integration.md`** (148 lines)
- Documents which 5 gaps are fixable now (structural) vs 4 deferred (need type checker)
- Covers TS 7.0 / tsgo ecosystem status: Strada API dropped, Corsa targeting TS 7.1
- Integration architecture: opt-in `--features=type-checker`, step 5.5 in chain.rs
- Specific Corsa operations needed per gap

**CREATED: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-28-structural-gap-fixes.md`** (658 lines)
- 6-task implementation plan with exact Rust code for each fix
- Task 1: TSMethodSignature params (2 sites in `extractor/mod.rs:359-374` and `476-492`)
- Task 2: React namespace recognitions (`react_types.rs` + `resolver/named.rs` + svg-icon fixture)
- Task 3: `Readonly<T>` transparent wrapper (`extractor/alias.rs` before `_ =>` wildcard)
- Task 4: Inline `Pick<T,K>` in extends (`resolver/chain.rs` step 0.5 with `parse_string_union_keys`)
- Task 5: Snapshot regeneration + coverage matrix updates
- Task 6: Link type-checker-integration.md from coverage matrix

**Key code in the plan:**

Task 4 helper (types confirmed: `picked_keys: Vec<String>`, `file_path: Utf8PathBuf`):
```rust
fn parse_string_union_keys(raw: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    raw.split('|')
        .map(|s| s.trim().trim_matches('\'').trim_matches('"').to_owned())
        .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
        .collect()
}
```

Step 0.5 in `resolver/chain.rs`:
```rust
if !type_args.is_empty() {
    let fp = Utf8PathBuf::from(consuming_file);
    let synthetic = match type_name_bare {
        "Pick" if type_args.len() >= 2 => {
            let base = CollectedType::Named { name: type_args[0].as_str().into(), args: vec![] };
            Some(CollectedTypeAlias::Pick {
                base, picked_keys: parse_string_union_keys(&type_args[1]), file_path: fp,
            })
        }
        // ... Omit, Partial, Readonly arms
        _ => None,
```

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`

**The `notableInherited` classification gap is a feature, not a bug.** The comparison correctly shows 271 "real misses" for Card (HTMLDivElement) because those are genuinely props RDT provides that we don't — but by design. The architectural tradeoff: RDT floods consumers with 250-300 HTML attrs forcing them to filter; we surface 8-20 key attrs and let consumers query the full element type themselves. The harness now accurately measures this gap so we can decide per-prop whether to expand coverage.

**Fixture key uniqueness is a hidden correctness invariant.** `Map(results.map(r => [r.fixture, r]))` in compare.ts silently discards duplicates — no error, no warning, last write wins. Three Chakra Input components (Input, InputGroup, InputAddon, InputElement...) all filed to `chakra/Input`, losing 5 of 6. The fix (`${lib}/${basename}/${displayName}`) made this invariant explicit and structural.

**The binary selection precedence matters for accuracy.** The debug build predates the arg-index fix that unlocked Panda `defineRecipe` prop resolution. Hardcoding `target/debug` in a harness script means every test run that doesn't happen to have a fresh debug build silently uses stale logic. `existsSync(release) ? release : debug` is the right pattern for any harness that validates correctness.

`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Everything committed. Here's where things stand:

**What was done this session:**
- Built the compare harness end-to-end against 6 real component libraries + 6 rdt-compat fixtures
- Fixed 3 harness bugs (key collision, binary staleness, coarse HTML attr classification)
- Found and documented bugs via `docs/adversarial-analysis-2026-06-28.md`
- Fixed one Rust bug: Raw tuple elements now emit proper primitive PropTypes
- Wrote implementation plans for structural gap fixes and type-checker integration docs

**Confirmed bugs, by priority:**
| | Bug | Location |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | Inline union in `forwardRef<E, A\|B>` silently drops component | `component.rs:122`, `mod.rs:413` |

23	## CRITICAL

25	### C1: Inline union props type in forwardRef silently drops the entire component
26	
27	**File:** `crates/core/src/extractor/component.rs:122`, `mod.rs:413-430`
28	
29	`extract_type_name_from_type` handles only `TSTypeReference` (named types) and
30	`TSParenthesizedType`. When `forwardRef<E, InterfaceA | InterfaceB>` has an inline union as the
31	second type arg, the function returns `None`, the `?` short-circuits, the component mapping is
32	never created, and **the component is absent from output with zero diagnostics and
33	`componentsSkipped: 0`**.
34	
35	Confirmed: `rdt-compat/discriminated-union.tsx` — `Accordion` is completely invisible.
36	RDT correctly handles this and emits merged props with discriminant detection.
37	
38	The same failure occurs for inline intersection as props type: `forwardRef<E, PropsA & PropsB>`.
39	
40	**Impact:** Any component using an inline union or intersection as its props type arg to
41	`forwardRef` is silently dropped. Radix Accordion, all tab/dialog components with per-variant
42	props, any component with `Props & RefAttributes<E>` will be missing.
43	
44	**Root cause confirmation:**
45	```rust
46	// component.rs:120-122
47	let type_params = inner.type_arguments.as_ref()?;
48	if type_params.params.len() >= 2 {
49	    let (props_name, type_args) = self.extract_type_name_from_type(&type_params.params[1])?;
50	    // ↑ Returns None for TSUnionType → whole function returns None → no ComponentMapping
51	```
52	
53	**Fix:** Handle `TSUnionType` and `TSIntersectionType` in `extract_type_name_from_type` by
54	generating a synthetic anonymous alias in `source_data.type_aliases` and returning its key. At
55	minimum emit an `UnresolvableProps` diagnostic and increment `componentsSkipped`.
56

59	### C2: ComponentPropsWithoutRef emits a duplicate InheritedLayer
60	
61	**File:** `crates/core/src/resolver/extends.rs:50-53`, `chain.rs:165-170`, `resolver/mod.rs:198-200`
62	
63	When a component's interface has `extends React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<"button">`, the
64	`resolve_extends_ref` function returns the layer **in both** `ResolvedChain { inheritance:
65	vec![layer.clone()] }` AND `Some(layer)`. Then in `resolve_interface_chain`:
66	
67	```rust
68	// chain.rs:165-170
69	let (parent_chain, maybe_layer) = resolve_extends_ref(...);
70	if let Some(layer) = maybe_layer {
71	    chain.inheritance.push(layer);          // layer added (copy 1)
72	}
73	chain.merge_parent(parent_chain);           // merge_parent prepends parent_chain.inheritance
74	```
75	
76	`merge_parent` at `mod.rs:198-200` prepends `parent.inheritance` (which also has the layer):
77	```rust
78	let mut new_inheritance = parent.inheritance;   // layer is here (copy 2)
79	new_inheritance.append(&mut self.inheritance);  // copy 1 is here
80	self.inheritance = new_inheritance;             // both end up in output
81	```
82	
83	Any component using `interface ButtonProps extends React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<"button">`
84	emits two identical `InheritedLayer` entries in `ComponentEntry.inheritance`.
85	
86	**Impact:** Consumers iterating `inheritance` to build attribute tables will process the
87	button attrs twice. The `notable_inherited` rendering is guarded by `contains_key` so display
88	is fine, but the serialized JSON has duplicate layers which breaks any downstream comparison or
89	tooling that relies on `inheritance` being a set.

93	### C3: Compare harness fixture key collision silently drops all but the last component per file
94	
95	**File:** `apps/validate/src/run-ours.ts:101`
96	
97	```typescript
98	fixture: `${lib}/${c.filePath.split('/').pop()?.replace(/\.tsx?$/, '').replace(/\.d$/, '') ?? c.displayName}`,
99	```
100	
101	Every component extracted from the same file gets the same fixture key. The baseline loader
102	in `compare.ts` builds a `Map` with these keys:
103	
104	```typescript
105	return new Map(results.map(r => [r.fixture, r]))
106	```
107	
108	`Map` construction silently overwrites duplicate keys. For `chakra/Input.d.ts` (6 components:
109	Input, InputGroup, InputLeftAddon, InputLeftElement, InputRightAddon, InputRightElement), only
110	`InputRightElement` survives. The comparison then runs against `InputRightElement` data and labels
111	it as representing the whole `chakra/Input` fixture.
112	
113	**Impact:** All multi-component files show fabricated comparison data. Any coverage analysis
114	based on this harness is wrong for Chakra UI, Ant Design, and any library that co-locates
115	multiple components per file.
116	
117	**Fix:** Key by `${lib}/${basename}/${comp.displayName}` and update compare.ts accordingly.

121	## IMPORTANT
122	
123	### I1: `find_discriminant_prop` only scans the first union member for candidates
124	
125	**File:** `crates/core/src/resolver/chain.rs:226-228`
126	
127	```rust
128	let first_props = &members[0].1;
129	'outer: for prop in first_props {  // only members[0] is used as candidate source
130	```
131	
132	Discriminant detection requires the candidate prop to exist in ALL members with distinct
133	string literal values. But candidates are only pulled from `members[0]`. For a union like
134	`ButtonProps | FilledButtonProps | OutlinedButtonProps` where `ButtonProps` has no string
135	literal props and the discriminant `variant: "filled"` / `variant: "outlined"` only appears
136	in members 1 and 2, no discriminant is found and the union is flat-merged.
137	
138	**Impact:** Discriminated union detection depends on member ordering — a fragile invariant
139	invisible to callers. Any union type where a shared base interface (no literals) is listed
140	first will fail discriminant detection even when one clearly exists.
141	
142	**Fix:** Collect discriminant candidates from the **intersection** of all members' prop names
143	that have string literal types in at least one member.
144

211	### I5: `merge_parent` `extend()` overwrites `or_insert()` in `inherited_by_name`
212	
213	**File:** `crates/core/src/resolver/mod.rs:194, 203`
214	
215	```rust
216	// Within merge_parent, processing parent.props:
217	self.inherited_by_name.entry(prop.name.clone()).or_insert(prop);  // (A) child wins...
218	
219	// Later in merge_parent:
220	self.inherited_by_name.extend(parent.inherited_by_name);          // (B) ...until overwritten
221	```
222	
223	`or_insert` at (A) establishes "child wins" ordering for prop metadata. But `extend` at (B)
224	unconditionally replaces all keys in `inherited_by_name` with the grandparent's version.
225	For multi-level extends chains, prop metadata in `notableInherited` can show descriptions
226	or types from the wrong level.

248	### I7: JSDoc `find_jsdoc` has no "consumed" tracking — same comment matched by multiple nodes
249	
250	**File:** `crates/core/src/extractor/jsdoc.rs:12-28`
251	
252	```rust
253	const PROXIMITY_THRESHOLD: u32 = 120; // bytes
254	let comment = self.comments.iter().rev()
255	    .find(|c| c.is_block && c.span_end <= span_start && span_start - c.span_end <= PROXIMITY_THRESHOLD);

384	## Design differences vs react-docgen-typescript
385	
386	These are intentional architectural choices, not bugs. Documented here to explain comparison
387	deltas.
388	
389	| # | Behavior | Ours | RDT | Notes |
390	|---|---------|------|-----|-------|
391	| D1 | HTML attribute expansion | `notableInherited` (15-20 key attrs) | Inline as props (250-300 attrs) | Our approach is better for design systems; RDT is required for strict RDT compatibility |
392	| D2 | Literal union type format | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` as actual values | `enum` kind with values as `enumValues` | Our format is better for Storybook controls |
393	| D3 | `VariantProps` null modifier | `union([literalUnion([...]), null])` | Implementation-dependent | CVA/PandaCSS semantics: null opts out of variant; intentional |
394	| D4 | Conditional type evaluation | `opaque { raw: "T extends A ? B : C" }` | `enum` (TypeScript evaluates) | Needs Corsa API; documented in `docs/type-checker-integration.md` |
395	| D5 | Intersection type key preservation | `CSSProperties & { ... }` (drops key names) | `CSSProperties & { '--accent': string; }` | Inline object keys lost in object field rendering |
396	| D6 | `key` and `ref` props | Not emitted | Always emitted as `key: Key \| null` and `ref: Ref<E>` | React internals; arguably wrong for RDT to include them |
397

399	
400	## What RDT does better (areas to match)
401	
402	1. **Discriminated union at root props level** — RDT correctly handles `forwardRef<E, A | B>`
403	   by merging props and detecting the discriminant. We drop the component. RDT output for

## Your task: Fix duplicate InheritedLayer (C2)

**File:** `crates/core/src/resolver/extends.rs`

**The bug:** When a component extends `React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<"button">`, the `resolve_extends_ref` function returns the InheritedLayer in BOTH the returned `ResolvedChain.inheritance` AND in `Some(layer)`. Then in `chain.rs`, the caller does:

```rust
return (
```

```rust
return (

    Some(layer),
);
```

The layer is already returned in `Some(layer)` — the chain should NOT also include it. The caller in `chain.rs` already handles pushing the layer from `Some(layer)`.

input.prompt:
You are implementing a bug fix in the oxc-react-docgen Rust project at /Users/gabe/Projects/oxc-react-codegen.

## Your task: Fix JSDoc "consumed" tracking (I7)

**The bug:** `find_jsdoc` and `extract_jsdoc_tags` in `extractor/jsdoc.rs` have no consumed-comment tracking. The same `/** ... */` block comment can be returned multiple times — once for a component description, and again for the first prop's description. This causes:
- `Avatar.description = "Avatar diameter in pixels. @default 40"` — the `size` prop's JSDoc leaking as the component description
- `Select.description = "Whether the select is disabled."` — the `disabled` prop's JSDoc leaking

**Root cause:** Both functions search `self.comments` for the nearest block comment within 120 bytes of the given `span_start`. No tracking of which comments have already been "consumed."

## Solution

Add a `consumed_comment_ends: FxHashSet<u32>` field to `SourceDataCollector` and track usage.

### Step 1: Read these files first
- `crates/core/src/extractor/mod.rs` lines 65-95 (the `SourceDataCollector` struct definition)
- `crates/core/src/extractor/jsdoc.rs` (the whole file)
- Search for all callers of `find_jsdoc` and `extract_jsdoc_tags`:
  ```bash
  grep -n "find_jsdoc\|extract_jsdoc_tags" crates/core/src/extractor/*.rs
  ```

### Step 2: Add field to `SourceDataCollector` struct in `extractor/mod.rs`

In the struct definition, add:
```rust
/// Tracks which JSDoc comment spans have already been consumed (by span_end).
/// Prevents the same comment from leaking to both a component description and its first prop.
pub(super) consumed_jsdoc: FxHashSet<u32>,
```

In `SourceDataCollector::new(...)`, initialize it:
```rust
consumed_jsdoc: FxHashSet::default(),
```

### Step 3: Change `find_jsdoc` and `extract_jsdoc_tags` in `extractor/jsdoc.rs`

Change `find_jsdoc` signature from `&self` to `&mut self` and add consumed tracking:

```rust
pub(super) fn find_jsdoc(&mut self, span_start: u32) -> String {
    const PROXIMITY_THRESHOLD: u32 = 120;

    let comment = self
        .comments
        .iter()
        .find(|c| {
            c.is_block
                && c.span_end <= span_start
                && span_start - c.span_end <= PROXIMITY_THRESHOLD
                && !self.consumed_jsdoc.contains(&c.span_end)
        });

    match comment {
        Some(c) => {
            let span_end = c.span_end;
            let raw = &self.source[c.span_start as usize..c.span_end as usize];
            let text = parse_jsdoc_text(raw);
            if !text.is_empty() {
                self.consumed_jsdoc.insert(span_end);
            }
            text
        }
        None => String::new(),
    }
}
```

Note: changed `iter().rev()` to `iter()` — with consumed tracking we no longer need reverse iteration (we find the first unconsumed comment within threshold). Actually, keep `rev()` to still pick the NEAREST comment:

```rust
let comment = self
    .comments
    .iter()
    .rev()
    .find(|c| {
        c.is_block
            && c.span_end <= span_start
            && span_start - c.span_end <= PROXIMITY_THRESHOLD
            && !self.consumed_jsdoc.contains(&c.span_end)
    });
```

Similarly change `extract_jsdoc_tags` to `&mut self` and also mark the comment consumed:

```rust
pub(super) fn extract_jsdoc_tags(&mut self, span_start: u32) -> BTreeMap<String, String> {
    const PROXIMITY_THRESHOLD: u32 = 120;

    let comment = self
        .comments
        .iter()
        .rev()
        .find(|c| {
            c.is_block
                && c.span_end <= span_start
                && span_start - c.span_end <= PROXIMITY_THRESHOLD
                && !self.consumed_jsdoc.contains(&c.span_end)
        });

    match comment {
        Some(c) => {
            let raw = &self.source[c.span_start as usize..c.span_end as usize];
            extract_jsdoc_tags(raw)
            // Note: we do NOT mark consumed here — extract_jsdoc_tags is called AFTER
            // find_jsdoc for the same span, so find_jsdoc already consumed it.
        }
        None => BTreeMap::new(),
    }
}
```

### Step 4: Fix all callers that broke due to `&self` → `&mut self`

After compiling you'll see every method that calls `self.find_jsdoc(...)` or `self.extract_jsdoc_tags(...)`. Each of those callers needs to be `&mut self` too (they probably already are, since they're building `SourceData`).

```bash
cargo build -p oxc-react-docgen-core 2>&1 | grep -E "^error" | head -30
```

Fix any "cannot borrow `*self` as mutable" errors by changing the calling method signatures from `&self` to `&mut self`.

### Step 5: Run tests
```bash
cargo test -p oxc-react-docgen-core 2>&1 | grep -E "FAILED|passed|failed|test result" | tail -10
```

Snapshot tests WILL fail — component descriptions in some snapshots will change (Avatar, Select, IconButton). This is expected and correct. Do NOT update snapshots — just verify the fix compiles and unit tests (non-snapshot) pass.

### Step 6: Commit
```bash
git add crates/core/src/extractor/jsdoc.rs crates/core/src/extractor/mod.rs
git commit -m "fix(extractor): track consumed JSDoc comments to prevent description leaks"
```

## Non-negotiables
- `FxHashSet` for `consumed_jsdoc` (not std HashSet)
- No `unwrap()` outside `#[cfg(test)]`
- Do not update snapshots

## Key constraint: call ORDER matters
`find_jsdoc` should be called BEFORE `extract_jsdoc_tags` for the same `span_start` — find_jsdoc marks the comment consumed, and extract_jsdoc_tags finds the same comment (now consumed) and reads tags from it. Check the calling code in `collect_property_signature` and similar functions to verify the order is: `find_jsdoc` first, then `extract_jsdoc_tags`.

If the caller calls `extract_jsdoc_tags` first (or the order matters differently), adjust the consumed-marking to be in `extract_jsdoc_tags` instead. Read the callers to understand the actual call order.

**The parallel speedup was real.** 8 fixes that would have taken ~2 hours sequentially finished in ~16 minutes wall-clock. The only serialization cost was the anyhow advisory — every team hit it and fixed it redundantly. A shared "pre-run setup" step would eliminate this in future waves.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
**Why synthetic alias registration works here:**  
The extractor's `SourceData.type_aliases` is a flat `FxHashMap<String, CollectedTypeAlias>` that gets merged into `GlobalSourceData` during the pipeline phase. Any alias we insert during extraction — even one derived from an inline union in `forwardRef<E, A|B>` — becomes visible to the resolver just like a top-level `type X = A | B` declaration. We're essentially desugaring the inline union into an anonymous named alias.

**Why `len()` is a safe key suffix:**  
Between collecting members (which may recursively insert aliases for nested unions) and computing the key, no other insertion happens. So `len()` gives us the next unused slot — safe without a separate counter field.

**Why intersection gets the same treatment:**  
`A & B` as forwardRef's props type is common in `*.d.ts` files (e.g. `ButtonProps & React.ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement>`) and in older library patterns. The same `TSIntersectionType` arm costs nothing and unblocks the whole pattern.
