469	aren't declared directly on `HTMLDivElement` — they're inherited via `extends HTMLElement` (and, for `nonce`,
470	`HTMLElement extends ... HTMLOrSVGElement`) — and the existing field lookup only checked an interface's own
471	`props`, never its extends chain. Added `lookup_interface_including_ambient` (checks
472	`ctx.ambient_global_files` as a fallback) and a small recursive ancestor-chain search over `ExtendsRef::SameFile`
473	entries. All 4 props now resolve to `string`; `day-picker/DayPicker` prop count now matches
474	react-docgen-typescript exactly (68/68).
475	
476	### Fixed: `(typeof X)[number]` on a flat `const X = [...] as const` array
477	
478	**Fixture:** `fixtures/antd/buttonHelpers.tsx`
479	
480	```ts
481	const _ButtonTypes = ['default', 'primary', 'dashed', 'link', 'text'] as const;
482	export type ButtonType = (typeof _ButtonTypes)[number];
483	```
484	
485	Two gaps, neither previously covered: nothing captured a plain array-literal `const` (only cva/tv's `variants`
486	object shape and const-object enums), and indexed access never handled a `[number]` key — `key` there is
487	`CollectedType::Number` (the `number` keyword type), not a string literal, so the existing string-literal-keyed
488	lookup always missed it. Added `SourceData::const_arrays` (deliberately separate from `enums`, which has
489	per-entry variant names and is surfaced directly in the public output — a plain array has neither), populated by
490	a new `try_collect_const_array` mirroring `try_collect_const_enum`'s shape but for `ArrayExpression`. Added a
491	matching `const_array_bare_index` on `ResolutionContext` (same O(1) pattern as `enum_bare_index`) and a new
492	branch in `resolve_indexed_access` that builds a `LiteralUnion` from the array's values when `obj` is `TypeOf`
493	and `key` is `Number`. All 5 exported unions in the fixture (`ButtonType`, `ButtonShape`, `ButtonHTMLType`,
494	`ButtonVariantType`, `ButtonColorType`) now resolve correctly; the 10 associated diagnostics are gone.
495	
496	`ButtonColorType`'s source array uses a spread (`['default', 'primary', 'danger', ...PresetColors]`) — the
497	spread element is silently skipped (no expression to read a literal from), so that one union resolves with 3 of
498	its real ~19 members. A known, honest partial result, not a crash or a wrong type; matches how cva/tv variant
499	extraction already treats constructs it can't statically read.
500	
501	### Fixed: static `X.defaultProps = {...}` assignment not read
502	
503	`ComponentMapping::param_defaults` already had a `DefaultSource::DefaultProps` variant — designed for but never
504	wired up. Only destructured defaults (`function Button({ size = 'md' })`, via `extract_param_defaults`) were
505	ever populated. Real components (MUI ships this on several) also set defaults via a static assignment after the
506	declaration:
507	
508	```ts
509	function Button(props: ButtonProps) { ... }
510	Button.defaultProps = { size: 'md' };
511	```
512	
513	Added `try_scan_default_props`, mirroring the existing `try_scan_display_name`'s shape (same "find the
514	`ExpressionStatement` assigning to `X.<prop>`, look up the matching `ComponentMapping`" pattern) — extracts each
515	object property via `eval_expr_as_default`, now parameterized with a `DefaultSource` instead of hardcoding
516	`Destructuring`, so both call sites tag their defaults correctly. The resolver's consumption side
517	(`resolver/chain.rs`'s `mapping.param_defaults.get(&raw_prop.name)`) needed no changes — it was already
518	source-agnostic, just never had anything to read from this path.
519	
520	No fixture ships a real static `defaultProps` assignment today — `fixtures/blueprint/Table.tsx` had in fact been
521	deliberately written *around* this exact gap (its header comment said so explicitly). Comment updated; fixture
522	coverage stays as destructured defaults since upstream Blueprint's `Table` is a class component and this fixture
523	uses a function component by design (a separate, unrelated tradeoff — see the fixture's own comment). Covered
524	instead by a dedicated extractor unit test and a pipeline end-to-end test proving the value reaches
525	`ParsedProp.default_value`.
526	
527	---
528	
529	## Note: React 19 `ref`-as-prop — investigated, not a real gap
530	
531	`ReactVersion::ref_as_prop`/`implicit_children` (`react_types.rs`) exist as fields, are correctly plumbed from
532	the `--react-version`/`docgen.config.ts` CLI surface down to `PipelineOptions.react_version` (tested), and are
533	then never read by anything in `crates/core`. That looked like a real gap — the original spec's worry was that
534	`function Button({ ref, ...props }: ButtonProps)` (React 19's plain-prop `ref`, no `forwardRef`) wouldn't be
535	recognized.
536	
537	Tested directly against both real shapes:
538	
539	```ts
540	// ref declared directly on the props interface
541	interface ButtonProps { label: string; ref?: Ref<HTMLButtonElement>; }
542	export function Button({ ref, ...props }: ButtonProps) { ... }
543	
544	// ref merged in via intersection (the more common real-world shape)
545	type ButtonProps = BaseProps & { ref?: Ref<HTMLButtonElement> };
546	export function Button({ ref, ...props }: ButtonProps) { ... }
547	```
548	
549	Both already extract `ref` correctly as `{ kind: 'ref', element: 'HTMLButtonElement' }`, no special-casing
550	involved — the extractor doesn't care that the member happens to be named `ref`; it walks whatever the props
551	type structurally contains, same as any other member, regardless of React version. The one case this doesn't
552	cover — `ref` implicitly present via `ComponentProps<'button'>`'s real React 19 typing rather than an explicit
553	member — falls under the existing, already-accepted "curated mode doesn't expand full HTML attributes" limit,
554	not a version-specific gap.
555	
556	Left the `ReactVersion` fields and CLI flag in place (real, tested, user-facing surface) rather than ripping them
557	out — but didn't invent speculative behavior for a bug that isn't reproducible. If a concrete React-version-
558	dependent extraction difference ever surfaces, this is where it'd get wired in.
559	
560	### Fixed: bare passthrough identifier alias not renaming the component
561	
562	**Fixture:** `fixtures/antd/Button.tsx`
563	
564	Found by a full-fixture validation sweep (`apps/validate`'s comparison across all 20 libraries at once, not a
565	per-fixture check) — `antd/Button/Button` showed `ours found nothing` despite the component clearly being
566	extracted correctly under a different name. antd's real `Button` export:
567	
568	```ts
569	const InternalCompoundedButton = React.forwardRef<...>((props, ref) => { ... });
570	const Button = InternalCompoundedButton;   // (real upstream: `as CompoundedComponent`)
571	Button.displayName = 'Button';
572	export default Button;
573	```
574	
575	`try_scan_display_name` couldn't help here — it matches the assignment's left-hand object name
576	(`"Button"`) against an existing mapping's name, but the mapping was still `"InternalCompoundedButton"`, so the
577	match never fired. The actual gap was one level earlier:
578	`try_rename_identifier_wrapped_component` (added for Headless UI's `forwardRefWithAs(ButtonFn) as X` — an
579	*unrecognized wrapper call* around an already-detected component) only matched a `CallExpression` init. antd's
580	shape has no wrapper call at all — just a bare `const NewName = OldName;` passthrough, optionally `as`-cast.
581	Added a second match arm for a bare `Expression::Identifier` init, reusing the same rename logic. `Button` now
582	surfaces with all 23 real props under its actual export name.
583	
584	## Note: compound components (`Dialog.Trigger`) — investigated, not a real gap
585	
586	The original worry: `Dialog.Trigger`, `Select.Item` — sub-components hung off a parent via dot access — aren't
587	detected as separate components at all.
588	
589	Checked every fixture with a multi-component "family" shape. None uses the actual `<Namespace.Member>` dot-
590	access pattern. `fixtures/ariakit`'s `Menu`/`MenuButton`/`MenuItem`/`MenuProvider` are just independently
591	exported, independently named components — nothing to detect beyond what already works.
592	`fixtures/headlessui/Listbox.tsx` gets closest — real Ark UI/Headless UI code does
593	`Object.assign(ListboxRoot, { Button: ListboxButton, ... })` to expose `Listbox.Button` as a deprecated
594	convenience alias — but `ListboxButton` is *also* independently exported (`export let ListboxButton =
595	forwardRefWithAs(ButtonFn) as _internal_ComponentListboxButton`) as the primary, non-deprecated API, and that
596	already gets detected and extracted correctly today (confirmed: `Listbox`, `ListboxButton`, `ListboxOption` all
597	present in the output, each with accurate props).
598	
599	What's actually missing, if anything, is purely cosmetic: no dot-qualified display name (`"Listbox.Button"`
600	instead of `"ListboxButton"`) and no parent/child grouping metadata for doc tools that want to nest sub-
601	components under their parent. There's no fixture or test demonstrating this as broken, and no evidence for
602	which of several plausible designs (rename the display name vs. add a separate grouping field) real consumers
603	would actually want — building either now would be speculative, not a fix. Left alone.
604	
605	## Note: slot recipes — partial support
606	
607	`defineSlotRecipe` (PandaCSS) and `tv({ slots })` (tailwind-variants) are in the recognized callee list and benefit from the 2026-06-28 arg-index fix. However, slot recipe variant values are objects (`{ root: "class", header: "class" }`) rather than plain strings. The current `try_collect_cva_call` variant value extraction reads only string values, so slot recipe variants will have 0 entries in `global.enums` even after the arg-index fix.
608	
609	The `RecipeVariantProps<typeof slotRecipe>` reference will fall back to opaque output with `raw: "VariantProps<typeof slotRecipe>"` in the `composes` array. This is documented as a limitation, not a bug.
610	
611	**To support slot recipes:** extend the variant value extractor to accept both `string` and `ObjectExpression` values, treating the object's string values as the display representation.

# RDT Spec Coverage Matrix

Maps each react-docgen-typescript (RDT) output field and component pattern to the fixtures that exercise it. Run `cargo test -p oxc-react-docgen-core --test snapshots` to validate the original 8 snapshot fixtures. The 8 real-world library fixtures added since (fluentui, base-ui, antd, ark-ui, zendesk-garden, day-picker, headlessui, blueprint) aren't snapshot-tested — validate them via `pnpm --filter @oxc-react-docgen/validate compare:all`.

---

## PropType kinds

Each `PropType` variant the resolver can emit; whether any fixture produces it.

| Kind | Covered by |
|------|-----------|
| `string` | all fixtures |
| `number` | all fixtures |
| `boolean` | all fixtures |
| `null` | mui, shadcn |
| `unknown` | mui |
| `reactNode` | chakra, mantine, mui, react-aria |
| `cssProperties` | chakra, mui, react-aria, shadcn |
| `elementType` | chakra, mantine, mui |
| `stringLiteral` | chakra, mantine, mui, react-aria, shadcn |
| `union` | chakra, mantine, mui, react-aria, shadcn, **day-picker** (7-way discriminated) |
| `named` | chakra, mantine, mui, react-aria |
| `eventHandler` | all fixtures; real param names from `(open: boolean) => void`-style handlers (not a hardcoded `"e"`) verified against **headlessui**, **ark-ui** |
| `ref` | mantine, mui |
| `object` | mantine, **rdt-compat/types** (`raw_string()` renders real fields — `{ key: Type; key2?: Type2 }` — not the literal placeholder `"object"`) |
| `literalUnion` | mantine, shadcn, **panda** (after defineRecipe arg-index fix) |
| `array` | **rdt-compat/types** (`string[]` syntax), **day-picker** (`readonly string[]` type-operator form) |
| `tuple` | **rdt-compat/types** (`[number, number]`; `raw_string()` renders real elements, not the placeholder `"tuple"`) |
| `numberLiteral` | **rdt-compat/types** (`1 \| 2 \| 4 \| 8`) |
| `boolLiteral` | **rdt-compat/types** (`true` literal type) |
| `undefined` | **rdt-compat/types** (explicit `?: undefined`) |
| `sxProps` | **rdt-compat/types** (unresolved `SxProps` ref → known-pattern shortcut) |
| `htmlAttributes` | **rdt-compat/types** (`ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'button'>` as prop value); real per-element attribute resolution (not just this metadata layer) — see [HtmlAttributeMode](#htmlattributemode-curated--full--none) below |
| `intersection` | **rdt-compat/types** (`CSSProperties & { '--accent': string }`) |
| `opaque` | **rdt-compat/types** (inline conditional type `T extends A ? B : C`) |
| `void` | ❌ not covered — `() => void` captured as `eventHandler`, standalone `void` never appears |
| `never` | ❌ not covered — no real-world prop has type `never` |
| `any` | ❌ not covered — `any` suppressed by TypeScript `strict` in fixtures |

> **Note on `void` / `never`:** These kinds exist in the type system for completeness but are not realistic prop types. A function return type `() => void` is always emitted as `eventHandler`, and `never` typically indicates a broken discriminant. No fixture is planned for either.

## HtmlAttributeMode: curated / full / none

`PipelineOptions.html_attributes` (CLI: `--html-attributes <curated|full|none>`; NAPI: `htmlAttributes: 'curated' | 'full' | 'none'`; config file: `htmlAttributes` in `docgen.config.ts`) controls how much of an inherited HTML element's attribute surface gets exposed:

- **Curated (default)** — unchanged original behavior: ~15-20 hand-picked, commonly-documented attributes per element (`onClick`, `disabled`, `aria-*`, etc.) synthesized into `notableInherited`.
- **Full** — actually resolves `@types/react`'s real `HTMLAttributes`/`AriaAttributes`/`DOMAttributes`/`<Element>HTMLAttributes` interface chain (merged into `GlobalSourceData` by the pipeline, looked up by the resolver like any other interface) and merges the real fields directly into `props` — matching how RDT flattens everything into one props map. Verified against a real button: 238 of ~250 real attributes resolve (the remainder is a narrower, separate gap — see below). Costs ~16ms once per `@types/react` version (cached the same way any other `.d.ts` is), not per extraction run.
- **None** — no inherited HTML attributes synthesized at all; own props only.

**Known residual gap, not fixed:** a handful of fields inside `@types/react`'s own interface chain (`AriaAttributes` referenced bare from within the same enclosing `declare namespace React {}` block, not through an explicit `React.` qualifier) don't resolve — same-namespace *sibling* reference resolution is narrower than the namespace-*qualified* reference resolution fixed for cross-file/explicit cases. ## Fixed bugs (previously tracked here as open)

### Fixed: method-shorthand handler losing param type

**Fixture:** `fixtures/rdt-compat/controlled.tsx`

Previously: `onValueChange?(value: string): void` (TSMethodSignature form) emitted `eventType: "..."` instead of `eventType: "string"`, while the arrow-function form correctly emitted `eventType: "boolean"`. Root cause: the extractor's method-signature handling didn't extract parameter types the same way as property-signature handling. Fixed — confirmed live: `onValueChange` now correctly resolves to `(value: string) => void`.

---

### Fixed: `Pick<T, Keys>` not resolved even for source types

**Fixture:** `fixtures/rdt-compat/pick-source.tsx`

Previously: `interface IconButtonProps extends Pick<ButtonBaseProps, 'disabled' | 'type' | 'form'>` lost the picked props entirely — only `icon`/`label` (the interface's own props) appeared. Fixed — confirmed live: `IconButton` now correctly includes `disabled`, `form`, `type` alongside `icon`/`label`.

---

### Fixed: union-of-interfaces root props type silently skipped the component

**Fixture:** `fixtures/rdt-compat/discriminated-union.tsx`

Previously: `Accordion` with props type `AccordionSingleProps | AccordionMultipleProps` was completely absent from the output, no diagnostic. Fixed — confirmed live: `Accordion` now resolves with all 5 real props.

---

### Fixed: component description set to last prop's JSDoc

**Fixtures:** `fixtures/rdt-compat/controlled.tsx`, `pick-source.tsx`, `memo.tsx`

Previously: when a component had no JSDoc of its own, `ComponentEntry.description` picked up the last prop's JSDoc instead of staying empty (the extractor's proximity-based `find_jsdoc` scan finding the wrong nearest comment). Fixed — confirmed live: `Select`/`IconButton`/`Avatar` all correctly show `description: ""`.

---

### Fixed: forwardRef wrapped in an `as`-cast

**Fixtures:** `fixtures/fluentui/Button.tsx`, `fixtures/ark-ui/Select.tsx`

Fluent UI's real Button (and Ark UI's real Select) are authored as `const X: SomeWrapper<Props> = React.forwardRef((props, ref) => {...}) as SomeWrapper<Props>` — neither `try_fc_annotation` (the wrapper type name wasn't recognized) nor `try_forward_ref`/`try_hoc_wrapped` (both required the initializer to be a `CallExpression` directly, not a `TSAsExpression` wrapping one) detected this; the component was silently invisible. Fixed by recognizing `ForwardRefComponent<P>` as a wrapper annotation and peeling `as`-casts before matching the call expression underneath. Confirmed: Fluent's Button 0 → 8 props.

---

### Fixed: same-file namespace member resolution

**Fixture:** `fixtures/base-ui/MenuRoot.tsx`, `MenuTrigger.tsx`

Base UI's real pattern is `namespace MenuRoot { export type Props<Payload> = ... }`, referenced elsewhere in the same file as `MenuRoot.Props`. Storage keyed on the bare member name while the resolver looked up the fully-qualified dotted name — same-file namespace member references could never resolve. Fixed by tracking an enclosing-namespace stack during extraction and qualifying storage keys to match. Confirmed: MenuRoot 0 → 15 props (exact match with real RDT), MenuTrigger invisible → 11 props.

---

### Fixed: JSDoc `@tag` bleeding onto sibling props

**Fixture:** `fixtures/antd/Button.tsx`

`find_jsdoc` (description) tracked consumed comment spans so two elements never share one description; `extract_jsdoc_tags` (the `@tag` map) ran a separate scan with no consumed-tracking at all, so a `@deprecated` tag correctly claimed by one prop was still "found" and inherited by a later sibling with no JSDoc of its own. Fixed by merging both lookups into one consuming pass. Confirmed: only `iconPosition` carries `@deprecated` now, not `iconPlacement`/`shape`/`size`/`disabled`.

---

### Fixed: user-defined generic type alias substitution

**Fixture:** `fixtures/ark-ui/Select.tsx`

`type Assign<T, U> = Omit<T, keyof U> & U` used with concrete call-site arguments (Ark UI's real `SelectRootProps<T> = Assign<HTMLProps<'div'>, SelectRootBaseProps<T>>`) never substituted `T`/`U` — type alias declarations didn't record their own declared parameters, and call-site type arguments were computed but discarded before alias resolution ran. `Omit<T, keyof U>`'s `keyof U` was also silently treated as an empty key list. Fixed via a structural walk-and-replace substitution engine (no type inference — real field names for `keyof U` come from resolving `U` as its own props chain). Confirmed: SelectRoot 0 → 36 real props via the actual, unmodified upstream pattern.

---

### Fixed: `Partial<X>` cycle-detection key collision

**Fixture:** `fixtures/blueprint/Table.tsx`

`TableProps extends Partial<RowHeights>, Partial<ColumnWidths>` — the resolver's cycle-detection visited-key was built from the bare type name alone (`"Partial"`), not its type arguments, so the second `Partial<X>` extends target collided with the first's cycle-guard entry and silently resolved to nothing, with zero diagnostic. Fixed by folding type arguments into the key. Confirmed: Table 45 → 48 props, exact match with real RDT.

---

### Fixed: discriminated unions wrapped in an intersection

**Fixture:** `fixtures/day-picker/DayPicker.tsx`

Discriminant detection only ran when a type alias's RHS was *directly* a union (`type X = A | B`). Real Day Picker's `DayPickerProps = PropsBase & (7-way union)` — an intersection whose union member fell into a naive per-member merge instead, keeping only whichever branch's type was seen first per prop instead of unioning across all branches. Fixed by having the intersection-nested-union case delegate to the same discriminant-merge logic a direct union alias uses. Confirmed: `selected`'s type now correctly merges `Date | Date[] | DateRange` across all 7 branches (previously collapsed to bare `Date`). Also confirmed (and this is *correct*, not a remaining bug): `discriminantProp` stays `null` for Day Picker's real union, because `mode` repeats the same value across `PropsSingle`/`PropsSingleRequired` — it's only jointly unique with a second field (`required`), so no single field actually identifies the variant.

---

### Fixed: bare function-type alias silently dropped

**Fixture:** `fixtures/day-picker/props.ts`

`type OnSelectHandler<T> = (selected: T, ...) => void` — a bare function type as an alias body — fell through `classify_type_alias`'s catch-all and vanished from `type_aliases` with no diagnostic, same failure mode as the already-fixed inline-object-literal case. Fixed by routing `TSFunctionType` through the same `Passthrough` wrapping `TSTypeLiteral` already used. Confirmed: `OnSelectHandler` no longer triggers a "cannot resolve" warning.

---

### Fixed: identifier-wrapped components renamed to export binding

**Fixture:** `fixtures/headlessui/Listbox.tsx`

Headless UI's real Listbox family: standalone top-level function declarations (`function ButtonFn(props, ref)`) wrapped by a library-defined `forwardRefWithAs` (not React's own `forwardRef`) and reassigned (`export let ListboxButton = forwardRefWithAs(ButtonFn) as X`). `ButtonFn` was already independently detected as its own component (a valid top-level PascalCase function with a typed first param) under the wrong, inner-implementation-only name — neither `try_forward_ref` (the callee isn't `React.forwardRef`) nor `try_hoc_wrapped` (the argument is a bare identifier, not an inline function) recognized the wrapping assignment. Fixed the same way the existing `displayName`-scan already handles a similar after-the-fact rename: when a variable's initializer is (after unwrapping any `as` cast) a call whose sole argument is a bare identifier matching an already-collected component, rename that mapping to the outer binding. Confirmed: all three components (`Listbox`, `ListboxButton`, `ListboxOption`) now report their real export names, matching real RDT.

---

### Fixed: type alias union/intersection members resolved relative to the wrong file

**Fixture:** `fixtures/tanstack-table/types.ts`

`ColumnDef<TData, TValue> = DisplayColumnDef<...> | GroupColumnDef<...> | AccessorColumnDef<...>` — a union whose members are same-file siblings of the alias, imported cross-file into `data-table.tsx` as just `ColumnDef`. `resolve_type_alias_type` forwarded the *caller's* `consuming_file` into the recursive member resolution instead of the alias's own declaring file, so `DisplayColumnDef` etc. were looked up relative to `data-table.tsx` (which never imports them directly) and spuriously flagged as unresolvable, even though the actual `PropType::Named` output was already correct. Fixed by giving `CollectedTypeAlias` a `file_path()` accessor and using it instead of the passed-in file for every recursive call.

### Fixed: generic interface/alias's own type parameters flagged as unresolvable

**Fixture:** `fixtures/tanstack-table/data-table.tsx`

`DataTableProps<TData, TValue>` referencing its own `TData`/`TValue` in its body (`columns: ColumnDef<TData, TValue>[]`) had every such reference warned as "cannot resolve — will appear as opaque", even though a bare generic placeholder is the objectively correct, expected output. The resolver had no concept of a type's own declared parameters. Added `interface_type_params` (mirroring the existing `type_alias_params`) and a `ResolveState.in_scope_type_params` set populated when entering a generic interface/alias body; `resolve_named` checks it before warning. 234 → 173 diagnostics across all fixtures.

### Fixed: named type-only imports from `react` resolved to the wrong file/key

**Fixture:** `fixtures/react-resizable-panels/types.ts`

`import type { X } from "react"` (any `X` not special-cased via `html_element_for`) failed for two independent reasons: (1) `react`'s own `package.json` has no `"types"` field/condition — its real declarations live in the separate `@types/react` package — so the general import resolver landed on `index.js`; (2) `@types/react` declares everything inside `declare namespace React { ... }`, so even the right file's declarations are keyed `"React.X"`, not bare `"X"`. Fixed resolver-wide: `resolve_import_specifier` now tries `resolve_dts` + the `@types/<package>` fallback for bare specifiers (reusing the logic already proven for `HtmlAttributeMode::Full`), and new `lookup_interface`/`lookup_type_alias` helpers try the bare key before the `React.`-qualified one, replacing direct map lookups at every interface/alias resolution site.

### Fixed: indexed access into a generic interface's own field

**Fixture:** `fixtures/react-final-form/types.ts`

`RenderableProps<FieldRenderProps<FieldValue, T>>["children"]` (the real "children as a render-function-or-ReactNode union" pattern) degraded to `Opaque` — `resolve_indexed_access`'s only fallback resolved the object type and checked for `PropType::Object`, but an interface always resolves to a bare `PropType::Named` at the type level (never expanded there), so it never matched. Added a path that looks the field up directly on the interface's declaration and substitutes its declared type parameters with the caller's concrete arguments, reusing the existing generic-alias substitution machinery. Both indexed-access fields in this fixture (`children`, `component`) now resolve to real structured types with the correct substituted argument threaded through, zero diagnostics.

### Fixed: type aliases silently dropped for any unhandled body shape

**Fixture:** `fixtures/storybook-emotion/Button.tsx`

`type API_KeyCollection = string[]` — found while investigating the fixture below. `classify_type_alias`'s catch-all was `_ => None`: any alias body shape without a dedicated match arm vanished from `type_aliases` entirely, no diagnostic, same failure mode already fixed twice this session for `TSTypeLiteral` and `TSFunctionType` individually. Generalized the catch-all itself to `Passthrough`-wrap whatever `ts_type_to_collected` already produces, rather than adding a third narrow special case. 171 → 153 diagnostics across all fixtures (curated), 224 → 206 (full) — fixed the same silent-drop in other fixtures too, not just this one.

### Fixed: entire file silently discarded when JSDoc prose contains unmatched brackets

**Fixture:** the real `typescript` npm package's own `lib.dom.d.ts` (found while extending native-global resolution to DOM ambient types for the fix below).

`max_bracket_nesting_depth` — the pre-parse guard that bails out before handing pathologically nested types to `oxc_parser`'s recursive-descent parser — counted `(`/`{`/`[`/`)`/`}`/`]` byte-by-byte with no awareness of comments or string/template literals. Real-world `.d.ts` prose routinely contains unbalanced brackets (MDN-scraped JSDoc in `lib.dom.d.ts` has artifacts like `... MISSING: RFC(5646, '...')].`, a stray `]` with no opening `[`, roughly 2000 times); each one drove the running depth negative, and once negative enough, the next legitimate bracket in real code still left it negative — casting that negative `i64` to `usize` wrapped to ~`u64::MAX`, tripping the "exceeds maximum nesting depth" guard and silently discarding the entire 1.8MB file (0 interfaces extracted, no diagnostic reaching the user beyond a generic skip message). Rewrote the scan to skip `//`/`/* */` comments and `'...'`/`"..."`/`` `...` `` literals entirely rather than counting their bracket content, and switched `depth` to `usize` with `saturating_sub` so it can never go negative regardless of any remaining edge case. Confirmed against the real installed `lib.dom.d.ts`: 0 → thousands of interfaces extracted, no more false-positive `ExcessiveNesting` diagnostic.

### Fixed: indexed access into an ambient DOM interface not walking its `extends` chain

**Fixture:** `fixtures/day-picker/props.ts`

`dir?: HTMLDivElement["dir"]` (also `nonce`, `title`, `lang`) degraded to `Opaque` even after `lib.dom.d.ts` became parseable (previous fix). Two compounding gaps: `resolve_indexed_access`'s interface lookup only checked the consuming file's own imports/declarations, never TypeScript's own ambient lib files, so `HTMLDivElement` (never imported — it's a global) was never found at all; and even once found, `dir`/`nonce`/`title`/`lang` aren't declared directly on `HTMLDivElement` — they're inherited via `extends HTMLElement` (and, for `nonce`, `HTMLElement extends ... HTMLOrSVGElement`) — and the existing field lookup only checked an interface's own `props`, never its extends chain. Added `lookup_interface_including_ambient` (checks `ctx.ambient_global_files` as a fallback) and a small recursive ancestor-chain search over `ExtendsRef::SameFile` entries. All 4 props now resolve to `string`; `day-picker/DayPicker` prop count now matches react-docgen-typescript exactly (68/68).

### Fixed: `(typeof X)[number]` on a flat `const X = [...] as const` array

**Fixture:** `fixtures/antd/buttonHelpers.tsx`

```ts
const _ButtonTypes = ['default', 'primary', 'dashed', 'link', 'text'] as const;
export type ButtonType = (typeof _ButtonTypes)[number];
```

Two gaps, neither previously covered: nothing captured a plain array-literal `const` (only cva/tv's `variants` object shape and const-object enums), and indexed access never handled a `[number]` key — `key` there is `CollectedType::Number` (the `number` keyword type), not a string literal, so the existing string-literal-keyed lookup always missed it. Added `SourceData::const_arrays` (deliberately separate from `enums`, which has per-entry variant names and is surfaced directly in the public output — a plain array has neither), populated by a new `try_collect_const_array` mirroring `try_collect_const_enum`'s shape but for `ArrayExpression`. Added a matching `const_array_bare_index` on `ResolutionContext` (same O(1) pattern as `enum_bare_index`) and a new branch in `resolve_indexed_access` that builds a `LiteralUnion` from the array's values when `obj` is `TypeOf` and `key` is `Number`. All 5 exported unions in the fixture (`ButtonType`, `ButtonShape`, `ButtonHTMLType`, `ButtonVariantType`, `ButtonColorType`) now resolve correctly; the 10 associated diagnostics are gone.

`ButtonColorType`'s source array uses a spread (`['default', 'primary', 'danger', ...PresetColors]`) — the spread element is silently skipped (no expression to read a literal from), so that one union resolves with 3 of its real ~19 members. A known, honest partial result, not a crash or a wrong type; matches how cva/tv variant extraction already treats constructs it can't statically read.

### Fixed: static `X.defaultProps = {...}` assignment not read

`ComponentMapping::param_defaults` already had a `DefaultSource::DefaultProps` variant — designed for but never wired up. Only destructured defaults (`function Button({ size = 'md' })`, via `extract_param_defaults`) were ever populated. Real components (MUI ships this on several) also set defaults via a static assignment after the declaration:

```ts
function Button(props: ButtonProps) { ... }
Button.defaultProps = { size: 'md' };
```

Added `try_scan_default_props`, mirroring the existing `try_scan_display_name`'s shape (same "find the `ExpressionStatement` assigning to `X.<prop>`, look up the matching `ComponentMapping`" pattern) — extracts each object property via `eval_expr_as_default`, now parameterized with a `DefaultSource` instead of hardcoding `Destructuring`, so both call sites tag their defaults correctly. The resolver's consumption side (`resolver/chain.rs`'s `mapping.param_defaults.get(&raw_prop.name)`) needed no changes — it was already source-agnostic, just never had anything to read from this path.

No fixture ships a real static `defaultProps` assignment today — `fixtures/blueprint/Table.tsx` had in fact been deliberately written *around* this exact gap (its header comment said so explicitly). Comment updated; fixture coverage stays as destructured defaults since upstream Blueprint's `Table` is a class component and this fixture uses a function component by design (a separate, unrelated tradeoff — see the fixture's own comment). Covered instead by a dedicated extractor unit test and a pipeline end-to-end test proving the value reaches `ParsedProp.default_value`.

---

## Note: React 19 `ref`-as-prop — investigated, not a real gap

`ReactVersion::ref_as_prop`/`implicit_children` (`react_types.rs`) exist as fields, are correctly plumbed from the `--react-version`/`docgen.config.ts` CLI surface down to `PipelineOptions.react_version` (tested), and are then never read by anything in `crates/core`. That looked like a real gap — the original spec's worry was that `function Button({ ref, ...props }: ButtonProps)` (React 19's plain-prop `ref`, no `forwardRef`) wouldn't be recognized.

Tested directly against both real shapes:

```ts
// ref declared directly on the props interface
interface ButtonProps { label: string; ref?: Ref<HTMLButtonElement>; }
export function Button({ ref, ...props }: ButtonProps) { ... }

// ref merged in via intersection (the more common real-world shape)
type ButtonProps = BaseProps & { ref?: Ref<HTMLButtonElement> };
export function Button({ ref, ...props }: ButtonProps) { ... }
```

Both already extract `ref` correctly as `{ kind: 'ref', element: 'HTMLButtonElement' }`, no special-casing involved — the extractor doesn't care that the member happens to be named `ref`; it walks whatever the props type structurally contains, same as any other member, regardless of React version. The one case this doesn't cover — `ref` implicitly present via `ComponentProps<'button'>`'s real React 19 typing rather than an explicit member — falls under the existing, already-accepted "curated mode doesn't expand full HTML attributes" limit, not a version-specific gap.

Left the `ReactVersion` fields and CLI flag in place (real, tested, user-facing surface) rather than ripping them out — but didn't invent speculative behavior for a bug that isn't reproducible. If a concrete React-version-dependent extraction difference ever surfaces, this is where it'd get wired in.

### Fixed: bare passthrough identifier alias not renaming the component

**Fixture:** `fixtures/antd/Button.tsx`

Found by a full-fixture validation sweep (`apps/validate`'s comparison across all 20 libraries at once, not a per-fixture check) — `antd/Button/Button` showed `ours found nothing` despite the component clearly being extracted correctly under a different name. antd's real `Button` export:

```ts
const InternalCompoundedButton = React.forwardRef<...>((props, ref) => { ... });
const Button = InternalCompoundedButton;   // (real upstream: `as CompoundedComponent`)
Button.displayName = 'Button';
export default Button;
```

`try_scan_display_name` couldn't help here — it matches the assignment's left-hand object name (`"Button"`) against an existing mapping's name, but the mapping was still `"InternalCompoundedButton"`, so the match never fired. The actual gap was one level earlier: `try_rename_identifier_wrapped_component` (added for Headless UI's `forwardRefWithAs(ButtonFn) as X` — an *unrecognized wrapper call* around an already-detected component) only matched a `CallExpression` init. antd's shape has no wrapper call at all — just a bare `const NewName = OldName;` passthrough, optionally `as`-cast. Added a second match arm for a bare `Expression::Identifier` init, reusing the same rename logic. `Button` now surfaces with all 23 real props under its actual export name.

## Note: compound components (`Dialog.Trigger`) — investigated, not a real gap

The original worry: `Dialog.Trigger`, `Select.Item` — sub-components hung off a parent via dot access — aren't detected as separate components at all.

Checked every fixture with a multi-component "family" shape. None uses the actual `<Namespace.Member>` dot-access pattern. `fixtures/ariakit`'s `Menu`/`MenuButton`/`MenuItem`/`MenuProvider` are just independently exported, independently named components — nothing to detect beyond what already works. `fixtures/headlessui/Listbox.tsx` gets closest — real Ark UI/Headless UI code does `Object.assign(ListboxRoot, { Button: ListboxButton, ... })` to expose `Listbox.Button` as a deprecated convenience alias — but `ListboxButton` is *also* independently exported (`export let ListboxButton = forwardRefWithAs(ButtonFn) as _internal_ComponentListboxButton`) as the primary, non-deprecated API, and that already gets detected and extracted correctly today (confirmed: `Listbox`, `ListboxButton`, `ListboxOption` all present in the output, each with accurate props).

What's actually missing, if anything, is purely cosmetic: no dot-qualified display name (`"Listbox.Button"` instead of `"ListboxButton"`) and no parent/child grouping metadata for doc tools that want to nest sub-components under their parent. There's no fixture or test demonstrating this as broken, and no evidence for which of several plausible designs (rename the display name vs. add a separate grouping field) real consumers would actually want — building either now would be speculative, not a fix. Left alone.

## Note: slot recipes — partial support

`defineSlotRecipe` (PandaCSS) and `tv({ slots })` (tailwind-variants) are in the recognized callee list and benefit from the 2026-06-28 arg-index fix. However, slot recipe variant values are objects (`{ root: "class", header: "class" }`) rather than plain strings. The current `try_collect_cva_call` variant value extraction reads only string values, so slot recipe variants will have 0 entries in `global.enums` even after the arg-index fix.

The `RecipeVariantProps<typeof slotRecipe>` reference will fall back to opaque output with `raw: "VariantProps<typeof slotRecipe>"` in the `composes` array. This is documented as a limitation, not a bug.

**To support slot recipes:** extend the variant value extractor to accept both `string` and `ObjectExpression` values, treating the object's string values as the display representation.

content.text:
Full picture now. Status per tool:

**Set up well:**
- **pnpm** — pinned (`packageManager: "pnpm@10"`, proto pins the same major), workspace globs correct, CI has a real matrix (Node 24/26) plus a dedicated job that verifies the napi binary resolves as a transitive dep for both npm and pnpm consumers.
- **just** — comprehensive `justfile` (install, build, test, test-ts, bench, coverage, lint, fmt, deny, typos, ci, compare, clean, setup, plus moon/cargo passthroughs).
- **clippy** — enforced in three places consistently: `justfile`'s `lint`, moon's git pre-commit hook, and CI's `lint` job, all with `-D warnings`.
- **vitest** — well set up for `vite-plugin` (18 tests, clean mocking of the napi boundary), and CI actually runs it across a Node matrix.
- **Coverage** — real: `cargo llvm-cov` → lcov → uploaded to Codecov in CI. Rust-only though, and there's no badge in the README, so it's invisible unless you go looking.

**Deliberate substitutes, not gaps:**
- **mise** — not used; `proto` (moonrepo's toolchain manager) does this job instead, pinning node/pnpm/rust/moon in `.prototools`. Makes sense since `moon` is already the task runner — mise would be a second, competing tool doing the same thing.

**Real gaps:**
- **oxlint** — not set up at all. Zero TS/JS linting exists anywhere in the repo (no eslint either). `just lint` and CI's `lint` job are Rust-only. Given the whole project is built on OXC, this is the most natural gap to close.
- **oxcfmt** — not set up, and there's a live bug hiding behind it: `just fmt` calls `pnpm exec prettier --write .`, but prettier isn't a devDependency anywhere in `package.json` or `pnpm-lock.yaml`. That command likely fails or silently does something unpinned today.
- **tsdown** — not used; `vite-plugin`'s build is bare `tsc` (type-check + unbundled ESM emit, no bundler at all). Fine if nothing needs single-file distribution, but worth naming.
- **Test-result publishing** — coverage uploads, but there's no JUnit/annotation output from `cargo nextest`, so failures don't show up as PR check annotations, just log output.
- **Dependency updates** — no dependabot or renovate config anywhere.
- **`release.yml`** — exists but is explicitly marked "UNTESTED SCAFFOLDING" by whoever wrote it (transparent, but means it's not real yet).

Want me to close the concrete ones — pin/fix prettier (or swap for oxlint's formatter once I check its current maturity), and add oxlint for the TS/JS side?

content.text:
Quick correction first: this actually is a monorepo by the usual definition — `crates/core`, `crates/cli`, `crates/binding`, `packages/napi`, `packages/vite-plugin`, `apps/validate` are six independently-buildable projects across two languages, and `apps/validate` genuinely depends on `cli:build` finishing first (moon models that dependency). But the real question is whether moon's *machinery* (task graphs, caching, VCS hook sync) is worth it at this size — and looking at actual usage, it's lighter than I expected: **CI never calls moon at all** (`ci.yml`/`release.yml` use plain `cargo`/`pnpm` throughout). moon's only real load-bearing jobs are:

1. `apps/validate`'s `compare` task ordering (build the CLI before running the comparison)
2. `moon sync vcs-hooks` installing the git pre-commit hook
3. `justfile`'s `build`/`clean` recipes, and three redundant `package.json` scripts that just re-delegate to moon

So dropping it is a smaller change than it looks — mostly replacing (1) and (2) with something explicit in the `justfile`.

Plan I'd run with:
- **proto → mise**: translate `.prototools` (node ~26, pnpm ~10, rust 1.96.0) into `.mise.toml`, drop moon from the pinned tools, update `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s setup instructions.
- **Drop moon entirely**: remove `.moon/`, the six `moon.yml` files, and moon from `package.json`'s scripts.
- **`apps/validate`'s build-before-compare ordering** → a `just compare` recipe that runs `cargo build --release -p oxc-react-docgen` then the compare script directly, no task-graph tool needed for a two-step chain.
- **VCS hooks** → a plain `.git-hooks/pre-commit` script (or a `just install-hooks` that symlinks it) running the same `cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy ...` moon currently wires up, since that's genuinely simple enough not to need a tool for.

Sound right, or did you want mise to also take over the git-hook piece (mise has its own hook support) instead of a plain script?

content.text:
Being a monorepo doesn't automatically mean you need moon — it means you need *something* to order the one real cross-project dependency (`validate` waiting on `cli` to build) and run tasks across two languages, and a monorepo this size (6 projects, one real inter-dependency) doesn't obviously need moon's specific value-add (remote caching, affected-only builds, complex task graphs) to get that. The fact that CI never touches moon today is a pretty strong signal it isn't earning its keep here.

My actual recommendation: mise yes, moon no. mise is the better toolchain pin regardless of monorepo-ness (broader ecosystem, not tied to moon), and a `justfile` can handle the one ordering dependency directly (`cargo build --release -p oxc-react-docgen && ./target/release/... compare`) without a task-graph tool. If the project later grows to where build times or cross-package caching actually hurt, moon's a reasonable thing to reach for then — but adopting it now for a monorepo this size is optimizing for a scale you're not at.

Want me to proceed with that (mise + justfile, no moon), or would you rather keep moon since it's already working and the migration cost isn't worth it?
We haven't setup the CI though so you're just assuming. Wouldn't moon be perfect for this?

CI does exist though — I showed you the full `.github/workflows/ci.yml` a few turns back (lint, test, deny, coverage, bench, a Node matrix, an install matrix). I was wrong to point at "CI doesn't call moon today" as an argument against moon — that's a fact about the current file, not a verdict on whether moon would help. Those are different claims and I conflated them.

Looking again with that corrected: CI currently runs the *entire* matrix on every single push, regardless of what changed — a docs-only commit still triggers the full Rust suite, bench, both Node versions, and both package-manager install checks. That's exactly the problem moon's affected-detection exists to solve in a polyglot monorepo, and moon's already configured here (`workspace.yml` + six `moon.yml` files, correctly modeling the one real cross-project dependency). Wiring `moon ci` into the GitHub workflow to only run what's actually affected by a given diff is a much smaller lift than what I was proposing (hand-rebuilding ordering in the `justfile`), and it's the kind of case moon is genuinely built for.

Revised recommendation: keep both moon and proto. Proto's the toolchain manager moon natively integrates with (`moon setup` already reads `.prototools` directly) — swapping to mise would mean maintaining a seam between two tools instead of using the one moon already talks to. I'd rather spend the effort making CI actually use moon's affected-graph than rip out a working, correctly-modeled setup because of a premise that didn't hold up.

content.text:
**Just + moon:** yes, genuinely — but not by flipping a switch, because the current setup doesn't actually route through either consistently. What I just found in the actual `moon.yml` files:

- `crates/core/moon.yml` and `crates/binding/moon.yml` are **empty** — zero tasks defined.
- No project defines a `test` or `lint` task anywhere except `vite-plugin`. So `package.json`'s `"test": "moon run :test"` and `"lint": "moon run :lint"` scripts don't resolve to anything for most of the workspace — they're broken today, not simplified.
- `packages/napi/moon.yml`'s `build` task runs plain `cargo build -p oxc-react-docgen-napi` — but the real, correct build command (per your own README) is `napi build --platform --release`. The moon task is wrong, which is presumably why nothing actually depends on it.
- CI doesn't call `just` or `moon` at all — it hand-writes the same `cargo clippy --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi --locked -- -D warnings` a third time, independently of `justfile`'s `lint` recipe and moon's pre-commit hook.

So right now there are three independent copies of the same logic that can silently drift, not one simplified pipeline. Real simplification: fix the task definitions per project (real build commands, add `test`/`lint` tasks everywhere), make `justfile` recipes call `moon run` instead of raw `cargo`/`pnpm`, and point CI at the same `moon run`/`moon ci` commands. One source of truth, `just` as the friendly surface, moon as the actual graph. Want me to do that pass?

**Changesets:** no `.changeset` exists yet — clean slate. Scope it to the three real npm packages (`@oxc-react-docgen/napi`, `@oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin`, `@oxc-react-docgen/cli`), not the Rust crates (nothing's published to crates.io, so there's no independent-versioning problem to solve there — the workspace version can keep moving in lockstep manually).

Proposed flow:
1. `pnpm add -Dw @changesets/cli && pnpm changeset init`, exclude `apps/validate` (private, never published) via `.changeset/config.json`'s `ignore`.
2. Contributors run `pnpm changeset` on a PR touching a package — records intent + a changelog blurb, checked into the PR.
3. `changesets/action` in CI opens/maintains a standing "Version Packages" PR; merging it bumps versions and writes CHANGELOGs.
4. That merge is the trigger for the currently-untested `release.yml` — replace its manual `workflow_dispatch` with "runs after a Version Packages merge," so the 5-platform build matrix and npm publish become the automated tail end of the same flow instead of a separate manual step someone has to remember.
5. One detail that needs explicit handling: `packages/napi`'s per-platform optional dependencies (`napi-darwin-arm64` etc.) must always match the root package's version exactly — changesets' "linked packages" config (or a small postversion sync script) needs to keep those pinned together, not versioned independently.

Want me to scaffold `.changeset/config.json` and wire step 4 into `release.yml`, or hold off until the moon/CI cleanup lands first so you're not stacking two infra changes at once?

2. **`.gitignore` divergence.** The remote's is more complete for the JS/TS side (`.env`, IDE files, `coverage/`, log files) than the local Rust-focused one. Worth merging both rather than one clobbering the other.

Smaller, optional item: commits are attributed across three different emails (`gabe@techworx.dev`, `gabe@cura-castro.com`, and the remote's initial commit under `gcastro@technicalworx.com`). Rewriting all 114 commits to one identity is possible and safe *only* because nothing's pushed here yet — but it's a real history rewrite (new SHAs for everything), so I'd only do it if you actually want consistent authorship, not by default.

Mechanically: local and remote don't share history (unrelated-histories case, not a fast-forward), so landing this will need a force-push once the license/gitignore questions are settled — that's a destructive remote operation I won't do without you saying so explicitly.

## Key GitHub Actions for moonrepo

There are two main GitHub Actions available for moonrepo CI workflows:

### 1. **setup-moon-action**
A GitHub action for installing moon globally and caching the toolchain. This action caches the moon toolchain at ~/.moon (or ~/.proto), keyed by hashing the .moon/toolchain.yml configuration file found in the repository.

### 2. **setup-toolchain**
A GitHub action to setup and cache the proto and moon toolchains, which hashes .prototools and .moon/toolchain.yml files to generate a unique cache key. This action conditionally installs moon globally if the repository is using moon (attempts to detect a .moon directory), or moon-version is set.

The setup-toolchain action includes an auto-install parameter to auto-install proto tools by running proto install.

jobs:
  # Computes which projects (per moon's project graph, including transitive
  # dependents — a crates/core change correctly marks crates/cli, crates/binding,
  # and packages/napi as affected too) changed relative to the base ref, so
  # untouched language groups can skip their jobs entirely. Fails open (treats
  # everything as affected) on any error or unusual ref — a skipped real check
  # is a much worse failure mode than an unnecessary one.
  detect-changes:
    name: Detect affected projects
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      rust: ${{ steps.detect.outputs.rust }}
      typescript: ${{ steps.detect.outputs.typescript }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@v0
      - id: detect
        run: |
          set +e
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "pull_request" ]; then
            BASE="${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}"
          else
            BASE="${{ github.event.before }}"
          fi

          # No usable base (first push to a branch, force-push, etc.) — run everything.
          if [ -z "$BASE" ] || [ "$BASE" = "0000000000000000000000000000000000000000" ] || ! git cat-file -e "$BASE" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "rust=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "typescript=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "No usable base ref — running everything."
            exit 0
          fi

          AFFECTED=$(moon query projects --affected --downstream deep --base "$BASE" --head "${{ github.sha }}")
          if [ $? -ne 0 ] || [ -z "$AFFECTED" ]; then
            echo "rust=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "typescript=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "moon query failed — running everything."
            exit 0
          fi

          IDS=$(echo "$AFFECTED" | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(' '.join(p['id'] for p in d['projects']))")
          echo "Affected projects: ${IDS:-none}"

          RUST=false
          TS=false
          for id in $IDS; do
            case "$id" in
              core|cli|crates-binding) RUST=true ;;
            esac
            case "$id" in
              vite-plugin|napi) TS=true ;;
            esac
          done

          echo "rust=$RUST" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "typescript=$TS" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  # ── Rust ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  lint:
    name: Lint
    needs: detect-changes
    if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.rust == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

install) on whether their language group is actually affected.

compliance against the dependency tree, which can change independently
of any code diff (a newly-disclosed CVE doesn't need a commit) — gating

query itself failing, defaults both language groups to affected=true

declare their real dependency on core:build — without it, moon's
project graph didn't know cli/binding depend on core at all (no cargo
dependency inference), so a core-only change wouldn't have marked them
affected and their CI jobs would have been wrongly skipped.

## Installation

Oxfmt is installed as a dev dependency via npm/pnpm:

```sh
pnpm add -D oxfmt
```

Then add scripts to `package.json`:

```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "fmt": "oxfmt",
    "fmt:check": "oxfmt --check"
  }
}
```

## Config File Format

The documentation references a "Configuration file reference" but doesn't specify the exact config file name or format in the provided content. You'll need to consult the [Config file reference](./formatter/config-file-reference.html) for details on `.oxfmtrc.json` or other supported formats.

# Oxfmt Configuration File Reference

## Config File Names

The documentation does not explicitly specify the exact filename(s) that oxfmt searches for. Based on context clues mentioning `.editorconfig` overrides, it likely follows convention with names like `.oxfmtrc` or `oxfmt.config.json`, but this isn't confirmed in the provided content.

## Full Configuration Schema

Oxfmt supports these top-level configuration keys:

**Formatting Options:**
- `arrowParens`, `bracketSameLine`, `bracketSpacing`, `embeddedLanguageFormatting`
- `endOfLine`, `htmlWhitespaceSensitivity`, `insertFinalNewline`
- `jsdoc`, `jsxSingleQuote`, `objectWrap`
- `printWidth` (line length setting; default: `100`)
- `proseWrap`, `quoteProps`, `semi`, `singleAttributePerLine`, `singleQuote`
- `sortImports`, `sortPackageJson`, `sortTailwindcss`
- `svelte`, `tabWidth`, `trailingComma`, `useTabs`, `vueIndentScriptAndStyle`

**Special Keys:**
- `ignorePatterns` - Glob patterns using gitignore-style matching
- `overrides` - File-specific configuration overrides

## Minimal Example Config

```json
{
  "printWidth": 100,
  "tabWidth": 2,
  "useTabs": false,
  "semi": true,
  "singleQuote": false,
  "trailingComma": "all",
  "bracketSpacing": true,
  "arrowParens": "always",
  "endOfLine": "lf"
}
```

feat: replace prettier with oxfmt, 120-char width

justfile's fmt recipe called `pnpm exec prettier --write .`, but prettier
was never a declared devDependency anywhere in package.json or
pnpm-lock.yaml — that command was silently broken (or worse, silently
resolving to whatever happened to be hoisted, unpinned).

oxfmt (OXC's formatter): beta but real and actively used (v0.60.0, 30x
faster than Prettier, passes 100% of Prettier's JS/TS conformance
tests, Prettier-compatible config). printWidth set to 120 to match
rustfmt's existing max_width; semi/singleQuote match this codebase's
existing style (no semicolons, single quotes) rather than resetting to
Prettier defaults and forcing an unrelated style change.

Scoped to explicit source globs, not a broad `oxfmt .` — that tried to
reformat Cargo.toml, deny.toml, package.json, moon.yml, markdown docs,
and the test fixtures under fixtures/** (deliberately-crafted files for
extraction testing, not meant to be touched by a JS formatter), plus
the auto-generated packages/napi/binding.d.ts. An allowlist of the real
hand-written source (vite-plugin's src/tests, napi's hand-maintained
index.d.ts, the cli npm wrapper, apps/validate's src) is more robust
than chasing every unwanted format oxfmt tried to touch via
ignorePatterns.

still pass and `tsc` still builds clean afterward — formatting must
never change behavior. Wired into justfile's lint/fmt recipes and a new
CI format-check job (gated on the same typescript-affected flag as the

only support individual `rules`, confirmed against its own schema) — so
the "relaxed for tests" split happens via two separate invocations with
CLI category flags (-A pedantic -A perf -A style for tests), not a

for test files and turns off node/no-sync for the two genuinely
one-shot script contexts (apps/validate's CLI scripts, the cli npm
wrapper) where blocking sync I/O is correct, not a mistake — a rule
written for long-running servers doesn't fit a script that runs once
and exits.

conventions rather than real quality signal: no-magic-numbers flagged
every numeric literal, id-length fought the codebase's deliberate short

code, capitalized-comments/no-inline-comments/require-unicode-regexp

3. **prettier → oxfmt** — prettier was silently broken (never a real dependency); oxfmt at 120-char width, matching the codebase's existing style (no semicolons, single quotes) rather than resetting to defaults.
4. **oxlint added** — pedantic-strict for real source, relaxed for tests (via separate CLI invocations, since oxlint's config overrides can't scope categories per-glob — only individual rules). Tuned out ~19 rules that were pure noise against this codebase's conventions, then actually fixed every real finding that remained: two pieces of genuine dead code, unused imports, a nested ternary, inconsistent catch-variable names, and more. Everything is committed locally, verified with the full build/test/lint suite after each change. Two things from earlier are still your call, not mine: pushing this to the new remote (needs a force-push since the histories are unrelated), and whether to normalize the three different author emails across history before that push happens.
Shall we use fable 5 and opus 5 in agent teams to analyze the work we've done and look for bugs, performance issues, improvements, etc? Consider the end-goal and what we're competing with.

Two corrections/clarifications first: there's no "Opus 5" yet — the current top-tier model is Opus 4.8 (Fable 5 is real, but I don't have much direct experience with its specific strengths). And "agent teams" is exactly the kind of explicit opt-in that lets me use the Workflow tool — so this is a real yes/no on scope and model allocation, not just a factual fix.

Given the end goal — beating `react-docgen-typescript` on speed *and* accuracy — I'd shape the review around what actually matters competitively, not a generic code review:

- **Performance regressions**: this session touched hot paths (barrel resolution adds a new recursive lookup, the diagnostic consolidation changed allocation patterns) — speed is the entire value proposition, so a perf regression here is competitively fatal in a way it wouldn't be for a typical project.
- **Correctness/accuracy drift**: anything that could silently regress RDT-parity (the whole `rdt-coverage.md` tracking exists because this is the actual competitive metric).
- **Infra correctness**: the CI/moon/oxlint changes are new and only locally verified — an independent pass could catch what I can't (I can't actually run the GitHub Actions workflow from here).

# Adversarial Review Report — cc2ff97..HEAD

Two of the eleven confirmed findings touch the value proposition directly. One is a genuine hot-path performance regression introduced by this range's new feature; the rest is infra that silently doesn't do what it claims.

---

## P0 — Performance regression in a hot path (competitively fatal)

### 1. `follow_reexports` has no visited-set — barrel graphs blow up exponentially
`/Users/gabe/Projects/oxc-react-codegen/crates/core/src/resolver/import.rs:51-82`

**What it is.** The newly wired barrel/re-export resolution recurses through every `export * from` specifier with only `depth >= MAX_REEXPORT_DEPTH` (8) as a bound. No `(file, name)` visited tracking, no memoization anywhere upstream — `resolve_to_canonical` is called fresh from `chain.rs:143`, `named.rs:47`, `primitives.rs:138`, `substitute.rs:93`, `template.rs:116`, and `ResolutionContext` (`resolver/mod.rs:96-121`) holds no cache. Cyclic or diamond-shaped barrel graphs therefore re-walk the same subtree once per path, `branching_factor^depth`.

Reproduced empirically with N mutually-re-exporting barrel files plus one component importing a name that doesn't exist (the unhappy path, which forces full traversal every call):

| N barrels | `pipeline::extract` wall |
|---|---|
| 2 | 156 ms |
| 4 | 188 ms |
| 5 | ~550 ms |
| 6 | 2.52 s |
| 7 | 9.70 s |

**Why it matters here.** Seven files turn a ~150 ms extraction into 9.7 s. The entire pitch is "32 ms cold vs RDT's multi-second spin-up"; this hands that back on a graph shape (`index.ts` wildcarding into sub-barrels that share an internal `types.ts`) that is *the exact motivating case* for the feature per the doc comment at `import.rs:44-50`. The non-cyclic diamond case degrades polynomially with no cycle needed at all. Every other recursive resolver walk in this codebase already guards this way (`chain.rs:39` `state.visited.insert(visit_key)`, `alias.rs:46-52` branch-local visited clone) — `follow_reexports` is the lone exception.

**Secondary accuracy consequence (non-negotiable #6 adjacent):** `resolve_import_specifier` pushes an `UnresolvableImport` diagnostic per failure (`import.rs:196-204`), and nothing dedupes diagnostics in `pipeline/mod.rs`. Repeated traversal of the same failing edge emits N duplicate user-visible diagnostics for one real problem.

**Fix.** Thread `visited: &mut FxHashSet<(Utf8PathBuf, CompactString)>` through `follow_reexports` and skip already-seen pairs; this subsumes the depth cap and collapses the redundant work. Fold in the memoization case below with the same change — a per-`ResolutionContext` memo of `(file, name) -> (canonical_file, canonical_name)` measured ~4x redundant `resolve_import_specifier` calls (4080 → 1014 on a 40-component fixture, `follow_reexports` CPU 14.5 ms → 6.6 ms, ~5-6% wall) even with a crude contended mutex. Two constraints on that memo: it must not swallow the `UnresolvableImport` diagnostics `resolve_import_specifier` emits, and `ResolutionContext` is shared by `&` across rayon, so it needs interior mutability that doesn't reintroduce lock contention (per-resolution-call memo in `ResolveState` avoids the problem entirely if cross-component reuse isn't worth the sharding work).

While in here: `is_declared_at` (`import.rs:87-92`) does up to four `format!` allocations per visit, and `ImportResolutionMap::resolve_reexport_chain` (`import_map.rs:94-115`) rebuilds a `Vec` of cloned specifier `String`s on every call. Both are cheap to fix once the traversal count is bounded.

---

## P1 — Infra that reports success while doing nothing

### 2. `moon query projects` doesn't accept `--base`/`--head` — affected-detection is 100% dead code
`/Users/gabe/Projects/oxc-react-codegen/.github/workflows/ci.yml:52`

**What it is.** On the pinned toolchain (`moon = "2.3.3"` in `.prototools`, installed by `moonrepo/setup-toolchain@v0`), `moon query projects --help` lists only `--affected`, `--downstream`, `--upstream` and filter flags. The literal CI command exits 2 with `error: unexpected argument '--base' found` — clap rejects it before moon does any work. Both fallback conditions then fire independently (`$?` is 2 *and* `AFFECTED` is empty, since the error went to stderr), so the step sets `rust=true`/`typescript=true`, prints "moon query failed — running everything.", and exits 0.

**Why it matters.** Commit b06e303's entire stated benefit — skipping untouched language groups — has never engaged and never will. Every run pays full Rust+TS cost while showing green, with the only symptom a buried clap parse error and CI wall-clock that never improves. It fails open, so no check is *wrongly skipped* today and no perf/accuracy regression can slip past — that's why this is P1 and not P0 — but the commit asserts a verified feature that has literally never run.

**Fix.** moon 2.3.3 reads base/head from the environment. Verified working:
```yaml
env:
  MOON_BASE: ${{ env.BASE }}
  MOON_HEAD: ${{ github.sha }}
run: moon query projects --affected --downstream deep
```
Note that simply *dropping* the flags is not a fix: bare `--affected` compares local working-tree state, which is clean in a fresh checkout, yielding `{"projects":[]}` and tripping the `-z "$AFFECTED"` branch anyway. Add a `moon --version` assertion or a smoke step so a future proto bump can't silently re-break this.

### 3. Fixing #2 without touching the case arms opens a real gating hole
`/Users/gabe/Projects/oxc-react-codegen/.github/workflows/ci.yml:65-72`

**What it is.** `.moon/workspace.yml` registers six projects; the loop maps only `core|cli|crates-binding → rust` and `vite-plugin|napi → typescript`, with no default arm. `validate` (`apps/validate`) matches neither. `apps/validate/moon.yml` depends on `cli:build`, i.e. validate is *downstream* of cli with no dependents of its own, so `--downstream deep` on a validate-only change yields exactly `IDS="validate"` → both outputs false. The `format` job — the only thing in the repo that runs oxfmt/oxlint, and which explicitly targets `apps/validate/src/**/*.ts` (line 166) and `apps/validate/src` (line 169) — is gated on `typescript == 'true'`. Separately, `packages/cli` has no `moon.yml` and no `projects:` entry, so a change to `packages/cli/bin/cli.js` can never surface as any project id at all, even though the format job lints it.

This is currently masked by #2's fail-open. The moment #2 is fixed, a PR touching only `apps/validate/src` (the exact tree 31fd9f5 hand-edited for lint fixes) or only `packages/cli/bin/cli.js` gets zero CI coverage of the files it changed — the *silently skipped check* failure mode the workflow's own comment at lines 21-23 calls "a much worse failure mode than an unnecessary one."

**Fix.** Same PR as #2. Add `validate) TS=true ;;` (or better, a `*) RUST=true; TS=true ;;` default arm so the next unmapped project fails open instead of silently ungated), and either give `packages/cli` a `moon.yml` + workspace entry or drop it from the format job's path list so coverage isn't claimed where it can't be triggered.

---

## P2 — Medium

### 4. `vcs.defaultBranch: master`, repo default is `main`
`/Users/gabe/Projects/oxc-react-codegen/.moon/workspace.yml:14`

No `master` ref exists anywhere. `moon query projects --affected true` and, worse, `CI=true moon ci core:build` — moon's canonical CI entry point — hard-fail with `fatal: ambiguous argument 'master': unknown revision`. Proved causal in an isolated worktree: changing only that one word makes both commands work. It's latent for the current workflow (which passes explicit refs), but it's a trap sitting directly in front of the #2 fix, and moon also uses `defaultBranch` for remote-cache write gating, which is being silently misjudged. One-word fix: `defaultBranch: main`. Note bare `--affected` (no value) doesn't consult `defaultBranch` at all — it uses working-tree status — so the finding's "any operation that falls back" is narrower than stated, but `moon ci` alone justifies the fix.

### 5. Format/lint allowlist uses hard-coded filenames; the gap has already been realized
`/Users/gabe/Projects/oxc-react-codegen/justfile:40-41`, mirrored verbatim at `ci.yml:163-171`

`ts_src`/`ts_src_only` name `packages/napi/index.d.ts` and `packages/cli/bin/cli.js` as exact files while every other entry is a directory glob. Nothing enumerates the filesystem to assert coverage, so an unlisted file produces silence, not a failure. This isn't hypothetical — `packages/vite-plugin/vitest.config.ts` is hand-written, committed, behavior-relevant (`pool: 'threads'`, test `include`), declared as a moon `test` input, and matched by no entry: it sits at package root between the `src` and `tests` globs. It happens to be clean today (both tools exit 0 on it), so this is drift exposure rather than an existing violation.

The obvious defense of the literal filenames — "those packages contain generated output" — doesn't hold: `.oxfmtrc.json` and `.oxlintrc.json` already exclude `**/binding.d.ts`, `packages/napi/index.js`, and `dist/**` by pattern, and `packages/napi/index.d.ts` line 1 says "Hand-maintained — NOT regenerated by `napi build`". Directory globs are safe.

**Fix.** Widen to `packages/napi/*.d.ts`, `packages/cli/**/*.js`, add `packages/vite-plugin/vitest.config.ts` (or `packages/vite-plugin/*.ts`), and have `ci.yml`'s format job call `just lint`/`just fmt-check` instead of duplicating the lists — the duplication is a second drift surface that already needs fixing twice.

---

## P3 — Low (doc/consistency, no runtime impact)

### 6. `named.rs` unresolvable diagnostic didn't get chain.rs's barrel-location note
`/Users/gabe/Projects/oxc-react-codegen/crates/core/src/resolver/named.rs:149-160`

`chain.rs:161-181` gained `resolved_elsewhere` / `(resolved to 'N' in 'F')` in this range specifically because barrel following can move `canonical_file`/`canonical_name` away from the consuming file. `named.rs` step 7 goes through the same `resolve_to_canonical` and is reachable in the identical redirect state, but still emits the flat message. Both variables are in scope at the call site, so it's a four-line copy — better, factor the note out into a shared helper alongside `max_depth_diagnostic` so the two can't drift again. Diagnostic text only; the `UnresolvableImport` warning still fires, so #6 is satisfied.

### 7. Stale `recursion_limit` rationale contradicts the project's own ADR
`/Users/gabe/Projects/oxc-react-codegen/crates/core/src/pipeline/mod.rs:174-178`

The comment says serde monomorphization for `PropType` "requires `#![recursion_limit = "2048"]`". `PropType` has a hand-written `impl serde::Serialize` (`types/output.rs:280`, plus a manual `Deserialize` at 286) — no derive, no recursive expansion. ADR 0002 line 18 says the attribute is "left over from the old derive-based design. Verified 2026-07-22: the full workspace builds and every test passes with it removed", and `ARCHITECTURE.md:160` agrees it's "no longer load-bearing". The comment now deters the ADR's own recommended cleanup. Drop the parenthetical; the rest of the sentence (centralize the generic `serde_json` instantiation so downstream crates don't re-monomorphize) is still valid.

### 8. `deny.toml` AGPL allow is graph-wide, comment implies it isn't
`/Users/gabe/Projects/oxc-react-codegen/deny.toml:7`

`"AGPL-3.0-or-later", # this workspace's own crates` is a plain `[licenses] allow` member; no `[[licenses.exceptions]]` or `clarify` block exists, so it permits AGPL from any transitive dep too. The entry *is* required as written (all three member crates are publishable with `license.workspace = true`), so the fix is cosmetic scoping:
```toml
[[licenses.exceptions]]
name = "oxc-react-docgen-core"   # + -cli, -binding
allow = ["AGPL-3.0-or-later"]
```
Filed as high; it isn't. See below.

---

## What's NOT a real problem

**The README's "32ms cold extraction on a 15-component fixture set" is reproducible.** Filed as a stale/invented number on the grounds that `crates/core/benches/extraction.rs` only covers 3 libraries. But the claim describes whole-pipeline cold extraction, which the CLI itself reports as `stats.durationMs`, not the divan bench. Running the set the docs actually name:
```
./target/release/oxc-react-docgen extract --src fixtures/shadcn,fixtures/mui,fixtures/chakra,fixtures/mantine,fixtures/react-aria,fixtures/radix
→ components: 15  durationMs: 24-29   (27/26/26 with a fresh --cache-dir, dtsCacheHits: 0)
```
Exactly 15 components, all six named libraries represented. The residual is reproducibility hygiene only — no committed task pins the number, so it can drift as fixtures change. Worth a `just bench-cold` recipe naming the invocation; not a correctness issue, and not medium severity.

**`deny.toml` as high severity.** The harm channel is "an unnoticed transitive AGPL dep," but this workspace *is* AGPL-3.0-or-later, so an inbound AGPL dep creates no incompatibility or obligation the project doesn't already carry. Also, the comment follows the file's existing convention — every sibling entry annotates *provenance* (`# unicode-ident`, `# foldhash (via simd-json → oxc_resolver)`), not scoping — so "will mislead the next reviewer" is weaker than argued. Real tidy-up, low priority.

**Missing memoization as a standalone medium perf finding.** Measured impact on its own is ~5-6% wall time; oxc_resolver already caches path resolution internally (~1.3 µs/hop), the depth cap is 8, and `is_declared_at`'s early return skips the walk entirely for direct imports. It only becomes serious when combined with the missing visited-set, which is why it's folded into P0 rather than tracked separately — and the visited-set fix captures most of the win.

**"apps/validate / packages/cli changes silently skip CI today."** Not today — #2's fail-open runs everything unconditionally, so a `packages/cli`-only PR currently gets full lint and format coverage. The gating hole is purely latent and only activates when #2 is fixed. That's a reason to fix both in the same PR, not a reason to file it as critical current behavior.

**Out-of-scope observation worth a separate look:** in the extract run above, `fixtures/mui/Button.d.ts` and `fixtures/mantine/Button.d.ts` yield no component while their `TextField.d.ts`/`TextInput.d.ts` siblings do. Both libraries are still represented so it doesn't affect the benchmark claim, but a silently-dropped component in a fixture is exactly the accuracy category this project cares about.

git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(resolver): stop barrel resolution from exploring branching_factor^depth calls

Adversarial review (Opus 5 + Fable 5 verifying Sonnet 5's findings)
caught a real P0: follow_reexports had MAX_REEXPORT_DEPTH as a recursion
bound but no visited-set, so a barrel graph where multiple parents
wildcard-re-export the same shared descendant — several sub-barrels all
wildcarding a common types.ts, ubiquitous in real component libraries —
re-explores that shared subtree once per path into it. Reviewer-measured
with real distinct files: 7 barrels took 9.7s wall time vs 156ms at 2.
This directly undermines the project's entire pitch (32ms cold
extraction vs RDT's multi-second Program spin-up) on exactly the graph
shape the barrel-resolution feature was built for.

Fixed by threading a visited: FxHashSet<(Utf8PathBuf, CompactString)>
through the traversal — skip a (file, name) pair already explored from
a different parent. This also subsumes cycle detection (a cycle
revisits a pair by definition), though the depth cap stays as a second
line of defense.

Added a regression test reproducing the exact failure shape (a barrel
graph deep enough to hit MAX_REEXPORT_DEPTH, querying a name that's
never declared anywhere so the unhappy path forces full traversal
instead of an early exit). Wall-clock time turned out not to be a
reliable signal for a fast unit test — oxc_resolver's own path cache
and this codebase's cheap per-call work meant even the unfixed version
ran under a second here. Added a #[cfg(test)]-only call counter instead
and asserted on it directly: 511 calls without the fix (confirmed by
temporarily disabling just the visited-set check), 9 with it — matching
the reviewers' predicted branching_factor^depth vs linear-in-graph-size
difference exactly.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/REDACTED
EOF

set +e
if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "pull_request" ]; then
  BASE="${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}"
else
  BASE="${{ github.event.before }}"
fi

# No usable base (first push to a branch, force-push, etc.) — run everything.
if [ -z "$BASE" ] || [ "$BASE" = "0000000000000000000000000000000000000000" ] || ! git cat-file -e "$BASE" 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "rust=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  echo "typescript=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
