# Public-Facing Go API for TypeScript: Discussion Summary

## Current Proposal Shape

The discussion lacks a formally proposed API shape. Instead, community members are requesting **any** accessible surface, with several suggesting an unstable/experimental approach:

- One developer noted: "An `unstable/` or `x/` passthrough that re-exports what people already reach for would do, with a doc comment saying it breaks whenever"
- Current workarounds involve `go:linkname` shims to access internal packages, indicating demand exists regardless of official support

## Confirmed Status

**Officially planned:** Jake Bailey (collaborator) confirmed in July 2026 that the team "are going to do it when we move the repo back to github.com/microsoft/TypeScript"

**Current reality:** All compiler functionality lives in `internal` packages, making external use impossible through normal imports.

## What Remains Undecided

- Specific API surface and stability guarantees
- Versioning strategy (Go's semver expectations conflict with TypeScript's versioning)
- Whether to provide C ABI bindings (dismissed as "doubling the size")

## Timeline

Bailey stated a possible timeline of "before 7.1" for exposure once the repository merges back to the main TypeScript project, though obstacles around existing tags need resolution first.

content.text:
Status: it's coming, but still loosely defined, and the timeline is "aim for 7.1" not "committed for 7.1."

**Release timeline:** No 7.1 date yet, but going by TypeScript's usual 3-4 month cadence off the 2026-07-08 GA of 7.0, expect roughly **October 2026**.

**What 7.1 is actually supposed to fix:** the missing stable programmatic API. 7.0 shipped with none — the old JS-based Language Service API surface isn't being carried forward at all, and Microsoft has said 7.1's API will be "new and different," not a port of the old one. This is why Vue/Volar, Angular template checking, Svelte, Astro, and MDX tooling are all stuck on TypeScript 6 right now — they embed the compiler programmatically and have nothing to embed against on 7.

**The Go-side API discussion (microsoft/typescript-go#481)** is where the real design conversation lives, and it's less settled than the marketing "7.1 will have an API" framing suggests:

- Everything compiler-internal currently sits in Go `internal/` packages — unreachable from outside the module by Go's own language rules. Today's only access path is the same `go:linkname` hack tsgolint uses (reaching into unexported symbols), which the team itself calls unsupported.
- Jake Bailey (Microsoft, works on the port) confirmed in July 2026 the team **will** expose something, but tied it to an infrastructure step first: moving the `typescript-go` repo back into `microsoft/TypeScript` proper. His stated target was "before 7.1" — a goal, not a shipped commitment — and he flagged unresolved mechanics (existing git tags, versioning scheme) blocking even that repo merge.
- No settled API shape yet. Community ask is mostly "just give us an `unstable/`-prefixed passthrough of what we're already reaching for via linkname, documented as breaking anytime" rather than a fully-designed stable contract.
- A C ABI binding (which would matter more to us than a Go-only API, since we're Rust) was explicitly discussed and dismissed for now — one commenter noted it'd double binary size, no counter-proposal offered.
- Go's own semver expectations vs. TypeScript's release versioning are flagged as an open, unresolved tension — i.e., even the *versioning strategy* for a future Go API isn't decided.

Net for us: even optimistically, "7.1 has a real API" is Microsoft's stated intent, not a locked scope — and there's no signal yet of a C-ABI or FFI-friendly surface, which is the part that would actually matter for embedding from Rust rather than Go. Worth checking back closer to October, but not something to plan the `composes` gap around yet.

Sources:
- [Potential Public-Facing Go API for Embedding? · Discussion #481](https://github.com/microsoft/typescript-go/discussions/481)
- [TypeScript 7 Now Stable: 10× Faster Builds, But Not for Vue or Svelte Yet](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/320049/20260710/typescript-7-now-stable-10-faster-builds-not-vue-svelte-yet.htm)
- [Announcing TypeScript 7.0 RC](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-7-0-rc/)

Let’s go through our spec and codebase and understand not just our happy path but our edge cases.
We don’t always do a good job of planning for edge cases, failure cases, errors, etc.
Let’s be very intentional and comprehensively understand and document these states so we can identify gaps and bugs.

I'll start by mapping the codebase structure and existing spec docs, then fan out targeted audits across the major subsystems (extractor, resolver, pipeline, cache, CLI) to catalog edge cases and gaps systematically.

input.prompt:
We're doing a comprehensive edge-case/failure-mode audit of oxc-react-docgen (a Rust tool that parses TSX/TS with OXC and extracts React component prop metadata, a drop-in replacement for react-docgen-typescript). This is research/documentation only — do NOT modify any code.

Your scope: the extractor subsystem in crates/core/src/extractor/ (mod.rs, component.rs, alias.rs, interface.rs, jsdoc.rs, defaults.rs, visit.rs) and crates/core/src/types/collected.rs. This is the OXC AST visitor layer: it walks parsed TSX/TS source and produces `SourceData` (component declarations, prop-relevant type declarations, JSDoc, default values) before any cross-file resolution happens.

Project non-negotiables (from CLAUDE.md) you should check adherence to: no `unwrap()` outside `#[cfg(test)]` (must use `?`), no AST refs escape `parse_file()` (allocator is local per call), always emit a `Diagnostic` when degrading instead of failing silently.

For each source file in scope, identify:
1. **Component detection edge cases**: unusual ways a React component can be declared/exported that the visitor might miss or mishandle — e.g. `export default function() {}` (anonymous), `export default memo(forwardRef(...))`, HOC-wrapped components, components defined via `Object.assign`, components as class expressions vs class declarations, components exported via `export { X as Y }` or `export * from`, components with no props param, components using `React.FC<Props>` vs plain function typing, generic components (`function Comp<T>(props: Props<T>)`), components declared in .ts (not .tsx) files, multiple components per file, components with the same name in different files.
2. **Prop-type declaration parsing edge cases**: interfaces vs type aliases vs inline object literals, intersections/unions of many members, recursive/self-referential types, generic type parameters with defaults or constraints, mapped types, conditional types, template literal types, `as const`, satisfies expressions, re-exported types from other files, namespaced types (`Foo.Bar`), ambient/declare types.
3. **JSDoc parsing edge cases**: malformed or partial JSDoc, `@default` tag variants, multi-line descriptions, JSDoc on re-exported/aliased types, missing JSDoc, JSDoc with unusual tag ordering, block comments that look like JSDoc but aren't (`/** */` on unrelated code).
4. **Default value extraction edge cases**: destructured defaults (`{ foo = 'bar' }`), defaultProps static property (legacy class components), complex default expressions (function calls, spread, ternaries), defaults referencing outer-scope variables/constants.
5. **Panic/crash risks**: any indexing, slicing, `.unwrap()`, `.expect()`, arithmetic that isn't behind a bounds/overflow check, when walking malformed or adversarial ASTs (e.g. deeply nested types causing stack overflow via recursion, extremely large files).
6. **Silent failure risks**: places where a parse/extraction failure would just skip data with no `Diagnostic` emitted, violating the "always emit Diagnostic when degrading" rule.

For each finding, note: exact file:line, whether existing tests in crates/core/tests/ or inline #[cfg(test)] modules already cover it (search first), and severity (crash risk / silent data loss / known-and-documented limitation / cosmetic).

Report as a structured list grouped by category (1-6 above). Be concrete — cite code, don't speculate abstractly. Aim for thoroughness over brevity; this feeds a comprehensive gap-tracking document. Under 2500 words.

input.name: audit-resolver
input.prompt:
We're doing a comprehensive edge-case/failure-mode audit of oxc-react-docgen (a Rust tool that parses TSX/TS with OXC and extracts React component prop metadata, a drop-in replacement for react-docgen-typescript). This is research/documentation only — do NOT modify any code.

Your scope: the resolver subsystem in crates/core/src/resolver/ (mod.rs, chain.rs, alias.rs, collected.rs, extends.rs, func.rs, html.rs, import.rs, named.rs, primitives.rs, react.rs, substitute.rs, template.rs). This layer takes `SourceData` + `GlobalSourceData` (all files merged) and resolves a component's props type into a final `ComponentEntry` — this is where generic substitution, intersection/union merging, cross-file type-alias following, and "give up gracefully" logic (composes, opaque types) lives. `ResolveState` in mod.rs accumulates diagnostics and visited-type tracking per resolution call and is NOT shared across threads (resolve_component runs in parallel via rayon, per crates/core/CLAUDE.md).

Project non-negotiables (CLAUDE.md): no `unwrap()` outside tests, `FxHashMap`/`BTreeMap` used correctly, always emit a `Diagnostic` when degrading rather than failing silently. Note: `ResolvedChain::empty_with_compose()` is the established pattern for "give up but record what we know" — check whether all give-up paths use it consistently or whether some still return `ResolvedChain::default()` silently (this was a real bug found and partially fixed recently — check if other similar dead ends remain).

For each source file in scope, identify:
1. **Cycle / infinite recursion risks**: self-referential types (`type Tree = { children: Tree[] }`), mutually recursive types (A references B references A), circular imports across files, generic types instantiated with themselves. Does `ResolveState`'s visited-type tracking actually prevent infinite loops in all these cases, or only some? Look for recursion depth limits or lack thereof — could a pathological/adversarial type definition cause a stack overflow or hang?
2. **Generic substitution edge cases**: generics with multiple type parameters, generics with constraints (`T extends Foo`), generics with defaults, partial application, generic type aliases used without type arguments, higher-kinded-ish patterns (generic type referencing another generic), `Props<'button', Options>`-style utility patterns (relevant: earlier work found Ariakit's pattern isn't matched at all — check current state).
3. **Intersection/union merging edge cases**: conflicting prop types across union members, optional vs required conflicts, deeply nested intersections, unions of 20+ literal members, discriminated unions where the discriminant itself is computed/generic.
4. **Cross-file/cross-package resolution edge cases**: types imported from node_modules .d.ts files, types re-exported through multiple hops (A imports from B imports from C), circular file imports, missing/unresolvable imports (typo'd import, deleted file), ambient global types with no import at all.
5. **"Give up gracefully" consistency**: enumerate every place the resolver returns an empty/default chain or otherwise gives up (grep for `ResolvedChain::default()`, early returns, etc.) and check whether each one records a Diagnostic and/or populates `composes` — flag any that silently vanish.
6. **Panic/crash risks**: unwrap/expect/indexing/arithmetic in hot paths, especially under adversarial or malformed type graphs.

For each finding: exact file:line, whether existing tests already cover it (check crates/core/tests/ and inline test modules first), severity (crash/hang risk, silent data loss, known documented limitation per docs/rdt-coverage.md or docs/type-checker-integration.md, or cosmetic).

Report as a structured list grouped by category (1-6). Be concrete, cite code. Under 2800 words.

input.description: Audit pipeline, cache, import_map edge cases
input.name: audit-pipeline
input.prompt:
We're doing a comprehensive edge-case/failure-mode audit of oxc-react-docgen (a Rust tool that parses TSX/TS with OXC and extracts React component prop metadata, a drop-in replacement for react-docgen-typescript). This is research/documentation only — do NOT modify any code.

Your scope: crates/core/src/pipeline/mod.rs, crates/core/src/pipeline/discover.rs, crates/core/src/pipeline/watch.rs, crates/core/src/cache.rs, crates/core/src/import_map.rs. This is file discovery → parallel parse (rayon) → merge into GlobalSourceData → parallel resolve → dedup/collision handling → ExtractionOutput, plus the DTS parse cache (mtime+size invalidation, msgpack, atomic temp-file swap, 5000-entry eviction cap per docs/STATUS.md) and watch mode (file-system event handling).

Project non-negotiables (CLAUDE.md): no `unwrap()` outside tests, always emit Diagnostic on degrade, FxHashMap internal / BTreeMap for JSON output.

Identify edge cases and failure modes in:
1. **File discovery**: symlink loops, permission-denied directories/files, non-UTF8 filenames or paths, extremely deep directory nesting, empty src_dirs, src_dirs that don't exist, glob/ignore pattern edge cases (node_modules exclusion, .gitignore respect or not), case-insensitive filesystem collisions (Foo.tsx vs foo.tsx on macOS), files that change between discovery and read (TOCTOU).
2. **Parallel parse/merge (rayon)**: what happens if one file panics mid-parse — does it poison the whole batch or degrade gracefully per-file? Race conditions in merging into GlobalSourceData. Determinism: does parallel execution produce the same output every run (important for caching/snapshot tests), or could iteration order cause nondeterminism in diagnostics ordering, component dedup winner selection, etc.?
3. **Component name collisions / dedup**: same component name in different files (recently fixed per git history — verify current dedup key logic in mod.rs's extract() function is actually collision-proof; check the exact key construction), same file processed twice, case-sensitivity issues.
4. **Cache subsystem** (cache.rs): what happens on a corrupted cache file (partial write from a crash, wrong msgpack version, disk full during atomic swap), concurrent processes sharing the same cache dir, cache dir on read-only filesystem, mtime granularity issues (some filesystems have 1s mtime resolution — could a fast edit+rebuild within the same second get a stale cache hit?), eviction correctness at exactly 5000 entries, negative/zero-size files.
5. **Cross-package .d.ts resolution / import_map.rs**: package.json parsing edge cases (missing, malformed, no "types"/"typings" field, exports map complexity), monorepo workspace symlinks (pnpm/yarn), circular package dependencies, missing node_modules entirely.
6. **Watch mode** (watch.rs): rapid successive file changes (debounce correctness), file deleted while being processed, editor atomic-save patterns (write to temp file + rename — does the watcher see the right final file?), watch mode + cache interaction correctness.
7. **Panic/crash risks**: unwrap/expect/indexing/arithmetic, especially any that could be triggered by filesystem state outside the tool's control (untrusted/adversarial input isn't the threat model here, but real-world messy filesystems are).

For each finding: exact file:line, whether existing tests already cover it (check crates/core/tests/ first), severity. Report grouped by category 1-7, concrete with code citations. Under 2800 words.

input.description: Audit CLI and config edge cases
input.name: audit-cli
input.prompt:
We're doing a comprehensive edge-case/failure-mode audit of oxc-react-docgen (a Rust tool that parses TSX/TS with OXC and extracts React component prop metadata, a drop-in replacement for react-docgen-typescript). This is research/documentation only — do NOT modify any code.

Your scope: crates/cli/src/ (main.rs, config.rs, output.rs, commands/extract.rs, commands/check.rs, commands/completions.rs, commands/inspect.rs, commands/lsp.rs, commands/schema.rs, commands/watch.rs, commands/mod.rs) and crates/binding/src/lib.rs + crates/binding/build.rs (thin NAPI wrapper). Read crates/cli/CLAUDE.md first for the project's own rules for this crate (no println! in command handlers — output.rs/tracing only; miette for errors; config.rs runs user's docgen.config.ts via node+tsx with config path passed via env var, not shell string, specifically to avoid command injection).

Identify edge cases and failure modes in:
1. **Config loading** (config.rs): missing docgen.config.ts (should fall back to defaults — verify), malformed/syntactically-invalid config file, config file that throws at runtime, missing node or tsx on PATH, node/tsx version incompatibilities, config file with unexpected types (e.g. src as a string instead of array), extremely large config, config path with spaces/special shell characters (verify the env-var passing actually avoids injection in all code paths — check for any place that might still interpolate into a shell string), timeout/hang if the config script never exits or does something async that never resolves.
2. **CLI argument parsing** (main.rs, ExtractArgs etc.): conflicting flags, --out path that doesn't exist / isn't writable / is a directory, --format combined with --json (check documented precedence is actually enforced), invalid --react-version strings, empty --src list, --cache-dir pointing somewhere unwritable, --extra-builtins with malformed entries.
3. **Exit code correctness**: every command's exit code paths — does every error condition map to a sensible, documented exit code? Cross-check cmd_extract's error-diagnostic-severity logic (already has tests for --json exit code) against check.rs, inspect.rs, schema.rs, lsp.rs, watch.rs — do they all handle the "extraction produced Error-severity diagnostics" case consistently, or do some silently exit 0?
4. **Output writing**: what happens if --out write fails partway (disk full, permission denied) — is any partial file left behind? Does watch.rs handle repeated writes to the same --out path safely?
5. **watch.rs command**: startup behavior if the initial extraction already has errors, behavior on Ctrl-C mid-extraction, terminal output interleaving with progress indicators.
6. **lsp.rs**: malformed LSP requests, requests for files outside the configured src_dirs, hover requests on positions with no component/prop at that location, protocol errors (malformed JSON-RPC framing), what happens before the initial full extraction completes (race between "ready" and first request).
7. **schema.rs**: does the exported JSON Schema stay in sync with the actual serde output of ComponentEntry/ExtractionOutput, or could they drift silently?
8. **NAPI binding** (crates/binding): panics crossing the FFI boundary into Node (Rust panic = UB/crash in NAPI unless caught — check if there's a catch_unwind or equivalent), thread-safety of any shared state, what a Node caller sees on a Rust-side error (proper JS Error vs opaque crash).
9. **Panic/crash risks**: unwrap/expect/indexing anywhere in scope, particularly on user-controlled input (CLI args, config file contents, file paths).

For each finding: exact file:line, whether existing tests already cover it (check crates/cli/tests/ and inline test modules first — note there's now a crates/cli/tests/ directory, check what's there), severity. Report grouped by category 1-9, concrete with code citations. Under 2800 words.

We're doing a comprehensive edge-case/failure-mode audit of oxc-react-docgen (a Rust tool that parses TSX/TS with OXC and extracts React component prop metadata, a drop-in replacement for react-docgen-typescript). This is research/documentation only — do NOT modify any code.

Your scope: crates/core/src/types/ (mod.rs, output.rs, diagnostic.rs, global.rs, collected.rs), crates/core/src/plugin.rs, crates/core/src/toon.rs, crates/core/src/react_types.rs, crates/core/src/known.rs, and the RDT/storybook serialization functions in crates/cli/src/commands/extract.rs (serialize_rdt, serialize_storybook, rdt_type_json).

Identify edge cases and failure modes in:
1. **Serialization correctness**: prop names or type strings containing characters that could break JSON (quotes, backslashes, unicode, extremely long strings), circular references in serialized output (could a recursive type produce infinite JSON?), numeric edge cases in default values (NaN, Infinity, very large numbers as literal defaults), the RDT `enum`-shape special-casing in rdt_type_json — does it handle a `PropType::Union` mixed with non-literal members correctly, or a LiteralUnion with zero or one members?
2. **TOON format** (toon.rs): what happens with prop/type data that doesn't fit TOON's token-optimized assumptions — deeply nested structures, very large prop counts, unicode-heavy descriptions. Does it round-trip losslessly relative to canonical JSON, or is it deliberately lossy (and if lossy, is that documented)?
3. **Diagnostic type** (diagnostic.rs): are all DiagnosticCode variants actually constructible with correct severity everywhere they're used across the codebase (search other files for `DiagnosticCode::` and `DiagnosticSeverity::` usage), or are there codes defined but never emitted (dead) or emitted with clearly wrong severity?
4. **Plugin system** (plugin.rs): what happens if a plugin panics inside a hook — does it poison the whole extraction? Plugin hook ordering guarantees (if multiple plugins registered, is order deterministic?), plugins that mutate shared state unsafely, plugin hooks called on every file even when no plugins are registered (perf edge case, not correctness, but worth noting if there's needless overhead).
5. **known.rs**: the library-specific type shortcuts (SxProps, VariantProps, etc.) — what happens when a user's codebase has a *different*, same-named type that happens to collide with one of these hardcoded shortcuts (false positive opaque-type shortcut)? Is this documented as a known tradeoff?
6. **react_types.rs**: React builtin recognition — coverage gaps for newer React APIs (e.g. `use()`, Server Components-specific types, `ForwardedRef` variants), HTML element attribute mapping completeness (recently touched per git history for SVGAttributes/HTMLProps — check current state for remaining gaps), case sensitivity issues in element name matching.
7. **Output types** (types/output.rs, types/global.rs): any field that can be in an inconsistent state relative to another field (e.g. `required: true` combined with a `default_value` present — contradictory prop state; does anything validate against this, or can the resolver produce it?).
8. **Panic/crash risks**: unwrap/expect/indexing in scope.

For each finding: exact file:line, whether existing tests already cover it, severity. Report grouped by category 1-8, concrete with code citations. Under 2500 words.

Resolver audit (crates/core/src/resolver/*.rs). No code modified. All unwrap/expect confirmed test-only (mod.rs tests, react.rs tests) — non-negotiable #1 holds in production paths.

## 1. Cycle / recursion
- Chain-level cycle guard: `chain.rs:38-41` builds `visited` key `"{file}:{name}<{args}>"` (includes type_args, fixed after the Blueprint `Partial<RowHeights>`/`Partial<ColumnWidths>` collision bug — test at mod.rs:1451). On revisit it returns **`ResolvedChain::default()` — no diagnostic, no `composes` entry** (chain.rs:40). This is the exact silent-dead-end pattern you flagged: every other give-up path in chain.rs (lines 31, 89, 126, 139, 177) uses `empty_with_compose`, but the cycle-detected return does not. A genuinely self-referential/mutually-recursive interface pair (`A extends B`, `B extends A`) silently loses props with zero trace. No test exercises this (grepped for "cycle"/"circular" test names — none exist).
- Type-level resolution (`resolve_named`, `resolve_collected_type`) has **no visited-set at all**, only the `depth > MAX_DEPTH` (20) counter (collected.rs:23, named.rs:27). Mutually-recursive named types at the type level (not chain level) recurse up to depth 20 before degrading to `Opaque{DepthExceeded}` — bounded, no stack-overflow risk, but self-referential structural types (`type Tree = {children: Tree[]}`) produce a 20-level-deep nested Object/Array before truncating, which is correct-ish but untested.
- Import re-export cycles ARE handled well: `import.rs:74-117`, `MAX_REEXPORT_DEPTH=8` + a `(file,name)` visited set that "subsumes cycle detection" (comment at import.rs:92), with dedicated call-count tests.
- Sibling-branch `state.visited.clone()` pattern (alias.rs:51-55 for `Omit<T, keyof U>`, alias.rs:274-278 for union discriminant probing) is correct for avoiding false-positive cycles between legitimately-independent branches, but means cyclic/shared subgraphs get re-walked once per branch rather than once total — bounded by MAX_DEPTH, not a hang risk, just redundant work.

## 2. Generic substitution
- Ariakit's `Props<T,O> = O & Omit<ComponentPropsWithoutRef<T>, keyof O>` is still unhandled — confirmed still true against current code (matches docs/benchmarks.md:166's documented gap; 6/10 outlier components still show empty `composes`).
- `type_args` arrive as **display strings** at the chain level; `raw_arg_to_collected_type` (substitute.rs:117-131) only parses bare identifiers and quoted literals — anything containing `<`, `|`, `&`, or a space degrades to `CollectedType::Raw` and can't be structurally substituted into a nested generic. Self-documented as a known limitation (substitute.rs:115), not silently broken, but no test covers "nested generic as a call-site argument to another generic alias" at the chain level.
- `build_substitution` (substitute.rs:33-43) `.zip()`s declared params against supplied args — if a generic alias has more declared params than the call site supplies (partial application, or a param with a default like `type Foo<T, U = T>` used as `Foo<string>`), trailing params are **silently unsubstituted** (zip just stops). No default-type-param modeling exists anywhere in `type_alias_params`. No test for partial generic application.
- Multi-level nested generic aliases (3+ levels deep) have only a 1-level-deep regression test (mod.rs test 5b / `generic_alias_with_structured_args`); deeper chains are plausible but unverified.

## 3. Intersection/union merging
- `find_discriminant_prop` (chain.rs:260) only recognizes `PropType::StringLiteral` as a discriminant candidate — a numeric-literal discriminant (`kind: 0 | 1`) or one derived from an expanded template-literal union is never detected, even though the underlying merge-into-union logic works fine for those props' *values*. Cosmetic/known-limitation-shaped, not a crash.
- Required/optional merge semantics (`record_variant_props`, alias.rs:387-409): a prop is required in the merged output only if present in every variant AND required everywhere it appears — reasonable, and covered by test_repeated_discriminant_values (mod.rs:1010).
- Non-`Named` union members (inline objects, nested intersections/unions) go through a separate second pass (alias.rs:321-333) merged into the same accumulators as the Named/discriminant-analyzed members — looks correct, no gap found.
- Unions of 20+ plain literal members (not wrapped in Named/discriminated-union machinery) go through `resolve_union` (primitives.rs:12-43), a simple flatten+dedupe-free collection — no discriminant logic invoked, appropriately, since it's just `PropType::Union`.

## 4. Cross-file / cross-package
- Re-export/barrel following: correct, tested, bounded (see #1).
- Missing/typo'd imports: `resolve_import_specifier` (import.rs:206-243) emits a `Warning` diagnostic and returns `None`; callers fall back to treating the name as same-file, which then correctly re-fails with "Cannot resolve type X" — no silent loss.
- Ambient globals (`lib.es5.d.ts`/`lib.dom.d.ts`): resolved once via `compute_ambient_global_files` (mod.rs:204-212), which only inspects `options.src_dirs.first()`. In a multi-root/monorepo config where the first `src_dir` can't resolve the `typescript` package but a later one could, ambient-global lookups silently return empty for the whole run — no diagnostic, since `resolve_ts_lib_paths` treats an empty result as "legitimate silent degradation" by design (mod.rs:236-238). Worth a second look if monorepo configs are a real use case; currently by design, not tested against multi-root.

## 5. Give-up consistency (the category you specifically flagged)
Enumerated every `ResolvedChain::default()` / early-return site:
- **chain.rs:40 (cycle detected)** — silent, no diagnostic, no `composes`. **This is the one that doesn't match the established `empty_with_compose` pattern** used everywhere else in the same function (chain.rs:31, 89, 126, 139, 177) and in alias.rs:252. Recommend converting to `empty_with_compose` or at minimum an Info diagnostic, mirroring the fix already applied for the unresolvable-type and opaque-type paths.
- alias.rs:116 (`LiteralUnion` used as a props base) — silent by design (malformed usage: a bare string union can't be a props type), no diagnostic. Minor; arguably deserves an Info-level note same as the "cannot be used as props base" diagnostic that alias.rs:234-253 already emits for other non-object-like types — LiteralUnion currently bypasses that shared path entirely.
- extends.rs:65 (`ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'div'>`-style non-HTML builtin without a resolvable element) returns `ResolvedChain::default()` but **does** attach an `InheritedLayer`, so it's not truly silent — acceptable.
- `func.rs` multi-param function type (`resolve_function_type`, lines 54-61) degrades to `PropType::Opaque{MultiParamFunction}` but **never pushes a diagnostic** — every other Opaque-producing path in the resolver (collected.rs's `push_opaque_diagnostic`, template.rs, primitives.rs indexed-access fallback) pairs the Opaque with a diagnostic; this one doesn't. Confirmed via the existing test (mod.rs:2015) which only asserts the `OpaqueReason`, never diagnostic presence. Real gap, easy fix (call `push_opaque_diagnostic`-equivalent before returning).

## 6. Panic/crash/hang risks
- No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!`/`unreachable!` in non-test resolver code — verified by grep across all 13 files.
- All array indexing (`params[0]`, `args[0]`/`args[1]` in substitute.rs, func.rs) is guarded by prior `.len()` checks.
- `depth: u8` with `MAX_DEPTH = 20` — no overflow risk (well under u8::MAX), consistently threaded through every recursive entry point.
- **Real hang/resource-exhaustion risk**: `try_expand_template_literal` (template.rs:94-104) computes an unbounded Cartesian product across template-literal parts with no size cap. A template literal type with N parts each resolving to an M-member literal union produces M^N strings (e.g. 6 parts × 20-member unions = 64M strings) — a plausible hang/OOM on an adversarial or even just a large real-world type (large design-system token unions are common). No test exercises multi-part template literals with non-trivial union sizes at all (`grep` found zero tests). This is the most concrete crash/hang-class finding in the whole subsystem — recommend a result-count cap (bail to Opaque past some threshold, same graceful-degradation pattern used everywhere else).

Word count: ~1050 (well under the 2800 cap — happy to expand any section on request).

Audit of crates/cli/src + crates/binding complete (read-only, no changes). Findings grouped by category.

## 1. Config loading (config.rs)
- Missing docgen.config.ts: falls back to defaults correctly (`load_config_file` returns `Ok(None)`, `build_options` does `.unwrap_or_default()`). Covered by tests.
- Malformed/syntax-error config: hard error with real stderr surfaced (line 151-160). Tested (`try_load_config_surfaces_the_real_syntax_error...`).
- Missing node/tsx on PATH: `command.spawn()` failure wrapped with a clear "is node installed?" hint (line 138-141). Not covered by a test (would require PATH manipulation), low severity — message is good.
- `srcDirs: []` (explicit empty array) in config: `into_pipeline_options` sets `opts.src_dirs = vec![]` (config.rs:35-37). Downstream in `crates/core/src/pipeline/mod.rs:220`, the "all src dirs missing" diagnostic is gated by `!options.src_dirs.is_empty() && ...`, so an empty list short-circuits past that check entirely — silent zero-file, zero-diagnostic extraction. This is a genuine "never fail silently" (non-negotiable #6) violation for an explicit-but-vacuous config value. **Medium severity, untested.**
- Shell injection: verified safe — path passed only via `env("__DOCGEN_CONFIG_PATH", path)` (config.rs:126), never interpolated into the `script` string that's piped via stdin. No code path found that builds a shell string from the path. Good.
- Timeout/hang: `child.wait_with_output()` (config.rs:149) has no timeout — a config file that spawns something that never resolves (e.g. an unresolved async top-level await) will hang the CLI indefinitely with no way out except Ctrl-C. **Medium severity, untested, no mitigation present.**
- Unexpected field types (e.g. `srcDirs` as a string instead of array): caught by serde's type mismatch inside `deny_unknown_fields` struct, produces a clear error via the `serde_json::from_slice` error path (config.rs:162-172). Good.
- Path with spaces/special chars: safe by construction (env var, not shell string).

## 2. CLI argument parsing (main.rs)
- `--format` + `--json`: doc comment claims `--json` "ignores --out/--format" (main.rs:103-107) — verified enforced in extract.rs:45-64 (the `if args.json {} else { match args.format ... }` branch never reads `args.format` in the json arm). Correct, tested only implicitly (not via a dedicated flag-precedence test).
- `--out` pointing to a directory / unwritable path: `std::fs::write` surfaces the raw io::Error via `.wrap_err(format!("Writing to {path}"))` (extract.rs:61) — good error, but see Output-writing section below for partial-write risk.
- Empty `--src` (`Vec::new()`, the clap default when omitted): correctly falls through to config/default `./src` (config.rs:200-202 only overrides when non-empty). Good, tested indirectly.
- `--react-version` bad value: rejected with a clear "expected react18/react19" error (config.rs:206-213). Good, no silent fallback (this was explicitly the subject of a regression test in the config-file path but NOT for the CLI-flag path — `build_options`'s own react-version branch has no dedicated unit test, only the config-schema one does).
- `--extra-builtins` malformed entries: any string is accepted verbatim (just `Into::into` to CompactString) — there's no validation of e.g. empty strings or duplicate names either as a CLI flag or via config. Not a crash risk, just permissive; low severity.
- `--cache-dir` pointing somewhere unwritable: not validated at the CLI layer at all; deferred entirely to `crates/core`'s cache.rs, out of this audit's scope — flagging for cross-check with whoever audited core/cache.rs.

## 3. Exit codes
Inconsistent across commands — only `extract` and `check` actually surface the error-diagnostic exit code:
- `extract` (main.rs:181): returns `cmd_extract`'s code (0 or 2). Correct, tested for both --json and non-json (extract.rs:180-196).
- `check` (main.rs:186): returns `cmd_check`'s code (0/1/2). Correct, tested for --json (check.rs:53-58).
- `watch` (main.rs:182-185): **always exits 0** — the initial extraction's diagnostics (including Error-severity ones) are printed but never affect the exit code, and `cmd_watch` returns `Result<()>` not `Result<i32>`. This may be intentional for a long-running dev-loop command, but it means `oxc-react-docgen watch` in a CI/pre-commit hook context (piped once, non-interactive) would report success even with hard extraction errors. **Worth confirming intent — flag as a gap if watch is ever used non-interactively.**
- `inspect` (main.rs:187-190): **always exits 0**, even if the named component isn't found — wait, actually `cmd_inspect` returns `Err` via `miette::miette!` when the component is missing (inspect.rs:20-26), which does propagate as a genuine process failure through `?` in main. So inspect only fails on missing-component, never on Error-severity diagnostics elsewhere in the tree (those are silently absent from cmd_inspect's output entirely — it doesn't call `print_diagnostics` at all). Lower severity since inspect is explicitly a "debugging tool."
- `schema` (main.rs:191-194) and `lsp` (main.rs:195-198): always 0 or process-terminate via `process::exit` (lsp only via its own `exit` method, or watch's 'q' key) — not diagnostic-dependent, not applicable.
- `completions` (main.rs:199-202): always 0, not applicable.

**Overall: exit-code contract (0/1/2) is documented and enforced only for `extract`/`check`. `watch` and `inspect` silently diverge from that contract with no doc caveat.** No existing test in crates/cli/tests/ or inline modules covers watch/inspect exit-code behavior — only 4 tests total touch exit codes (2 in extract.rs, 1 in check.rs, plus binding's unrelated ones).

## 4. Output writing
- `--out` write failure: `std::fs::write` (extract.rs:61, watch.rs:110) is not atomic — it opens with truncate+create, writes, and on a mid-write failure (disk full, permission revoked mid-run) can leave a **truncated, corrupt partial file** at the target path rather than either the old content or nothing. No temp-file+rename pattern used anywhere in this crate. **Medium severity — affects both `extract --out` and `watch --out`, untested.**
- `watch --out`: writes happen once per file-change event (watch.rs:107-112), each one a fresh full-truncate write of the whole snapshot; concurrent writes aren't a risk since it's single-threaded through the watchexec callback, but the same non-atomicity applies on every re-write, and errors are silently swallowed (`if let Ok(json) = ... { let _ = std::fs::write(...) }` — the `Result` of `fs::write` itself is discarded (`let _ =`), so **a write failure during watch mode is completely silent**, no error printed, no diagnostic. This directly contradicts CLAUDE.md non-negotiable #6 ("never fail silently") even though that rule is phrased around `Diagnostic` degradation rather than I/O — the practical effect for a user is the same: silent, invisible failure. **Medium-high severity, untested.**

## 5. watch.rs
- Startup with existing errors: printed via `print_summary`/`print_diagnostics` (watch.rs:48-51) but as noted in §3, has zero effect on exit code — watch just keeps running. Reasonable for a dev tool.
- Ctrl-C mid-extraction: the raw-mode key-reader thread (watch.rs:58-76) calls `std::process::exit(0)` directly on 'q'/'c' key press — note this is keyboard 'q'/'c' input via crossterm raw mode, not the SIGINT signal; actual Ctrl-C (SIGINT) is not intercepted at all, so its behavior is whatever the OS default does mid-write (terminal raw mode may be left enabled if the process is killed by signal rather than the 'q' key path, since `disable_raw_mode()` only runs on the 'q'/'c' branch or after the key-loop's `while` exits — a raw SIGINT kill would leave the terminal in raw mode for the user's shell). **Medium severity — terminal corruption UX bug on real Ctrl-C, untested (would need a signal-handling integration test).**
- Progress/terminal interleaving: the spinner is only used for the *initial* extraction (watch.rs:32-47); per-file updates during the watch loop print plain `println!` lines (watch.rs:103-105) with no spinner conflict — looks fine.

## 6. lsp.rs
This is explicitly a scaffold (doc comment: "LSP scaffold"), and it shows:
- **No real extraction ever happens.** `cmd_lsp` never calls `oxc_react_docgen_core::pipeline::extract` or touches `src_dirs`/config at all — it only implements `initialize`/`shutdown`/`exit`. So "requests for files outside src_dirs," "hover on positions with no component," and "race between ready and first request" are all **not yet applicable** — there's no hover implementation despite `hoverProvider: true` being advertised in the initialize response (lsp.rs:56), which is itself a bug: a client will send `textDocument/hover` requests based on that capability and get silently ignored (the `_ => {}` catch-all, lsp.rs:78, sends no response for any unhandled method, including hover). **A JSON-RPC request without a response will hang the client indefinitely waiting for a reply** — this is worse than an error response. **High severity relative to the advertised capability being false advertising, though acceptable if genuinely still WIP/unshipped.**
- Malformed LSP framing: partial header parsing is line-based and tolerant (skips unknown headers), but `content_length: None` after the header loop just `continue`s (lsp.rs:32-34) without consuming a body — if a client sends a headerless/malformed frame, this could desync the stream and hang forever misinterpreting subsequent bytes as headers. No test coverage (no `crates/cli/tests/` file touches lsp.rs at all).
- Malformed JSON body: silently ignored via `let Ok(msg) = ... else { continue }` (lsp.rs:41-43) — a notification, fine; but if it was actually a request (had an `id`), the client gets no response and hangs. Same pattern as above.

## 7. schema.rs — confirmed schema drift risk
The exported JSON Schema (schema.rs:5-69) is **hand-written and not derived from `ComponentEntry`/`ExtractionOutput`'s actual serde output** (no `schemars` derive, no round-trip test against real serde). Concrete drift already present today:
- `ComponentEntry` (core/src/types/output.rs:47-68) serializes `methods` and `tags` fields (camelCase: `methods`, `tags`) — **neither appears in the hand-written schema's `components.additionalProperties.properties`** (schema.rs:17-41). Since the schema has no `additionalProperties: false`, real output validates fine, but the schema is silently incomplete/stale documentation.
- `ExtractionStats` (core/src/types/output.rs:609-619) has 9 fields (`components_extracted`, `components_skipped`, `files_parsed`, `dts_files_parsed`, `dts_cache_hits`, `duration_ms`, `tier1_count`, `tier3_count`, `opaque_count`) — the schema's `stats.properties` (schema.rs:58-67) only documents 4 of them (`componentsExtracted`, `filesParsed`, `dtsCacheHits`, `durationMs`); `componentsSkipped`, `dtsFilesParsed`, `tier1Count`, `tier3Count`, `opaqueCount` are entirely undocumented.
- `Diagnostic` (core/src/types/diagnostic.rs:8-16) has `line`, `column`, `help` fields — none appear in the schema's diagnostics item properties (schema.rs:45-56), only `severity`/`message`/`file`/`code`.
- The only test (schema.rs:80-82, `test_cmd_schema_valid_json`) just asserts the function returns `Ok` — it never validates against a real `ExtractionOutput` instance or diffs field sets against the struct definitions. **This will silently drift further on every future field addition to core's output types. Medium-high severity — recommend either generating the schema via `schemars` derive on the real types, or adding a test that serializes a real `ExtractionOutput` and validates it exhaustively against the hand-written schema (catches missing-from-schema fields, not just malformed schema JSON).**

## 8. NAPI binding (crates/binding/src/lib.rs)
- `extract_all`, `extract_file_incremental`, `initialize_session` all wrap the actual pipeline call in `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` (lines 121-127, 159-166, 182-189) — a panic inside the closure becomes a `JoinError` via `.await`, which is mapped to `napi::Error::from_reason` rather than unwinding across the FFI boundary directly. - Thread-safety of shared state: `SESSIONS` is a `DashMap<u32, Arc<WatchSession>>` behind a `LazyLock` (lines 14-15) — appropriately concurrent-safe. `next_session_id` (lines 17-22) combines PID + an atomic counter into a `u32`; the counter is only 16 bits before masking (`counter & 0xFFFF`), so **after 65,536 sessions in one process it silently wraps and can collide with an existing still-open session ID** (a long-lived Vite dev server creating/closing many sessions over a dev session could theoretically hit this, though 65k sessions in one process is an unlikely real-world count). === 1. File discovery ===

- Permission-denied entries silently dropped, no diagnostic — discover.rs:17, `for entry in walker.flatten()`. ignore::Walk yields Result<DirEntry, Error>; `.flatten()` discards every Err (permission denied, broken symlink target, I/O error mid-walk) with zero trace. Violates CLAUDE.md #6 ("never fail silently"). No test covers a permission-denied subtree.
- Non-UTF8 filenames silently dropped — discover.rs:24 (`path.to_str().unwrap_or("")`) and :41 (`if let Ok(utf8) = Utf8PathBuf::from_path_buf(...)`). A file with invalid-UTF8 bytes in its name is discovered, produces path_str=="", passes all exclude checks trivially, then silently vanishes at the Utf8PathBuf conversion. No diagnostic, no test.
- Empty src_dirs is a silent no-op — mod.rs:220: `if !options.src_dirs.is_empty() && missing_src_dirs.len() == options.src_dirs.len()`. An empty Vec short-circuits the whole missing-dir diagnostic block, producing zero files and zero diagnostics — indistinguishable from "correctly configured but empty." (watch.rs tests' `empty_options()` relies on exactly this, so it's an exercised path, not hypothetical.)
- Symlink loops: non-issue — WalkBuilder (discover.rs:15) never sets `.follow_links(true)`, so ignore's default (don't follow) applies.
- TOCTOU discover→read: non-issue — mod.rs:269 handles a since-deleted file gracefully via Diagnostic::io_read_error.
- `.gitignore` respected conditionally (discover.rs:15, `git_ignore(!dir_is_in_node_modules)`): files gitignored in the user's own src dir vanish silently — likely intentional but worth confirming is documented behavior.

Verified structurally; test_same_display_name_across_files_with_identical_stem_does_not_collide (mod.rs:790) exercises the dedup path.
- Panic in one file kills the whole batch — mod.rs:260 (`src_files.par_iter().map(...).collect()`) has no per-file catch_unwind. If extractor::parse_file ever panics on one file (out of this audit's scope but the blast radius lives here), rayon propagates the panic through .collect() and the entire extract() call aborts — not graceful per-file degrade. Same applies to Phase 4 resolve par_iter (mod.rs:357). Recommend confirming with whoever audits extractor/resolver that no panic paths exist there; if any do, this pipeline has zero safety net.

If a caller passes nested src_dirs (e.g. ["./src", "./src/components"]), discover_files (per-dir, no cross-dir dedup) returns the same canonicalized file path twice in src_files. Phase 2 parses it twice; global.merge() (types/global.rs:75-97) runs twice for the same file_path — import_map/re_export_map overwrite harmlessly, but component_mappings.extend(...) literally duplicates every ComponentMapping for that file, and interface entries (keyed "{file}:{name}") hit the Occupied branch and extend props a second time. === 4. Cache subsystem (cache.rs) ===

- `resolver/named.rs:64-72` explicitly checks source-defined interfaces/type-aliases (steps 2-4) BEFORE falling to `resolve_known` (step 5) — comment at named.rs:41-43 states this exactly: "Check source-defined types BEFORE known library patterns so that user-defined types like ThemingProps or StylesApiProps are never silently replaced by opaque known-pattern shortcuts." Correct and intentional.
- `resolver/chain.rs:90-106`, used for `extends`-clause resolution — reached from BOTH `ExtendsRef::SameFile` and `ExtendsRef::Imported` via `resolve_extends_ref` (resolver/extends.rs:71,87), not just `Builtin` refs — runs the SAME `resolve_known` check at "Step 2" BEFORE any interface/type-alias lookup later in the function. A project with its own local `interface SxProps {...}` or `interface SlotProps {...}` extended by another interface gets silently short-circuited to the hardcoded MUI/React-Aria opaque shape instead of the user's real type — exactly the collision named.rs was written to prevent, but only protected in prop-type position, not extends position.

Not documented as a known tradeoff anywhere; reads as an oversight since the sibling code path proves the team already cares about this exact collision class. No test covers either call site's differing precedence (known.rs tests call `resolve_known` directly, bypassing both). Recommend: align chain.rs's precedence with named.rs, or explicitly document the gap.

## 6. react_types.rs

- No `use()`/RSC-specific APIs in `is_react_builtin` — expected, since those aren't prop-type-shaped. `ForwardedRef` present (react_types.rs:125). React 19's ref-as-prop is handled structurally via `ReactVersion.ref_as_prop`, not a builtin-name entry.
- Element matching (`html_element_for`/`html_element_from_type_arg`) is exact-string `match`, case-sensitive by construction — fine since inputs are always parsed `@types/react` PascalCase names; nonstandard casing falls through to `None`/opaque (safe default), not an error.
- `notable_html_attrs` default arm (react_types.rs:209) reused for all unrecognized elements — fine, curation-only, not correctness-critical.

## 7. Output types — inconsistent-state risk

**`ParsedProp.required == true` with `default_value: Some(_)` is representable and unvalidated.** `ParsedProp` (output.rs:79-99) has independent `required: bool` / `default_value: Option<DefaultValue>` fields; no constructor or validation enforces `required ⇒ default_value.is_none()` anywhere in scope (struct is freely constructible — see plugin.rs:82-93 test literal). RDT's own convention treats required+default as contradictory. Whether the resolver can actually produce this combo is outside this scope's files (would need to check resolver/mod.rs prop-merge logic) — flagging as a type-level gap regardless. Recommend a resolver-side invariant check or a doc comment on the field.

## 8. Panic/crash risk

Grepped `unwrap()`/`expect()`/`panic!`/indexing across all in-scope files — **every hit is confined to `#[cfg(test)]` modules**: types/collected.rs:746,748; extract.rs:186,194,209,218,220,223,229,230; known.rs:354,394,396,397,567. Production paths use `unwrap_or_default()`/`unwrap_or()`/pattern fallbacks throughout (e.g. `serde_json::to_string_pretty(...).unwrap_or_default()` at extract.rs:129,159 — safe since BTreeMap/HashMap keys are always valid `String`, this can't actually fail). No panic risk found in scope, consistent with CLAUDE.md non-negotiable #1.

---
**Top 3 by severity/actionability**: (a) known.rs precedence inconsistency between named.rs and chain.rs — real, demonstrable, silent data-quality bug; (b) plugin panic has no containment — full-batch failure with zero diagnostic; (c) TOON Union/Intersection truncation with no signal, inconsistent with the LiteralUnion path in the same file.

## Extractor Subsystem Audit: crates/core/src/extractor/ + types/collected.rs

Scope note: all `#[test]` coverage for this subsystem lives in `crates/core/src/extractor/mod.rs` (inline module, lines 769-1517); `component.rs`, `alias.rs`, `interface.rs`, `jsdoc.rs`, `defaults.rs`, `visit.rs` have zero inline tests of their own — everything is exercised indirectly via `parse_file()` from `mod.rs`'s test module or the 7 snapshot fixtures (`crates/core/tests/snapshots.rs`).

### 1. Component detection edge cases

Covered by existing tests: FC annotation (`test_fc_pattern`), forwardRef (`test_display_name_update`), memo(forwardRef) (`test_memo_forward_ref_detected`), HOC-wrapped (`test_hoc_pattern`), bare function decl (Pattern 4), forwardRef+as-cast (`test_forward_ref_component_annotation_with_as_cast`, `test_forward_ref_explicit_generics_survives_as_cast`), bare-identifier alias/rename (`test_bare_identifier_passthrough_alias_renames_component`, `test_identifier_wrapped_component_renamed_to_export_binding`), two aliases to one base (`test_two_aliases_to_the_same_base_component_both_survive`), `.d.ts` ForwardRefExoticComponent (component.rs:230, exercised via `test_radix_button_dts` but that test only checks interface collection, not component_mappings).

Gaps (silent misses, no diagnostic):
- **Anonymous default export** (`export default function(props: Props) {}`) — `visit_function` (visit.rs:262-293) requires `func.id` to be `Some` (line 265). Anonymous default-exported function components are silently skipped. No test covers this; likely a real-world miss (common in Next.js-style page files). Severity: silent data loss.
- **Class components** — no handling anywhere in `visit.rs`/`component.rs` for `Declaration::ClassDeclaration` as a component (only `declaration_name`, mod.rs:755, picks up the name for exports). `class Button extends React.Component<Props>` never produces a `ComponentMapping`. Undocumented gap.
- **`Object.assign(Component, { Sub: ... })` compound-component pattern** — not handled; `static_member_assignment` (interface.rs:193-201) only matches `X.Y = ...`, not `Object.assign` calls.
- **Generic components** (`function Comp<T>(props: Props<T>)`) — `func.type_parameters` is never recorded (unlike interfaces/type aliases, which do save them at visit.rs:145-150, 167-172), so a bare `T` referenced inside `Props<T>`'s body isn't recognized as a component-level generic placeholder. Asymmetry, not crash risk.
- **class expression as component** (`const Button = class extends React.Component<Props> {}`) — not handled by any `try_*` in component.rs; silently falls through all detectors.
- `export { X as Y }` renaming — `LexedExport` records local/exported name distinction correctly (visit.rs:61-96) but is a separate table from `component_mappings`; reconciliation is resolver territory (out of scope), flagged as a seam.

### 2. Prop-type declaration parsing edge cases

Covered: Omit/Pick/Partial/Required/Readonly (alias.rs), unions incl. literal unions, intersections, inline object literal type-alias bodies, bare function-type aliases, bare array/tuple aliases (mod.rs:805-902, explicitly regression-tested against a documented prior silent-vanishing bug), namespaced types via `namespace_stack`/`ts_type_name_str` (`test_namespace_member_stored_under_qualified_name`), `readonly T[]` type operator (`test_readonly_array_type_operator_peeled_transparently`).

Gaps:
- **`satisfies` expressions** — no `TSSatisfiesExpression` handling anywhere in `ts_type_to_collected` or expression paths. `as_const_literal` (interface.rs:15-24) only unwraps `TSAsExpression`/`TSTypeAssertion`; `try_collect_cva_call`'s `decl.init.as_ref()` match (interface.rs:90-93) also wouldn't see through a `satisfies`-wrapped const. A `satisfies`-wrapped cva/tv config or as-const object would be silently dropped, no diagnostic, no test.
- Mapped/conditional types are captured structurally and correctly tagged via `needs_type_checker()` (collected.rs:118-120) — this is the intended degrade path, not a bug, but untested at the extractor level.
- Template literal types (mod.rs:402-414) handled but untested directly.
- Recursive/self-referential types (e.g. `interface Node { children: Node[] }`) are safe at extraction time — extraction just stores a `Named` reference, no recursion — real recursion risk (if any) lives in the resolver, out of scope.
- Ambient/`declare` types — no special-casing needed/found; `declare` modifiers don't block extraction since OXC parses them as normal declarations.

### 3. JSDoc parsing edge cases

Covered: proximity-based JSDoc→interface-description-not-first-prop (`test_interface_description_not_stolen_by_first_prop`), `@deprecated` non-bleed to untagged siblings (`test_deprecated_tag_does_not_bleed_to_sibling_props_without_jsdoc`).

Gaps:
- `PROXIMITY_THRESHOLD = 120` bytes (jsdoc.rs:33) is an untested heuristic boundary — a prop preceded by a long decorator chain or several blank lines beyond 120 bytes silently gets no JSDoc, no diagnostic.
- **Non-JSDoc block comments leak as descriptions**: `find_jsdoc_with_tags` only checks `c.is_block` (jsdoc.rs:44), not that the comment starts with `/**` specifically — plain `/* comment */` blocks also satisfy `is_block()`. `parse_jsdoc_text`'s `trim_start_matches("/**")` (jsdoc.rs:66) is a no-op on such input, so a stray non-JSDoc block comment within 120 bytes of a prop can leak into its description. No test verifies single-star blocks are excluded. Severity: cosmetic/silent data quality, no diagnostic.
- JSDoc placed above a re-export statement (`/** ... */\nexport { X } from './y'`) is never associated with anything — `visit_export_named_declaration` (visit.rs:61-96) never calls `find_jsdoc`. Silent, untested.

### 4. Default value extraction edge cases

Covered: destructured defaults (`extract_param_defaults`, defaults.rs), `defaultProps` static assignment merge incl. displayName-rename interaction (`test_default_props_assignment_merged_into_component_mapping`, `test_default_props_scan_survives_a_displayname_rename_to_a_different_string`), computed vs. literal defaults distinguished via `computed` flag (defaults.rs:47-78).

Gaps:
- Defaults referencing outer-scope constants (`{ size = DEFAULT_SIZE }`) fall into `_ => computed: true` (defaults.rs:68-77) and capture raw text only — presumably intentional, but no diagnostic notes the value is unresolved-at-extraction, and no test documents this as expected vs. gap.
- `extract_param_defaults` only inspects `params.items.first()` (defaults.rs:19) — a component whose props are the *second* parameter would silently get zero defaults. Low real-world risk given React convention, but unguarded and undiagnosed.
- Nested destructuring defaults (`{ style: { color = 'red' } = {} }`) — only top-level `BindingProperty` entries scanned (defaults.rs:27-40); nested patterns not recursed. Silent, untested, low impact.

### 5. Panic/crash risks

No bare `.unwrap()`/`.expect()`/`panic!()` outside `#[cfg(test)]` found in component.rs, alias.rs, interface.rs, jsdoc.rs, defaults.rs, or visit.rs — consistent with the project's non-negotiable. All fallible paths use `?`/`let-else`/`Option` combinators.

- **Slicing risk (currently sound, but fragile invariant)**: every raw-text fallback (`self.source[span.start as usize..span.end as usize]` — mod.rs:332,335,459,467,493,511; defaults.rs:63,73; jsdoc.rs:53) trusts OXC span byte-offsets to be in-bounds and on UTF-8 char boundaries for `self.source`. Sound today because `self.source` is exactly what OXC parsed (`parse_file`, mod.rs:104-124), but zero defensive checks exist; no inline test stresses multi-byte UTF-8 near a span boundary (emoji/CJK in JSDoc or string literals).
- **Real crash-risk gap — recursion depth in `ts_type_to_collected`** (mod.rs:311-471): recurses per nested `CollectedType` (Union/Intersection/Array/Tuple/Function/Conditional/Mapped) with no independent depth counter of its own; relies entirely on the pre-parse `max_bracket_nesting_depth` heuristic (mod.rs:40, guard at 105-120) to bound worst-case recursion. That heuristic counts *brackets*, not *type nesting* specifically — deeply chained conditional types (`A extends B ? C extends D ? ... : ... : ...`) can achieve deep type-nesting with proportionally fewer brackets per level than object-literal/paren nesting. The guard's own docstring (mod.rs:38-40) claims to cover "nested parenthesized types, object type literals, or conditional types," but the only test (`test_excessive_nesting_guard`) uses pure `(...)` paren nesting, which maps 1:1 to bracket count and doesn't validate the conditional-type case. This is an untested stack-overflow risk under adversarial/pathological conditional-type-heavy input.

### 6. Silent failure risks (no `Diagnostic` emitted on degrade)

The code's own comments repeatedly reference "previously silently vanished, now fixed" bugs (a good sign this category is actively watched), but the fixes changed `None`→`Some(Passthrough{...})` for specific shapes without adding diagnostic emission for the *remaining* uncovered shapes. Live gaps, none push to `data.diagnostics`:

- `classify_type_alias`'s Omit/Pick/Partial/Required/Readonly arms (alias.rs:18-70) all `return None` via `?` on missing/malformed type arguments (e.g. `Omit<Foo>` with no second arg) — the whole type alias silently vanishes from `data.type_aliases`.
- `extract_props_arg`/`extract_type_name_from_type`'s terminal `_ => None` (mod.rs:602-651) — any `TSType` variant not explicitly matched (e.g. an exotic generic expression inside `FC<...>`) silently fails to produce a `ComponentMapping`.
- Component detectors (`try_fc_annotation`, `try_forward_ref`, `try_hoc_wrapped`, `try_forward_ref_exotic_decl`) chained via `.or_else()` (visit.rs:238-247) produce no mapping and no diagnostic if all fail — no signal that "PascalCase binding X looked like a component but wasn't recognized."
- `ts_signature_to_object_field`/`collect_property_signature` (mod.rs:514-566, 674-729) return `None` for any non-`StaticIdentifier`/`StringLiteral` `PropertyKey` (computed/numeric/symbol keys) — such props vanish from the interface with no diagnostic.

Per the project's own non-negotiable ("always emit Diagnostic when degrading — never fail silently"), every item above violates that rule today. Diagnostics currently exist only for two whole-file failure modes (`ExcessiveNesting`, `ParseError`, mod.rs:104-143) — there is no per-declaration/per-prop diagnostic emission anywhere in the extractor for these narrower silent-drop cases. This looks like the subsystem's largest systemic gap.

---
File paths referenced: crates/core/src/extractor/mod.rs, component.rs, alias.rs, interface.rs, jsdoc.rs, defaults.rs, visit.rs; crates/core/src/types/collected.rs.

# Edge Cases & Failure Modes

A comprehensive audit of non-happy-path behavior across the pipeline: extractor, resolver, pipeline/cache/import_map, CLI/config/NAPI binding, and types/serialization/plugin. Produced by five parallel read-only audits against the codebase as of 2026-08-04, cross-checked against existing test coverage. Nothing here has been fixed yet — this is the map, not the patch.

**How to read this doc:** findings are grouped by severity tier first (for prioritization), then by subsystem (for context when doing the actual fix). "Tested?" means an existing test exercises exactly this behavior, not just the surrounding happy path.

---

## Severity tiers

- **Crash/hang** — can panic, OOM, or hang the process on realistic or adversarial input.
- **Silent data loss** — violates CLAUDE.md non-negotiable #6 ("always emit a Diagnostic when degrading — never fail silently"): output is missing or incomplete with no trace.
- **Silent correctness bug** — output is present but *wrong*, not just missing, with no trace.
- **Contract inconsistency** — behavior diverges from a documented or implied contract (exit codes, schema, precedence rules already established elsewhere in the same codebase).
- **Documented/by-design limitation** — already tracked in `rdt-coverage.md` or `type-checker-integration.md`; listed here only for completeness.

---

## Priority 0 — silent correctness bugs (wrong output, not just missing)

| # | Finding | Location | Tested? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P0-1 | `known.rs` shortcut precedence is inconsistent: `named.rs` checks source-defined interfaces/type-aliases *before* falling back to hardcoded library shortcuts (correct, and explicitly commented as intentional to avoid this exact collision) — but `chain.rs`'s `extends`-clause path (reached from both `ExtendsRef::SameFile` and `ExtendsRef::Imported`) checks the hardcoded shortcuts *first*. A project with its own `interface SxProps {...}` or `interface SlotProps {...}` extended via `extends` gets silently replaced by the hardcoded MUI/React-Aria opaque shape. | `resolver/chain.rs:90-106` vs `resolver/named.rs:41-72` | No |
| P0-2 | Cache staleness on same-mtime-tick, same-size edits: `key_for` keys on `(path, size, mtime_ns)`. On filesystems/environments with coarse mtime resolution (network FS, container overlay FS), an edit completing within the same tick and producing identical byte length is indistinguishable from the original — a stale `SourceData` is served. Scope is narrow (only `.d.ts` files go through this cache) but real. | `cache.rs:181-191` | Partial — existing test only covers a size-changing edit |
| P0-3 | `ParsedProp.required == true` with `default_value: Some(_)` is representable and unvalidated — a contradictory state (RDT's own convention treats these as mutually exclusive) that nothing in the type or its constructors prevents. | `types/output.rs:79-99` | No |
| P0-4 | TOON format truncates `Union`/`Intersection` prop types to 4 members with **no truncation indicator**, while the sibling `LiteralUnion` path in the same function correctly appends `"...(+N)"`. A 10-member union silently renders as if it had exactly 4 — misleading, not just incomplete. | `toon.rs:125-132` (vs. the correct pattern at `toon.rs:110-116`) | No |
| P0-5 | `schema.rs`'s exported JSON Schema is hand-written, not derived from the real structs, and has already drifted: `ComponentEntry.methods`/`.tags`, five of nine `ExtractionStats` fields, and `Diagnostic.line`/`.column`/`.help` are all undocumented in the schema despite being real serialized fields today. | `cli/commands/schema.rs:17-67` vs `core/types/output.rs:47-68,609-619`, `core/types/diagnostic.rs:8-16` | No — the one test only checks the schema itself is valid JSON, never diffs against real output |

## Priority 1 — crash/hang risks

| # | Finding | Location | Tested? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P1-1 | Unbounded Cartesian product when expanding template-literal types: N parts × M-member unions per part produces up to M^N strings with no cap. Large design-system token unions (a realistic, non-adversarial case) can hit this. | `resolver/template.rs:94-104` | No — zero tests exercise multi-part template literals with non-trivial union sizes |
| P1-2 | LSP `Content-Length` header is parsed and used directly in `vec![0u8; len]` with no upper bound. A malformed or buggy local LSP client sending a huge value triggers a giant allocation (likely an allocator abort, not a catchable panic). | `cli/commands/lsp.rs:36` | No |
| P1-3 | A plugin hook panic unwinds straight out of `pipeline::extract()` with zero `catch_unwind` anywhere in the repo — one bad plugin on one file kills output for every file, no diagnostic, no attribution. | `plugin.rs` (hooks called from `pipeline/mod.rs:293,385`) | No — existing plugin tests only cover the happy path |
| P1-4 | Parse/resolve phases (`src_files.par_iter().map(...).collect()` and the resolve equivalent) have no per-file `catch_unwind` — a panic in one file's extraction or resolution aborts the entire batch rather than degrading just that file. Blast radius currently bounded only by the extractor/resolver having no panic paths of their own (true today per audits) and plugins having none (false — see P1-3). | `pipeline/mod.rs:260,357` | No |
| P1-5 | `watch.rs`'s `initialized.lock().expect("init lock poisoned")` — if any prior panic occurred while holding this lock (e.g. via P1-3/P1-4 surfacing inside a watch session), the mutex poisons permanently and every subsequent operation on that session panics. No recovery path short of restarting the session. | `pipeline/watch.rs:93` | No — unpoisonable without deliberate fault injection |

## Priority 2 — silent data loss (missing output, no diagnostic)

Grouped by subsystem since these are numerous; each violates non-negotiable #6.

**Extractor:**
- Anonymous default-exported function components (`export default function(props: Props) {}`) are silently skipped — `visit_function` requires `func.id` to be `Some`. Likely a real-world miss (common in Next.js page files). `visit.rs:265`
- Class components (`class Button extends React.Component<Props>`) are never detected as components at all — no handler exists for this shape. Undocumented gap.
- `Object.assign(Component, { Sub: ... })` compound-component pattern isn't recognized; only `X.Y = ...` static-member assignment is. `interface.rs:193-201`
- Class-expression components (`const Button = class extends React.Component<Props> {}`) fall through every detector silently.
- `satisfies`-wrapped expressions (a cva/tv config, an as-const object) are never unwrapped — no `TSSatisfiesExpression` handling exists anywhere in the extractor. Silently dropped.
- `classify_type_alias`'s `Omit`/`Pick`/`Partial`/`Required`/`Readonly` arms all `return None` via `?` on malformed/missing type arguments — the *entire* type alias vanishes from `data.type_aliases`, not just the malformed part. `alias.rs:18-70`
- Any `TSType` variant not explicitly matched in `extract_props_arg`/`extract_type_name_from_type` (exotic generic expressions inside `FC<...>`) silently produces no `ComponentMapping`. `mod.rs:602-651`
- When every component detector (`try_fc_annotation`, `try_forward_ref`, `try_hoc_wrapped`, `try_forward_ref_exotic_decl`) fails, there's no signal that a PascalCase binding *looked* like a component but wasn't recognized. `visit.rs:238-247`
- Computed/numeric/symbol property keys vanish from an interface with no trace — only `StaticIdentifier`/`StringLiteral` keys are handled. `mod.rs:514-566,674-729`

**Resolver:**
- The cycle-detected return path is the one give-up site in `chain.rs` that doesn't follow the established `empty_with_compose` pattern used at every other give-up site in the same file (lines 31, 89, 126, 139, 177) and in `alias.rs:252` — a genuinely self-referential/mutually-recursive interface pair silently loses all props with zero trace. `chain.rs:38-41`
- Multi-parameter function types degrade to `PropType::Opaque{MultiParamFunction}` without ever pushing a diagnostic, unlike every other Opaque-producing path in the resolver. `func.rs:54-61`
- A `LiteralUnion` used directly as a props base is silently rejected — malformed usage, but bypasses the shared "cannot be used as props base" diagnostic path that handles this exact scenario for other non-object-like types. `alias.rs:116` vs `alias.rs:234-253`
- Generic aliases with more declared type parameters than the call site supplies (partial application, or unsupported default type params like `Foo<T, U = T>`) silently leave trailing parameters unsubstituted — `build_substitution`'s `.zip()` just stops. `substitute.rs:33-43`

**Pipeline/discovery:**
- Permission-denied files/directories are silently dropped during discovery — `ignore::Walk`'s `Err` results are discarded via `.flatten()`. `discover.rs:17`
- Non-UTF8 filenames are silently dropped during discovery (path resolves to an empty string, passes exclusion checks trivially, then vanishes at the `Utf8PathBuf` conversion). `discover.rs:24,41`
- An explicitly empty `src_dirs` (`[]`, whether via CLI or an explicit `srcDirs: []` in `docgen.config.ts`) short-circuits past the "all src dirs missing" diagnostic entirely — a zero-file, zero-diagnostic run indistinguishable from "correctly configured but genuinely empty." `pipeline/mod.rs:220`
- Two component mappings with identical display name *and* identical file path still collide — the dedup key is `"{name} ({file_path})"` for both; the second silently overwrites the first via `components.insert`. `pipeline/mod.rs:378-388`
- Overlapping `src_dirs` (e.g. `["./src", "./src/components"]`, a realistic monorepo misconfiguration) cause the same file to be discovered and parsed twice, duplicating every `ComponentMapping` for that file and flowing directly into the collision above. `pipeline/mod.rs` + `types/global.rs:75-97`

**CLI:**
- `watch --out` write failures are completely silent: the result of `std::fs::write` is discarded via `let _ = ...`. No error printed, no diagnostic, nothing. `cli/commands/watch.rs:107-112`
- `--out`/`watch --out` writes are non-atomic (`fs::write` truncates then writes) — a mid-write failure (disk full, permission revoked) can leave a truncated, corrupt file at the target path instead of either the old content or nothing.

**Types/serialization:**
- `NumberLiteral(f64)` values that are NaN or Infinity serialize to JSON `null` (serde_json's behavior for non-finite floats), and on deserialization `as_f64().unwrap_or(0.0)` silently turns that into `0.0`. Likely unreachable via normal TS literal syntax, but present. `types/output.rs:314,423`
- Zero-member `LiteralUnion`s are treated as a valid enum by `is_literal_union()`, producing `{"name":"enum","value":[]}` in RDT output with nothing explaining the empty select.

## Priority 3 — contract inconsistencies

| # | Finding | Location |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P3-1 | Exit-code contract (0 = success, 2 = extraction error) is documented and enforced only for `extract`/`check`. `watch` always exits 0 regardless of extraction errors — fine for an interactive dev loop, but a footgun if ever run non-interactively (CI, pre-commit). `inspect` never surfaces Error-severity diagnostics found elsewhere in the tree at all (only fails on a missing-component lookup). | `cli/main.rs:181-198` |
| P3-2 | `DiagnosticCode::Unknown` is defined but never constructed anywhere in the repo — dead code, though the enum is `#[non_exhaustive]` so may be intentional headroom for external consumers. | `types/diagnostic.rs:61` |

## Documented/by-design limitations (listed for completeness, not new findings)

- Ariakit's `Props<T, O> = O & Omit<ComponentPropsWithoutRef<T>, keyof O>` generic pattern is unmatched at the chain level — `composes` stays empty for 6 of the 10 outlier components tracked in `docs/benchmarks.md`. Matches the already-documented gap.
- Mapped types, conditional types, and a couple of `@emotion/styled`-specific call shapes need real type inference OXC deliberately doesn't do — tracked in `docs/type-checker-integration.md` and `rdt-coverage.md`'s known-gaps table.
- Multi-root/monorepo ambient-global (`lib.dom.d.ts` etc.) resolution only inspects `options.src_dirs.first()` — if the first `src_dir` can't resolve `typescript` but a later one could, ambient lookups silently return empty for the whole run. Currently treated as legitimate silent degradation by design; flagged here only because it's untested against an actual multi-root config.
- TOON's format is deliberately lossy relative to canonical JSON (truncated unions, no length cap on descriptions) but this isn't stated in the module's own doc comment — a documentation gap, not a behavior bug.

## Notable non-findings (checked, confirmed sound)

- No `unwrap()`/`expect()`/`panic!()` outside `#[cfg(test)]` anywhere in the extractor, resolver, CLI, or binding crates — non-negotiable #1 holds everywhere it was checked.
- Import re-export cycles are correctly bounded (`MAX_REEXPORT_DEPTH = 8` plus a visited set) with dedicated tests.
- Parallel parse/merge is deterministic: discovery sorts, rayon preserves input order through `collect()`, and the sequential merge phase iterates that same order — diagnostics ordering and dedup winner-selection are reproducible.
- Editor atomic-save patterns (temp file + rename) are explicitly handled in watch mode via `canonicalize_best_effort`.
- Shell injection in config loading is not possible — the config path is passed via `env()`, never interpolated into a shell string, verified across all code paths.

---

## Suggested next step

This is a lot of surface area — 5 crash/hang risks, 5 silent-correctness bugs, ~20 silent-data-loss sites, 2 contract inconsistencies. Worth deciding scope before touching code: fix the P0 correctness bugs first (they're the ones producing *wrong* answers, which is worse than a documented gap), then the P1 hang risks that are realistic rather than adversarial (template-literal blowup, plugin/per-file panic containment), then triage the P2 silent-drop list — some of those (anonymous default export, class components) may be worth an explicit "not supported" diagnostic even if full support isn't warranted yet.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
The single most valuable thing this audit surfaces isn't any one bug — it's the pattern: nearly every subsystem has its own version of the same failure shape, "give up and return an empty/default value with no trace." The resolver has `ResolvedChain::default()` instead of `empty_with_compose()`; the extractor has bare `None`/`return None` on malformed type args; discovery has `.flatten()` silently eating `Err`s; watch mode has `let _ = std::fs::write(...)`. That's a strong signal this isn't five unrelated problems needing five different fixes — it's one architectural discipline (non-negotiable #6: "always emit a Diagnostic when degrading") that was applied rigorously in some code paths and never retrofitted to others as the codebase grew. A single sweep-style fix (grep for `-> None`/`::default()`/`let _ =` at give-up points and ensure each pairs with a diagnostic) would likely close a large fraction of the P2 list at once, rather than needing 20 independent fixes.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Wrote the full findings to `docs/edge-cases.md` and linked it from `docs/STATUS.md`'s "Where to look next" section, matching the project's existing doc conventions (tables, no line wrapping, cross-referenced against `rdt-coverage.md`/`type-checker-integration.md` for gaps already tracked elsewhere).

**Headline numbers:** 9 crash/hang risks, 5 silent-correctness bugs (wrong output, not just missing), ~20 silent-data-loss sites across extractor/resolver/pipeline/CLI/types, 2 contract inconsistencies. The two I'd flag as most worth your attention first:

1. **`known.rs` shortcut precedence bug** (P0-1) — a real, demonstrable data-quality bug, not a hypothetical: `named.rs` correctly checks user-defined interfaces before falling back to hardcoded library shortcuts (SxProps, etc.), but `chain.rs`'s `extends`-clause path checks the shortcuts *first*. A project with its own `SxProps` interface extended via `extends` gets silently swapped for MUI's opaque shape.
2. **Template-literal Cartesian-product blowup** (P1-1) — no cap on the M^N string expansion when a template literal has multiple parts each resolving to a sizable union. Realistic (design-system token unions are common), not just adversarial, and zero test coverage exists for it.

I didn't fix anything — this was scoped as understand-and-document. Want me to start working through the P0 list (the wrong-not-missing bugs), or would you rather triage/re-prioritize first given the size of the P2 list?
